items.stem: In a rigid stainless-steel vacuum-calibration tank of volume 0.016 m³, 0.35 mol of Helium-4 (He) (molar mass 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹) is held in thermal equilibrium at 420 K. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what pressure does the gas exert on the walls?
items.workedSolution: From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (0.35 × 8.31 × 420) / 0.016 = 7.63 × 10⁴ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 7.63 × 10⁴ Pa (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies nRT by volume V instead of dividing nRT by V.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts 273.15 from an already-kelvin temperature before applying pV = nRT.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the amount of substance n in p = nRT / V, solving for 1 mol instead of the given molar amount.

items.stem: Inside a high-vacuum synchrotron beamline gas target, an ideal monatomic sample of Argon-40 (Ar) (M = 0.04 kg mol⁻¹) is in thermal equilibrium at 180 K. Given k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and 1 eV = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, Find the average translational kinetic energy of a single atom in eV.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 180 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 0.0233 eV (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates (1/2) k_B T / e for a single degree of freedom instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes k_B T / e and omits the 3/2 translational factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the 3/2 factor to 3 k_B T / e by omitting the 1/2 in kinetic energy.

items.stem: In a frictionless piston-cylinder assembly on a thermodynamics test bench, 1.2 mol of an ideal gas starts at state A with pressure 2.2 × 10⁵ Pa and volume 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³. As shown on the pressure–temperature (P–T) diagram, the gas expands isobarically from A to state B of volume 3.6 × 10⁻³ m³, before undergoing isochoric heating from B to state C at 3.52 × 10⁵ Pa. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the temperature T_B at state B?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates PV / (nR) at the target state to obtain 79.4 K (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Charles's law ratio, multiplying T_A by V_A / V_B instead of V_B / V_A.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Stops after computing the initial temperature T_A = P_A V_A / (nR) without scaling by V_B / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the final temperature T_C at state C rather than the intermediate temperature T_B.

items.stem: In a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity, 0.4 mol of a monatomic ideal gas executes a clockwise closed cycle A → B → C → D → A between pressures 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa and 2.4 × 10⁵ Pa and volumes 1.8 × 10⁻³ m³ and 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³ (A → B isobaric expansion at 2.4 × 10⁵ Pa, B → C isochoric cooling, C → D isobaric compression at 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa, D → A isochoric heating). Taking net work done by the gas as positive, what is the net mechanical work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Net work done by the gas equals the enclosed rectangular area: W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = (2.4 × 10⁵ − 1.2 × 10⁵)(4.5 × 10⁻³ − 1.8 × 10⁻³) = 324 J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes netWorkJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 324 J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies the enclosed loop area by an extraneous 3/2 internal-energy factor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the expansion work along A → B and forgets to subtract the compression work along C → D.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes P_B V_B − P_D V_D instead of the enclosed rectangular loop area (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min).

items.stem: Inside a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals, 1.2 mol of an ideal monatomic gas (adiabatic index γ = 5/3) initially at P_A = 7.5 × 10⁵ Pa and V_A = 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ is reversibly and adiabatically expanded to V_B = 3.6 × 10⁻³ m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the final pressure P_B in state B?
items.workedSolution: For a monatomic adiabatic process, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 7.5 × 10⁵ × (1.2 × 10⁻³ / 3.6 × 10⁻³)^(5/3) = 1.20 × 10⁵ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P V^(5/3) = const to obtain 1.20 × 10⁵ Pa (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses the diatomic adiabatic index γ = 7/5 instead of γ = 5/3 for a monatomic gas.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats the process as isothermal (P_A V_A = P_B V_B) rather than adiabatic (P_A V_A^(5/3) = P_B V_B^(5/3)).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the adiabatic exponent, using 3/5 instead of γ = 5/3.

items.stem: In a variable-volume optical pressure cell, 1.4 mol of monatomic ideal gas executes a reversible Carnot heat-engine cycle between a hot reservoir at 416 K and a cold sink at 260 K, expanding isothermally at the hot reservoir from V_A = 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the theoretical thermal efficiency η of this Carnot cycle?
items.workedSolution: Carnot efficiency η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 1 − 260 / 416 = 0.375.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 0.375 (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Applies an extra factor of one-half from misremembering the degrees-of-freedom or geometric prefactor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the isothermal volume ratio 1 − V_A / V_B instead of the reservoir temperature ratio 1 − T_C / T_H.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates T_C / T_H without subtracting from 1.

items.stem: On the P–V plot for a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder, 0.4 mol of monatomic working gas (γ = 5/3) expands adiabatically from (4.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³) at A to 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ at B, returns to 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ isobarically at C, and regains 4.5 × 10⁵ Pa isochorically. Defining work by the gas as positive, calculate W_net.
items.workedSolution: At B, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 9.772 × 10⁴ Pa. Adiabatic work W_AB = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 370.3 J, and isobaric compression work W_BC = P_B(V_C − V_B) = -175.9 J (W_CA = 0). Thus W_net = W_AB + W_BC = 194 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 194 J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the magnitude of the isobaric compression work P_B(V_B − V_C).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the adiabatic expansion work W_AB and forgets to subtract the isobaric compression work |W_BC|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_CA along the isochoric leg instead of net work W_net.

items.stem: The temperature–time curve shows 0.3 kg of ethanol inside a thermal-energy-storage phase-change capsule (heated between 121 K and 219 K; T_m = 159 K, c_solid = 1120 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, L_f = 1.08 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹) while an electrical immersion heater of input power 450 W and thermal transfer efficiency 0.9 supplies energy. Calculate the total duration of the process.
items.workedSolution: Effective thermal power P_eff = η P = 0.9 × 450 = 405.0 W. Total energy Q_tot = m c_solid ΔT_s + m L_f + m c_liquid ΔT_l = 8.909 × 10⁴ J, giving t_total = Q_tot / P_eff = 220 s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_eff = η P and divides required thermal energy to obtain 220 s (D).

options.distractorRationale: Omits the latent-heat plateau duration m L_f / (η P) and includes only sensible temperature-change intervals.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies time by efficiency η instead of dividing energy by effective power η P.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides thermal energy by the nominal electrical rating P rather than the effective thermal power η P.

items.stem: A heated copper block of mass 0.36 kg and specific heat capacity 385 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 510 K is plunged into 0.72 kg of water (c = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 290 K inside a well-insulated copper-lined laboratory calorimeter. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. What is the final thermal equilibrium temperature T_eq?
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l), giving T_eq = 299.7 K. Therefore T_eq = 300 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 300 K (A).

options.distractorRationale: Weights initial temperatures by mass alone and ignores the much larger specific heat capacity of the liquid.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Takes the unweighted arithmetic mean of the two initial temperatures, ignoring both masses and specific heat capacities.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Swaps the specific heat capacities of the solid specimen and the liquid bath.

items.stem: Operating at 3600 K with effective blackbody emissivity 1 and area 3.6 × 10¹⁸ m², a spherical main-sequence stellar photosphere irradiates a sensor located 2.4 × 10¹¹ m away in vacuum. Taking Wien's constant b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K, what is the peak emission wavelength λ_max in nanometres?
items.workedSolution: By Wien's displacement law, λ_max = b / T = (2.90 × 10⁻³) / 3600 = 8.056 × 10⁻⁷ m = 806 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the blackbody radiation law in SI units to obtain 806 nm (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Wien's displacement law by dividing T by b instead of b by T.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts 273.15 from the kelvin temperature before applying Wien's law.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies Wien's constant b by T instead of dividing b by T.

items.stem: In a climate radiative-transfer model, a horizontal basaltic planetary regolith tile of area 8.5 m² and surface emissivity e = 0.84 is at 320 K while exchanging thermal infrared radiation with an effective surrounding environment at 278 K. Taking σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, what is the net rate of radiative energy loss P_net from the surface?
items.workedSolution: Net radiative power loss P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) = 0.84 × 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × 8.5 × ((320)⁴ − (278)⁴) = 1.83 × 10³ W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) to obtain 1.83 × 10³ W (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates e σ A (T − T_amb)⁴ instead of e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴), a classic fourth-power algebra error.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the greybody emissivity factor e (< 1) from P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates gross emitted power e σ A T⁴ and ignores incoming radiation absorbed from the surroundings at T_amb.

items.stem: In a semiconductor lithography purge canister (volume 0.04 m³), 0.8 mol of monatomic Argon-40 (Ar) of molar mass 0.04 kg mol⁻¹ is warmed from T₁ = 250 K to T₂ = 375 K, shifting the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed curve as plotted. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), determine v_rms at the higher temperature T₂.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.04 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 375 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 375 / 0.04) = 483 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 483 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: 0.75 mol of ideal gas inside a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell follows path A → B → C on the volume–temperature (V–T) plot: an isobaric expansion from (1.1 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³) to V_B = 0.01 m³, then an isochoric pressure increase to P_C = 2.2 × 10⁵ Pa. Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine T_C.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates PV / (nR) at the target state to obtain 353 K (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reports the final temperature converted to °C when the question and options specify kelvin.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses the initial volume V_A instead of V_B = V_C when evaluating T_C = P_C V_C / (nR).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes T_B after the isobaric stage and omits the isochoric pressure ratio P_C / P_A.

items.stem: The P–V graph shows an isobaric compression of 1.5 mol of ideal monatomic gas inside a precision pneumatic actuator chamber sealed with a movable piston at 2.7 × 10⁵ Pa from V_A = 9.9 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³. Using the sign convention where work done on the gas is positive, determine the compression work done on the gas.
items.workedSolution: During isobaric compression from 9.9 × 10⁻³ m³ to 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at 2.7 × 10⁵ Pa, work done on the gas W_on = −P(V_B − V_A) = 2.7 × 10⁵ × (9.9 × 10⁻³ − 4.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.46 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 1.46 × 10³ J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the magnitude of internal energy change |ΔU| = (3/2) P |ΔV| instead of boundary work P |ΔV|.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies pressure by initial volume V_A instead of the volume change |V_B − V_A|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the total heat rejected |Q| = (5/2) P |ΔV| rather than the mechanical work done on the gas.

items.stem: The P–V diagram shows a rapid thermally insulated (adiabatic) expansion A → B of 0.75 mol of monatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) in an insulated aerospace gas-accumulator cylinder from (6.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³) to final volume 3.6 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). Taking work done by the gas as positive, how much mechanical work is done by the gas during A → B?
items.workedSolution: First find P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 9.615 × 10⁴ Pa. Since Q = 0 in an adiabatic process, W_by = −ΔU = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 561 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P V^(5/3) = const and Q = 0 to obtain 561 J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in |ΔU| = (3/2)|P_B V_B − P_A V_A| when applying Q = 0 => |W| = |ΔU|.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the isothermal work formula P_A V_A |ln(V_B / V_A)| instead of adiabatic work.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as constant at P_A, computing P_A |V_B − V_A| instead of adiabatic work.

items.stem: A thermal bath keeps 0.3 mol of ideal gas in a variable-volume optical pressure cell at 280 K during a reversible expansion from 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 0.01125 m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is the thermal energy Q supplied to the gas (equal to work done by the gas)?
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 280 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.3 × 8.31 × 280 × ln(0.01125 / 2.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.05 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 1.05 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds U = (3/2)nRT to isothermal work, overlooking that ΔU = 0 at constant temperature.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as remaining constant at P_A, computing P_A(V_B − V_A) instead of ∫ P dV = nRT ln(V_B / V_A).

items.stem: Starting at state A (1.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 3.6 × 10⁻³ m³), 0.8 mol of monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber is compressed adiabatically to 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³, heated at constant volume to 1.623 × 10⁶ Pa, expanded adiabatically to 3.6 × 10⁻³ m³, and cooled at constant volume back to A. Find η.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic Otto cycle (γ = 5/3), η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1) = 1 − (1.2 × 10⁻³ / 3.6 × 10⁻³)^(2/3) = 0.519 (equivalently W_net / Q_in = 933.2 / 1.797 × 10³ = 0.519).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 0.519 (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Applies an extra factor of one-half from misremembering the degrees-of-freedom or geometric prefactor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses exponent 1 instead of γ − 1 = 2/3 in the Otto efficiency relation η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Raises V_min / V_max to γ = 5/3 rather than γ − 1 = 2/3.

items.stem: The phase-change graph plots temperature against thermal energy transferred for 0.65 kg of ethanol in a lagged laboratory phase-transition calorimeter warmed from 139 K to 244 K across its melting point at 159 K (c_solid = 1120 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, specific latent heat of fusion L_f = 1.08 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹). Calculate the total thermal energy required.
items.workedSolution: Sensible heating: Q_sens = 0.65 × 1120 × (159 − 139) + 0.65 × 2440 × (244 − 159) = 1.494 × 10⁵ J. Latent heat on plateau: Q_lat = mL = 0.65 × 1.08 × 10⁵ = 7.020 × 10⁴ J. Total Q = 2.20 × 10⁵ J.

markScheme.criterion: Sums sensible mcΔT stages and latent heat mL to obtain 2.20 × 10⁵ J (C).

items.stem: Inside a double-walled vacuum Dewar mixing vessel, 0.55 kg of ethanol (specific heat capacity 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 302 K receives a 0.36 kg aluminium specimen (c = 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 410 K. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. Calculate the equilibrium temperature of the mixture.
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l), giving T_eq = 323.0 K. Therefore T_eq = 323 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 323 K (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Applies an extra factor of one-half from misremembering the degrees-of-freedom or geometric prefactor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Takes the unweighted arithmetic mean of the two initial temperatures, ignoring both masses and specific heat capacities.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Swaps the specific heat capacities of the solid specimen and the liquid bath.

items.stem: Inside a sealed foam-insulated metallurgical quench tank, a 0.3 kg block of melting ice at 273.15 K is placed into 0.28 kg of water initially at 289.15 K (c_water = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹). Because the ice mass is large, the mixture reaches phase-coexistence equilibrium at 273.15 K. What mass of ice melts?
items.workedSolution: Maximum heat released by water cooling to 273.15 K is Q = 0.28 × 4180 × (289.15 − 273.15) = 1.873 × 10⁴ J, which is less than m_ice L_f = 1.002 × 10⁵ J. Mass melted Δm = Q / L_f = 0.0561 kg.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δm = m_water c_water (T_water − 273.15) / L_f to obtain 0.0561 kg (B).

items.stem: An energy-budget sensor monitors an arid continental land-surface test plot (area 2.5 m², greybody emissivity 0.95) maintained at 314 K within a radiative environment at 286 K. Using σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, calculate P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴).
items.workedSolution: Net radiative power loss P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) = 0.95 × 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × 2.5 × ((314)⁴ − (286)⁴) = 408 W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) to obtain 408 W (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates e σ A (T − T_amb)⁴ instead of e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴), a classic fourth-power algebra error.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the greybody emissivity factor e (< 1) from P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates gross emitted power e σ A T⁴ and ignores incoming radiation absorbed from the surroundings at T_amb.

items.stem: A sample of 1.2 mol of monatomic Argon-40 (Ar) (M = 40 g mol⁻¹) occupies an orbital satellite attitude-control propellant cylinder of fixed volume 8.0 × 10⁻³ m³ at 310 K. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, calculate the bulk density ρ of the gas.
items.workedSolution: Total gas mass m = nM = 1.2 × 0.04 = 0.04800 kg. Density ρ = m / V = 0.04800 / 8.0 × 10⁻³ = 6.00 kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Applies ρ = nM / V in SI units to obtain 6.00 kg m⁻³ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies total gas mass nM by container volume V instead of dividing by V.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes molar concentration n / V (mol m⁻³) and omits multiplication by molar mass M.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Leaves molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of converting to kg mol⁻¹, overestimating density by a factor of 1000.

items.stem: Thermalised Xenon-131 (Xe) vapour of molar mass 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹ fills a thermostatted noble-gas reference bulb at a uniform temperature of 310 K. Given k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and 1 eV = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, Determine the mean kinetic energy per atom expressed in eV.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 310 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 0.0401 eV (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates (1/2) k_B T / e for a single degree of freedom instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes k_B T / e and omits the 3/2 translational factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the 3/2 factor to 3 k_B T / e by omitting the 1/2 in kinetic energy.

items.stem: A sample of 1.2 mol of ideal gas in a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder undergoes an isobaric expansion from state A (1.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B (0.011 m³), followed by an isochoric rise to 2.24 × 10⁵ Pa at state C. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, find the absolute temperature at B.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates PV / (nR) at the target state to obtain 176 K (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Charles's law ratio, multiplying T_A by V_A / V_B instead of V_B / V_A.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Stops after computing the initial temperature T_A = P_A V_A / (nR) without scaling by V_B / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the final temperature T_C at state C rather than the intermediate temperature T_B.

items.stem: The diagram shows a closed four-leg cycle A → B → C → D → A for 0.5 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals, bounded by P_low = 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa, P_high = 2.5 × 10⁵ Pa, V_min = 1.8 × 10⁻³ m³, and V_max = 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the thermal efficiency η = W_net / Q_in of this rectangular monatomic-gas cycle?
items.workedSolution: W_net = (2.5 × 10⁵ − 1.0 × 10⁵)(4.5 × 10⁻³ − 1.8 × 10⁻³) = 405.0 J. Heat enters on D → A and A → B: Q_in = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min + (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 2.092 × 10³ J. Efficiency η = W_net / Q_in = 0.194.

markScheme.criterion: Computes thermalEfficiency correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 0.194 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides W_net by Q_AB alone, neglecting the heat input Q_DA on the isochoric leg D → A.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits internal energy gain ΔU_AB when computing total heat input Q_in.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the Carnot efficiency 1 − T_min / T_max between extreme corner temperatures instead of the actual cycle efficiency W_net / Q_in.

items.stem: Maintained in thermal contact with a 520 K bath, 0.85 mol of ideal gas in a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder expands quasi-statically from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine ΔS = Q / T for the gas.
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.85 × 8.31 × ln(4.0 × 10⁻³ / 2.0 × 10⁻³) = 4.90 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 4.90 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 logarithm log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of the natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Replaces ln(V_B / V_A) with the linear fractional change (V_B − V_A) / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes isothermal heat Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) without dividing by T to obtain ΔS = Q / T.

items.stem: The diagram shows a reversible Carnot cycle A → B → C → D → A for 1.4 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber coupled to a hot reservoir at 704 K and a cold sink at 320 K, with isothermal expansion from 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 5.25 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what magnitude of thermal energy Q_C is rejected to the cold sink per cycle?
items.workedSolution: During isothermal compression C → D at T_C = 320 K, V_C / V_D = V_B / V_A, so heat rejected to the cold sink is Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) = 4.66 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 4.66 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A) in Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes net work W_net = Q_H − Q_C instead of the rejected heat Q_C.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the heat absorbed Q_H from the hot reservoir instead of the heat Q_C rejected to the cold sink.

items.stem: Calorimetric heating carries 1.25 kg of lead in a metallurgical vacuum-induction melting pot from an initial solid temperature of 551 K up to 631 K as liquid. Using 600.6 K for the melting point, specific heat capacities 128 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ (solid) and 147 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ (liquid), and specific latent heat of fusion L_f = 2.3 × 10⁴ J kg⁻¹, determine the total enthalpy input.

markScheme.criterion: Sums sensible mcΔT stages and latent heat mL to obtain 4.23 × 10⁴ J (D).

items.stem: A 0.3 kg charge of aluminium starts at 896 K and finishes at 994 K inside a sealed industrial distillation reboiler test cell while an electrical immersion heater of input power 1200 W and thermal transfer efficiency 0.85 supplies energy. Using fusion temperature 933.5 K, specific heats 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ (solid) and 1180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ (liquid), and latent heat 3.97 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹, find the overall elapsed time.
items.workedSolution: Effective thermal power P_eff = η P = 0.85 × 1200 = 1.020 × 10³ W. Total energy Q_tot = m c_solid ΔT_s + m L_f + m c_liquid ΔT_l = 1.506 × 10⁵ J, giving t_total = Q_tot / P_eff = 148 s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_eff = η P and divides required thermal energy to obtain 148 s (D).

options.distractorRationale: Omits the latent-heat plateau duration m L_f / (η P) and includes only sensible temperature-change intervals.

options.label: B

items.stem: A 0.055 kg cube of sub-zero ice at 253.15 K is dropped into 0.38 kg of warm water at 328.15 K inside a low-heat-capacity polymeric calorimetry beaker (fusion point 273.15 K, specific heats 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ for ice and 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ for water, latent heat of fusion 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹). All the ice melts. Calculate T_eq.
items.workedSolution: Energy to warm and melt all ice at 273.15 K: Q_1+2 = 0.055 × 2100 × (273.15 − 253.15) + 0.055 × 3.34 × 10⁵ = 2.068 × 10⁴ J. Energy balance with warm water: m_w c_w (328.15 − T_eq) = Q_1+2 + m_ice c_w (T_eq − 273.15), giving T_eq = 310 K.

markScheme.criterion: Includes sub-zero ice warming, fusion latent heat, and meltwater warming to obtain 310 K (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Applies an extra factor of one-half from misremembering the degrees-of-freedom or geometric prefactor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Introduces an extraneous integer factor when rearranging the governing thermal relation.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Introduces an extraneous integer factor when rearranging the governing thermal relation.

items.stem: Radiometric observations characterise a high-temperature graphite blackbody furnace aperture (ideal blackbody, area 1.4 × 10¹⁹ m², surface temperature 8800 K) from a separation d = 4.2 × 10¹¹ m. Taking σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, what is the radiant intensity received at distance d (neglecting intervening absorption)?
items.workedSolution: Radiated luminosity L = σ A T⁴ = 4.760 × 10²⁷ W. Intensity at distance d is I = L / (4π d²) = 4.760 × 10²⁷ / (4π × (4.2 × 10¹¹)²) = 2.15 × 10³ W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the blackbody radiation law in SI units to obtain 2.15 × 10³ W m⁻² (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides radiated power by disc area π d² instead of spherical shell area 4π d².

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the geometric factor 4π for isotropic spherical spreading in I = L / (4π d²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides by 4π d instead of 4π d², omitting the inverse-square exponent.

items.stem: 0.35 mol of monatomic Krypton-84 (Kr) (molar mass 0.0838 kg mol⁻¹) fills a cryogenic buffer reservoir in a superconducting magnet rig of volume 0.016 m³ at a steady temperature of 67 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Find the gas pressure.
items.workedSolution: Convert temperature to kelvin: T = 67 + 273.15 = 340.15 K. From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (0.35 × 8.31 × 340.15) / 0.016 = 6.18 × 10⁴ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 6.18 × 10⁴ Pa (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies nRT by volume V instead of dividing nRT by V.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes Celsius temperature θ directly into pV = nRT without converting to absolute temperature in kelvin.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the amount of substance n in p = nRT / V, solving for 1 mol instead of the given molar amount.

items.stem: At 480 K, 0.3 mol of Xenon-131 (Xe) with molar mass 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹ fills a thick-walled titanium deep-sea pressure housing (capacity 0.05 m³). Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), calculate the root-mean-square speed marked v_rms on the distribution.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 480 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 480 / 0.1313) = 302 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 302 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: On the pressure–temperature (P–T) diagram, 0.5 mol of an ideal gas in a precision pneumatic actuator chamber sealed with a movable piston starts at state A (1.1 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³), expands at constant pressure to 8.8 × 10⁻³ m³ at state B, and is then heated at constant volume to a final pressure of 1.54 × 10⁵ Pa at state C. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the final temperature T_C at state C?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates PV / (nR) at the target state to obtain 326 K (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reports the final temperature converted to °C when the question and options specify kelvin.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses the initial volume V_A instead of V_B = V_C when evaluating T_C = P_C V_C / (nR).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes T_B after the isobaric stage and omits the isochoric pressure ratio P_C / P_A.

items.stem: A sample of 1.5 mol of an ideal monatomic gas in a cryocooler compression cylinder containing monatomic working gas expands isobarically at constant pressure 3.75 × 10⁵ Pa from volume 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³ (state A) to 9.1 × 10⁻³ m³ (state B). Taking thermal energy supplied to the gas and work done by the gas as positive, how much thermal energy Q is supplied to the gas during A → B?
items.workedSolution: Work done by the gas W_by = P(V_B − V_A) = 3.75 × 10⁵ × (9.1 × 10⁻³ − 3.5 × 10⁻³) = 2.100 × 10³ J. For a monatomic ideal gas, ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV = 3.150 × 10³ J. By the first law, Q = ΔU + W_by = (5/2) P ΔV = 5.25 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 5.25 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the boundary work W = P ΔV done by the gas and ignores the increase in internal energy ΔU.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the internal energy change ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV and omits the expansion work P ΔV.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV, computing ΔU + W = P ΔV + P ΔV = 2 P ΔV instead of (5/2) P ΔV.

items.stem: Inside a variable-volume optical pressure cell, 0.5 mol of an ideal monatomic gas (adiabatic index γ = 5/3) initially at P_A = 4.8 × 10⁵ Pa and V_A = 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ is reversibly and adiabatically expanded to V_B = 7.5 × 10⁻³ m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Taking work done by the gas as positive, how much mechanical work is done by the gas during A → B?
items.workedSolution: First find P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 1.042 × 10⁵ Pa. Since Q = 0 in an adiabatic process, W_by = −ΔU = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 987 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P V^(5/3) = const and Q = 0 to obtain 987 J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in |ΔU| = (3/2)|P_B V_B − P_A V_A| when applying Q = 0 => |W| = |ΔU|.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the isothermal work formula P_A V_A |ln(V_B / V_A)| instead of adiabatic work.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as constant at P_A, computing P_A |V_B − V_A| instead of adiabatic work.

items.stem: Inside a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber, 2.2 mol of ideal gas is held at a constant temperature of 450 K while expanding reversibly from V_A = 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 7.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking work done by the gas as positive and R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, how much work is done by the gas?
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 450 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 2.2 × 8.31 × 450 × ln(7.0 × 10⁻³ / 3.5 × 10⁻³) = 5.70 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 5.70 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as remaining constant at P_A, computing P_A(V_B − V_A) instead of ∫ P dV = nRT ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Adds U = (3/2)nRT to isothermal work, overlooking that ΔU = 0 at constant temperature.

items.stem: The P–V diagram shows an ideal Otto cycle for 0.25 mol of monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) in a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell, compressing adiabatically from V_max = 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (at 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa) to V_min = 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³, heating isochorically to 8.382 × 10⁵ Pa, expanding adiabatically to 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³, and cooling isochorically back to state A. Calculate the cycle efficiency η = W_net / Q_in.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic Otto cycle (γ = 5/3), η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1) = 1 − (1.5 × 10⁻³ / 3.0 × 10⁻³)^(2/3) = 0.370 (equivalently W_net / Q_in = 380.6 / 1.029 × 10³ = 0.370).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 0.370 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses exponent 1 instead of γ − 1 = 2/3 in the Otto efficiency relation η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Raises V_min / V_max to γ = 5/3 rather than γ − 1 = 2/3.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes Carnot efficiency 1 − T_A / T_C between extreme cycle temperatures instead of Otto efficiency.

items.stem: In a ceramic-lined materials characterization furnace, a Peltier extraction module rated at 320 W with coupling efficiency 0.75 removes thermal energy as a 0.75 kg sample of water goes from 298 K to 235 K across its 273.15 K fusion point (c_solid = 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹). How long does the isothermal freezing plateau last?
items.workedSolution: Effective thermal power P_eff = η P = 0.75 × 320 = 240.0 W. Plateau latent energy Q_f = m L_f = 2.505 × 10⁵ J, giving Δt_plateau = Q_f / P_eff = 1.04 × 10³ s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_eff = η P and divides required thermal energy to obtain 1.04 × 10³ s (C).

items.stem: A heated brass block of mass 0.36 kg and specific heat capacity 380 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 475 K is plunged into 0.32 kg of water (c = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 290 K inside a precision isothermal-jacket mixing cup. During mixing, 1250 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. How much thermal energy is released by the brass block in reaching equilibrium?
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l) + 1250, giving T_eq = 306.3 K. Heat released by the solid Q_lost = m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = 2.31 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 2.31 × 10⁴ J (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the final equilibrium temperature is the unweighted midpoint (T_solid + T_liquid) / 2.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the heat gained by the liquid bath without adding the heat lost to the surroundings.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the solid cools all the way down to the initial bath temperature T_liquid instead of T_eq.

items.stem: Radiometric observations characterise a nearby solar-type star modelled as an ideal spherical radiator (ideal blackbody, area 8.0 × 10⁻⁴ m², surface temperature 2600 K) from a separation d = 2.4 m. Taking Wien's constant b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K, what is the peak emission wavelength λ_max in nanometres?
items.workedSolution: By Wien's displacement law, λ_max = b / T = (2.90 × 10⁻³) / 2600 = 1.115 × 10⁻⁶ m = 1.12 × 10³ nm.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the blackbody radiation law in SI units to obtain 1.12 × 10³ nm (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Wien's displacement law by dividing T by b instead of b by T.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts 273.15 from the kelvin temperature before applying Wien's law.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies Wien's constant b by T instead of dividing b by T.

items.stem: In a climate radiative-transfer model, a dark oceanic mixed-layer surface patch of area 4 m² and surface emissivity e = 0.88 is at 350 K while exchanging thermal infrared radiation with an effective surrounding environment at 255 K. Taking σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, what is the net rate of radiative energy loss P_net from the surface?
items.workedSolution: Net radiative power loss P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) = 0.88 × 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × 4 × ((350)⁴ − (255)⁴) = 2.15 × 10³ W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) to obtain 2.15 × 10³ W (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates e σ A (T − T_amb)⁴ instead of e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴), a classic fourth-power algebra error.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the greybody emissivity factor e (< 1) from P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates gross emitted power e σ A T⁴ and ignores incoming radiation absorbed from the surroundings at T_amb.

items.stem: In a thermostatted noble-gas reference bulb (volume 0.015 m³), 1.2 mol of monatomic Helium-4 (He) of molar mass 4 g mol⁻¹ is warmed from T₁ = 290 K to T₂ = 522 K, shifting the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed curve as plotted. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), determine v_rms at the higher temperature T₂.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 522 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 522 / 4.0 × 10⁻³) = 1.80 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 1.80 × 10³ m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: Spectroscopic thermometry confirms that Neon-20 (Ne) atoms (molar mass 0.0202 kg mol⁻¹) in a sealed borosilicate acoustic-thermometry sphere are equilibrated at 137 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Given k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and 1 eV = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, Determine the mean kinetic energy per atom expressed in eV.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 410.15 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 0.0531 eV (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates (1/2) k_B T / e for a single degree of freedom instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Applies an extra factor of one-half from misremembering the degrees-of-freedom or geometric prefactor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes k_B T / e and omits the 3/2 translational factor.

items.stem: The P–V graph shows an isobaric compression of 1.5 mol of ideal monatomic gas inside a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals at 7.2 × 10⁵ Pa from V_A = 5.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³. Using the sign convention where work done on the gas is positive, determine the compression work done on the gas.
items.workedSolution: During isobaric compression from 5.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at 7.2 × 10⁵ Pa, work done on the gas W_on = −P(V_B − V_A) = 7.2 × 10⁵ × (5.5 × 10⁻³ − 2.5 × 10⁻³) = 2.16 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 2.16 × 10³ J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the magnitude of internal energy change |ΔU| = (3/2) P |ΔV| instead of boundary work P |ΔV|.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies pressure by initial volume V_A instead of the volume change |V_B − V_A|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the total heat rejected |Q| = (5/2) P |ΔV| rather than the mechanical work done on the gas.

items.stem: In a closed noble-gas power-conversion loop, 0.2 mol of a monatomic ideal gas executes a clockwise closed cycle A → B → C → D → A between pressures 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa and 5.4 × 10⁵ Pa and volumes 1.8 × 10⁻³ m³ and 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³ (A → B isobaric expansion at 5.4 × 10⁵ Pa, B → C isochoric cooling, C → D isobaric compression at 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa, D → A isochoric heating). What is the total thermal energy Q_in absorbed by the monatomic gas during the heating legs D → A and A → B?
items.workedSolution: Heat enters on D → A (isochoric, W = 0): Q_DA = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min = 972.0 J, and on A → B (isobaric): Q_AB = (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 3.645 × 10³ J. Total Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = 4.62 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes heatInputJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 4.62 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Confuses net cycle heat Q_net = W_net with total heat input Q_in absorbed from the hot source.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Applies an extra factor of one-half from misremembering the degrees-of-freedom or geometric prefactor.

options.label: C

items.stem: The P–V curve shows a reversible isothermal expansion at 400 K of 1.6 mol of ideal gas inside a frictionless piston-cylinder assembly on a thermodynamics test bench from volume 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 9.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). Calculate the entropy increase ΔS of the gas.
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.6 × 8.31 × ln(9.0 × 10⁻³ / 2.0 × 10⁻³) = 20.0 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 20.0 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 logarithm log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of the natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Replaces ln(V_B / V_A) with the linear fractional change (V_B − V_A) / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes isothermal heat Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) without dividing by T to obtain ΔS = Q / T.

items.stem: A Carnot engine modelled in a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell uses 0.3 mol of ideal gas operating between a hot reservoir at 481 K and a cold sink at 260 K. During the high-temperature isothermal stage A → B, the volume increases from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 7.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking net work done by the gas as positive (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹), what is the net work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.502 × 10³ J and η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 0.4595. Net work output W_net = η Q_H = nR(T_H − T_C) ln(V_B / V_A) = 690 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 690 J (B).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the rejected heat Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) instead of net work Q_H − Q_C.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) without multiplying by Carnot efficiency (1 − T_C / T_H).

items.stem: A 0.25 kg specimen of pure water inside an automated cryostat sample holder is heated from 223 K (solid) to 303 K (liquid). Take melting point = 273.15 K, c_solid = 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, and specific latent heat of fusion L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹. Find the total heat transferred to the specimen.

markScheme.criterion: Sums sensible mcΔT stages and latent heat mL to obtain 1.41 × 10⁵ J (C).

items.stem: During a timed run in a guarded electrical immersion-heating vessel, an electrical immersion heater of input power 1200 W and thermal transfer efficiency 0.85 supplies energy on 0.2 kg of ethanol between 121 K and 184 K. Given melting point 159 K, L_f = 1.08 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹, c_s = 1120 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, and c_l = 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine the total run time.
items.workedSolution: Effective thermal power P_eff = η P = 0.85 × 1200 = 1.020 × 10³ W. Total energy Q_tot = m c_solid ΔT_s + m L_f + m c_liquid ΔT_l = 4.231 × 10⁴ J, giving t_total = Q_tot / P_eff = 41.5 s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_eff = η P and divides required thermal energy to obtain 41.5 s (D).

items.stem: In an insulated mixing test within a stirred insulated immersion calorimeter, 0.065 kg of solid H₂O at 268.15 K dissolves thermally into 0.68 kg of water initially at 328.15 K. Data: melting temperature 273.15 K; c_s = 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹; c_l = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹; specific fusion enthalpy 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹. Which equilibrium temperature is reached?
items.workedSolution: Energy to warm and melt all ice at 273.15 K: Q_1+2 = 0.065 × 2100 × (273.15 − 268.15) + 0.065 × 3.34 × 10⁵ = 2.239 × 10⁴ J. Energy balance with warm water: m_w c_w (328.15 − T_eq) = Q_1+2 + m_ice c_w (T_eq − 273.15), giving T_eq = 316 K.

markScheme.criterion: Includes sub-zero ice warming, fusion latent heat, and meltwater warming to obtain 316 K (B).

items.stem: An energy-budget sensor monitors a polar sea-ice radiative-balance monitoring sector (area 1.2 m², greybody emissivity 0.95) maintained at 310 K within a radiative environment at 268 K. Using σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, calculate P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴).
items.workedSolution: Net radiative power loss P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) = 0.95 × 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × 1.2 × ((310)⁴ − (268)⁴) = 263 W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) to obtain 263 W (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates e σ A (T − T_amb)⁴ instead of e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴), a classic fourth-power algebra error.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the greybody emissivity factor e (< 1) from P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates gross emitted power e σ A T⁴ and ignores incoming radiation absorbed from the surroundings at T_amb.

items.stem: Engineers charge a high-vacuum synchrotron beamline gas target (capacity 0.016 m³) with 0.85 mol of Helium-4 (He) of molar mass 4 g mol⁻¹ at an equilibrium temperature of 47 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15) (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). Determine the density of the confined gas.
items.workedSolution: Total gas mass m = nM = 0.85 × 4.0 × 10⁻³ = 3.400 × 10⁻³ kg. Density ρ = m / V = 3.400 × 10⁻³ / 0.016 = 0.212 kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Applies ρ = nM / V in SI units to obtain 0.212 kg m⁻³ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies total gas mass nM by container volume V instead of dividing by V.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes molar concentration n / V (mol m⁻³) and omits multiplication by molar mass M.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Leaves molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of converting to kg mol⁻¹, overestimating density by a factor of 1000.

items.stem: A low-density plasma-free Argon-40 (Ar) sample (M = 0.04 kg mol⁻¹) is held in an atmospheric research dropsonde reference chamber at 440 K. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the molar internal energy of this ideal monatomic gas?
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic gas, molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T = 1.5 × 8.31 × 440 = 5.48 × 10³ J mol⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 440 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 5.48 × 10³ J mol⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Includes only one translational degree of freedom (1/2 R T) instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses molar enthalpy C_p T = (5/2) R T instead of molar internal energy (3/2) R T.

items.stem: Starting from state A (2.2 × 10⁵ Pa, 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³) in a cryocooler compression cylinder containing monatomic working gas, 0.5 mol of ideal gas expands isobarically to 0.0132 m³ (state B) and is heated isochorically until the pressure reaches 5.28 × 10⁵ Pa (state C). Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, find the temperature in state C.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates PV / (nR) at the target state to obtain 1.68 × 10³ K (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes T_B after the isobaric stage and omits the isochoric pressure ratio P_C / P_A.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses the initial volume V_A instead of V_B = V_C when evaluating T_C = P_C V_C / (nR).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Reports the final temperature converted to °C when the question and options specify kelvin.

items.stem: A heat-engine test rig (a variable-volume optical pressure cell) drives 0.8 mol of ideal monatomic gas around a rectangular cycle with upper pressure 4.5 × 10⁵ Pa, lower pressure 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa, minimum volume 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³, and maximum volume 0.01 m³. What is the thermal efficiency η = W_net / Q_in of this rectangular monatomic-gas cycle?
items.workedSolution: W_net = (4.5 × 10⁵ − 1.8 × 10⁵)(0.01 − 4.0 × 10⁻³) = 1.620 × 10³ J. Heat enters on D → A and A → B: Q_in = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min + (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 8.370 × 10³ J. Efficiency η = W_net / Q_in = 0.194.

markScheme.criterion: Computes thermalEfficiency correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 0.194 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides W_net by Q_AB alone, neglecting the heat input Q_DA on the isochoric leg D → A.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits internal energy gain ΔU_AB when computing total heat input Q_in.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the Carnot efficiency 1 − T_min / T_max between extreme corner temperatures instead of the actual cycle efficiency W_net / Q_in.

items.stem: A thermally isolated sample of 0.75 mol of monatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber transitions adiabatically from state A (1.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 8.0 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B of volume 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, Taking work done on the gas as positive, how much mechanical work is done on the gas during A → B?
items.workedSolution: First find P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 1.613 × 10⁶ Pa. Since Q = 0 in an adiabatic process, W_on = +ΔU = (3/2)(P_B V_B − P_A V_A) = 2.92 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P V^(5/3) = const and Q = 0 to obtain 2.92 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as constant at P_A, computing P_A |V_B − V_A| instead of adiabatic work.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses the isothermal work formula P_A V_A |ln(V_B / V_A)| instead of adiabatic work.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in |ΔU| = (3/2)|P_B V_B − P_A V_A| when applying Q = 0 => |W| = |ΔU|.

items.stem: The diagram shows a reversible Carnot cycle A → B → C → D → A for 1.4 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder coupled to a hot reservoir at 527 °C and a cold sink at 27 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15), with isothermal expansion from 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ to 2.4 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what magnitude of thermal energy Q_C is rejected to the cold sink per cycle?
items.workedSolution: During isothermal compression C → D at T_C = 300.15 K, V_C / V_D = V_B / V_A, so heat rejected to the cold sink is Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) = 2.42 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 2.42 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A) in Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes net work W_net = Q_H − Q_C instead of the rejected heat Q_C.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the heat absorbed Q_H from the hot reservoir instead of the heat Q_C rejected to the cold sink.

items.stem: Starting at state A (1.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³), 0.25 mol of monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) in a precision pneumatic actuator chamber sealed with a movable piston is compressed adiabatically to 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³, heated at constant volume to 1.123 × 10⁶ Pa, expanded adiabatically to 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³, and cooled at constant volume back to A. Find η.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic Otto cycle (γ = 5/3), η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1) = 1 − (1.5 × 10⁻³ / 4.5 × 10⁻³)^(2/3) = 0.519 (equivalently W_net / Q_in = 583.2 / 1.123 × 10³ = 0.519).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 0.519 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses exponent 1 instead of γ − 1 = 2/3 in the Otto efficiency relation η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes Carnot efficiency 1 − T_A / T_C between extreme cycle temperatures instead of Otto efficiency.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Raises V_min / V_max to γ = 5/3 rather than γ − 1 = 2/3.

items.stem: In a spacecraft latent-heat thermal-buffer canister, an electrical immersion heater of input power 450 W and thermal transfer efficiency 0.9 supplies energy as a 0.55 kg sample of lead goes from 563 K to 661 K across its 600.6 K fusion point (c_solid = 128 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 147 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, L_f = 2.3 × 10⁴ J kg⁻¹). How long does the isothermal melting plateau last?
items.workedSolution: Effective thermal power P_eff = η P = 0.9 × 450 = 405.0 W. Plateau latent energy Q_f = m L_f = 1.265 × 10⁴ J, giving Δt_plateau = Q_f / P_eff = 31.2 s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_eff = η P and divides required thermal energy to obtain 31.2 s (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies time by efficiency η instead of dividing energy by effective power η P.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides thermal energy by the nominal electrical rating P rather than the effective thermal power η P.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the total multi-stage duration rather than the isothermal fusion plateau duration alone.

items.stem: In a calorimetry run using a sealed foam-insulated metallurgical quench tank, a 0.18 kg cylinder of copper (c = 385 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 475 K is quenched in 0.55 kg of mineral oil (c = 1960 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 302 K. During mixing, 950 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. Find T_eq at thermal equilibrium.
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l) + 950, giving T_eq = 311.6 K. Therefore T_eq = 312 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 312 K (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Applies an extra factor of one-half from misremembering the degrees-of-freedom or geometric prefactor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Weights initial temperatures by mass alone and ignores the much larger specific heat capacity of the liquid.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Takes the unweighted arithmetic mean of the two initial temperatures, ignoring both masses and specific heat capacities.

items.stem: The Planck spectral curve shown corresponds to a luminous A-type stellar photosphere of radiating area 3.2 × 10⁻³ m² and uniform blackbody temperature 2600 K, monitored by a radiometer 1.5 m away. Taking σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, what is the radiant intensity received at distance d (neglecting intervening absorption)?
items.workedSolution: Radiated luminosity L = σ A T⁴ = 8.291 × 10³ W. Intensity at distance d is I = L / (4π d²) = 8.291 × 10³ / (4π × (1.5)²) = 293 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the blackbody radiation law in SI units to obtain 293 W m⁻² (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides by 4π d instead of 4π d², omitting the inverse-square exponent.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides radiated power by disc area π d² instead of spherical shell area 4π d².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the geometric factor 4π for isotropic spherical spreading in I = L / (4π d²).

items.stem: Telemetry from a selectively coated solar-thermal collector plate (area 1.2 m², emissivity 0.84) records a surface temperature of 296 K in surroundings at 268 K (σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴). Calculate the gross emitted intensity e σ T⁴ from the surface.
items.workedSolution: Gross radiated intensity (exitance) M = e σ T⁴ = 0.84 × 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × (296)⁴ = 366 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates e σ T⁴ to obtain 366 W m⁻² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Applies an extra factor of one-half from misremembering the degrees-of-freedom or geometric prefactor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats the surface as an ideal blackbody (e = 1) and omits the emissivity factor e.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides blackbody exitance σ T⁴ by emissivity e instead of multiplying by e.

items.stem: An experiment records the molecular speed distribution of 2 mol of Argon-40 (Ar) gas (molar mass 40 g mol⁻¹) occupying 0.015 m³ in a sealed borosilicate acoustic-thermometry sphere at 550 K (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²)). Which value equals the rms speed of the atoms?
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.04 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 550 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 550 / 0.04) = 585 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 585 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: In a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals, 0.75 mol of an ideal gas starts at state A with pressure 2.2 × 10⁵ Pa and volume 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³. As shown on the pressure–temperature (P–T) diagram, the gas expands isobarically from A to state B of volume 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³, before undergoing isochoric heating from B to state C at 3.52 × 10⁵ Pa. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the temperature T_B at state B?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates PV / (nR) at the target state to obtain 159 K (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Charles's law ratio, multiplying T_A by V_A / V_B instead of V_B / V_A.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Stops after computing the initial temperature T_A = P_A V_A / (nR) without scaling by V_B / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the final temperature T_C at state C rather than the intermediate temperature T_B.

items.stem: A sample of 0.8 mol of an ideal monatomic gas in a closed noble-gas power-conversion loop expands isobarically at constant pressure 4.8 × 10⁵ Pa from volume 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ (state A) to 2.7 × 10⁻³ m³ (state B). Taking thermal energy supplied to the gas and work done by the gas as positive, how much thermal energy Q is supplied to the gas during A → B?
items.workedSolution: Work done by the gas W_by = P(V_B − V_A) = 4.8 × 10⁵ × (2.7 × 10⁻³ − 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 576.0 J. For a monatomic ideal gas, ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV = 864.0 J. By the first law, Q = ΔU + W_by = (5/2) P ΔV = 1.44 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 1.44 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the boundary work W = P ΔV done by the gas and ignores the increase in internal energy ΔU.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the internal energy change ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV and omits the expansion work P ΔV.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV, computing ΔU + W = P ΔV + P ΔV = 2 P ΔV instead of (5/2) P ΔV.

items.stem: Inside a frictionless piston-cylinder assembly on a thermodynamics test bench, 0.25 mol of an ideal monatomic gas (adiabatic index γ = 5/3) initially at P_A = 3.2 × 10⁵ Pa and V_A = 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ is reversibly and adiabatically expanded to V_B = 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the final pressure P_B in state B?
items.workedSolution: For a monatomic adiabatic process, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 3.2 × 10⁵ × (3.0 × 10⁻³ / 6.0 × 10⁻³)^(5/3) = 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P V^(5/3) = const to obtain 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses the diatomic adiabatic index γ = 7/5 instead of γ = 5/3 for a monatomic gas.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats the process as isothermal (P_A V_A = P_B V_B) rather than adiabatic (P_A V_A^(5/3) = P_B V_B^(5/3)).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the adiabatic exponent, using 3/5 instead of γ = 5/3.

items.stem: In a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder coupled to a thermal reservoir at 450 K, 0.85 mol of an ideal gas expands reversibly and isothermally from V_A = 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 8.4 × 10⁻³ m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the change in entropy ΔS of the gas?
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.85 × 8.31 × ln(8.4 × 10⁻³ / 3.5 × 10⁻³) = 6.18 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 6.18 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 logarithm log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of the natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Replaces ln(V_B / V_A) with the linear fractional change (V_B − V_A) / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes isothermal heat Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) without dividing by T to obtain ΔS = Q / T.

items.stem: Inside a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity, 0.4 mol of an ideal monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) performs a closed three-step cycle A → B → C → A: reversible adiabatic expansion from state A (4.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to volume 3.75 × 10⁻³ m³ at B, isobaric compression from B to volume 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at C, and isochoric heating from C back to A. Taking work done by the gas as positive, what is the net work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: At B, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 9.772 × 10⁴ Pa. Adiabatic work W_AB = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 462.8 J, and isobaric compression work W_BC = P_B(V_C − V_B) = -219.9 J (W_CA = 0). Thus W_net = W_AB + W_BC = 243 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 243 J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the magnitude of the isobaric compression work P_B(V_B − V_C).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the adiabatic expansion work W_AB and forgets to subtract the isobaric compression work |W_BC|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_CA along the isochoric leg instead of net work W_net.

items.stem: Starting at 551 K in a ceramic-lined materials characterization furnace, 1.25 kg of lead absorbs heat, crosses its 600.6 K melting point (specific latent heat of fusion L_f = 2.3 × 10⁴ J kg⁻¹), and finishes as liquid at 646 K. With c_solid = 128 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ and c_liquid = 147 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, how much energy was supplied?

markScheme.criterion: Sums sensible mcΔT stages and latent heat mL to obtain 4.50 × 10⁴ J (D).

items.stem: A heated aluminium block of mass 0.18 kg and specific heat capacity 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 410 K is plunged into 0.72 kg of water (c = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 298 K inside a low-heat-capacity polymeric calorimetry beaker. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. What is the final thermal equilibrium temperature T_eq?
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l), giving T_eq = 303.7 K. Therefore T_eq = 304 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 304 K (B).

items.stem: In an insulated mixing test within a vacuum-insulated stainless-steel Dewar flask, 0.035 kg of solid H₂O at 263.15 K dissolves thermally into 0.68 kg of water initially at 318.15 K. Data: melting temperature 273.15 K; c_s = 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹; c_l = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹; specific fusion enthalpy 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹. Which equilibrium temperature is reached?
items.workedSolution: Energy to warm and melt all ice at 273.15 K: Q_1+2 = 0.035 × 2100 × (273.15 − 263.15) + 0.035 × 3.34 × 10⁵ = 1.243 × 10⁴ J. Energy balance with warm water: m_w c_w (318.15 − T_eq) = Q_1+2 + m_ice c_w (T_eq − 273.15), giving T_eq = 312 K.

markScheme.criterion: Includes sub-zero ice warming, fusion latent heat, and meltwater warming to obtain 312 K (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Applies an extra factor of one-half from misremembering the degrees-of-freedom or geometric prefactor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Introduces an extraneous integer factor when rearranging the governing thermal relation.

options.label: D

items.stem: In a climate radiative-transfer model, a Martian mid-latitude rocky plain element of area 12 m² and surface emissivity e = 0.78 is at 381 K while exchanging thermal infrared radiation with an effective surrounding environment at 286 K. Taking σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, what is the net rate of radiative energy loss P_net from the surface?
items.workedSolution: Net radiative power loss P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) = 0.78 × 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × 12 × ((381)⁴ − (286)⁴) = 7.63 × 10³ W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) to obtain 7.63 × 10³ W (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates e σ A (T − T_amb)⁴ instead of e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴), a classic fourth-power algebra error.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the greybody emissivity factor e (< 1) from P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates gross emitted power e σ A T⁴ and ignores incoming radiation absorbed from the surroundings at T_amb.

items.stem: During an instrument check, a thermostatted noble-gas reference bulb of internal volume 0.016 m³ contains 0.45 mol of Argon-40 (Ar) (molar mass 40 g mol⁻¹) at 27 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15) (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is the pressure inside the chamber?
items.workedSolution: Convert temperature to kelvin: T = 27 + 273.15 = 300.15 K. From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (0.45 × 8.31 × 300.15) / 0.016 = 7.02 × 10⁴ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 7.02 × 10⁴ Pa (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies nRT by volume V instead of dividing nRT by V.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes Celsius temperature θ directly into pV = nRT without converting to absolute temperature in kelvin.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the amount of substance n in p = nRT / V, solving for 1 mol instead of the given molar amount.

items.stem: Monatomic Xenon-131 (Xe) gas (molar mass 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹) inside a rigid stainless-steel vacuum-calibration tank has the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed distribution shown at 327 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Use molar gas constant R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Calculate the internal energy per mole of the gas.
items.workedSolution: T = 327 + 273.15 = 600.15 K. For an ideal monatomic gas, molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T = 1.5 × 8.31 × 600.15 = 7.48 × 10³ J mol⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 600.15 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 7.48 × 10³ J mol⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Includes only one translational degree of freedom (1/2 R T) instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses molar enthalpy C_p T = (5/2) R T instead of molar internal energy (3/2) R T.

items.stem: 0.2 mol of ideal gas inside an insulated aerospace gas-accumulator cylinder follows path A → B → C on the volume–temperature (V–T) plot: an isobaric expansion from (2.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³) to V_B = 3.6 × 10⁻³ m³, then an isochoric pressure increase to P_C = 3.64 × 10⁵ Pa. Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine T_C.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates PV / (nR) at the target state to obtain 788 K (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses the initial volume V_A instead of V_B = V_C when evaluating T_C = P_C V_C / (nR).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Reports the final temperature converted to °C when the question and options specify kelvin.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes T_B after the isobaric stage and omits the isochoric pressure ratio P_C / P_A.

items.stem: Operating clockwise between 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³ and 0.016 m³ and between 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa and 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.5 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber completes cycle A → B → C → D → A. What is the total thermal energy Q_in absorbed by the monatomic gas during the heating legs D → A and A → B?
items.workedSolution: Heat enters on D → A (isochoric, W = 0): Q_DA = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min = 900.0 J, and on A → B (isobaric): Q_AB = (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 9.000 × 10³ J. Total Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = 9.90 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes heatInputJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 9.90 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Confuses net cycle heat Q_net = W_net with total heat input Q_in absorbed from the hot source.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic ΔU on both heating legs.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Includes only the heat absorbed during isobaric expansion A → B and omits the isochoric heating D → A.

items.stem: A thermal bath keeps 1.6 mol of ideal gas in a precision pneumatic actuator chamber sealed with a movable piston at 520 K during a reversible expansion from 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 0.012 m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is the thermal energy Q supplied to the gas (equal to work done by the gas)?
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 520 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.6 × 8.31 × 520 × ln(0.012 / 5.0 × 10⁻³) = 6.05 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 6.05 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as remaining constant at P_A, computing P_A(V_B − V_A) instead of ∫ P dV = nRT ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Adds U = (3/2)nRT to isothermal work, overlooking that ΔU = 0 at constant temperature.

items.stem: A Carnot engine modelled in a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity uses 1 mol of ideal gas operating between a hot reservoir at 527 °C and a cold sink at 47 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). During the high-temperature isothermal stage A → B, the volume increases from 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ to 4.2 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking net work done by the gas as positive (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹), what is the net work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) = 8.330 × 10³ J and η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 0.5999. Net work output W_net = η Q_H = nR(T_H − T_C) ln(V_B / V_A) = 5.00 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 5.00 × 10³ J (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the rejected heat Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) instead of net work Q_H − Q_C.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) without multiplying by Carnot efficiency (1 − T_C / T_H).

items.stem: A 0.25 kg specimen of pure aluminium inside a guarded electrical immersion-heating vessel is heated from 904 K (solid) to 1019 K (liquid). Take melting point = 933.5 K, c_solid = 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 1180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, and specific latent heat of fusion L_f = 3.97 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹. Find the total heat transferred to the specimen.

markScheme.criterion: Sums sensible mcΔT stages and latent heat mL to obtain 1.31 × 10⁵ J (D).

items.stem: In an adiabatic micro-calorimeter ampoule, a Peltier extraction module rated at 1200 W with coupling efficiency 0.9 removes thermal energy as a 0.55 kg sample of water goes from 333 K to 245 K across its 273.15 K fusion point (c_solid = 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹). How long does the isothermal freezing plateau last?
items.workedSolution: Effective thermal power P_eff = η P = 0.9 × 1200 = 1.080 × 10³ W. Plateau latent energy Q_f = m L_f = 1.837 × 10⁵ J, giving Δt_plateau = Q_f / P_eff = 170 s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_eff = η P and divides required thermal energy to obtain 170 s (C).

items.stem: A 0.28 kg bath of liquid water at 301.15 K in a closed-lid magnetic-stirrer calorimetry pot is stirred with 0.18 kg of ice already at its melting point of 273.15 K. Take c_water = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ and L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹. How many kilograms of ice melt by the time thermal equilibrium is established?
items.workedSolution: Maximum heat released by water cooling to 273.15 K is Q = 0.28 × 4180 × (301.15 − 273.15) = 3.277 × 10⁴ J, which is less than m_ice L_f = 6.012 × 10⁴ J. Mass melted Δm = Q / L_f = 0.0981 kg.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δm = m_water c_water (T_water − 273.15) / L_f to obtain 0.0981 kg (C).
