options.distractorRationale: Divides available thermal energy by the latent heat of vaporization (2.26 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹) instead of fusion.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes the mass of unmelted ice remaining at 273.15 K rather than the mass of ice that melts.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the dimensionless melted fraction Δm / m_ice instead of the melted mass Δm in kg.

items.stem: The Planck spectral curve shown corresponds to an exoplanet host star in radiative equilibrium of radiating area 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ m² and uniform blackbody temperature 1500 K, monitored by a radiometer 1.5 m away. Taking σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, what is the total electromagnetic power radiated?
items.workedSolution: By the Stefan–Boltzmann law for a blackbody (e = 1), P = σ A T⁴ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ × (1500)⁴ = 71.8 W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the blackbody radiation law in SI units to obtain 71.8 W (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses T² instead of T⁴ in the Stefan–Boltzmann law P = σ A T⁴.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses Celsius-shifted temperature (T − 273.15)⁴ instead of absolute kelvin temperature T⁴.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes surface exitance σ T⁴ (W m⁻²) and omits multiplication by surface area A.

items.stem: Inside an ion-propulsion xenon feed manifold of internal volume 0.024 m³, 1.2 mol of ideal Krypton-84 (Kr) gas (molar mass 83.8 g mol⁻¹) is maintained at 520 K. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what is the mass density of the gas?
items.workedSolution: Total gas mass m = nM = 1.2 × 0.0838 = 0.1006 kg. Density ρ = m / V = 0.1006 / 0.024 = 4.19 kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Applies ρ = nM / V in SI units to obtain 4.19 kg m⁻³ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies total gas mass nM by container volume V instead of dividing by V.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes molar concentration n / V (mol m⁻³) and omits multiplication by molar mass M.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Leaves molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of converting to kg mol⁻¹, overestimating density by a factor of 1000.

items.stem: The graph shows the Maxwell–Boltzmann molecular speed distribution for 0.8 mol of ideal Xenon-131 (Xe) gas (molar mass 131.3 g mol⁻¹) inside a laser-interferometer gas-cell enclosure of volume 0.015 m³ at 480 K. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²). What is the root-mean-square (rms) speed of the atoms?
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 480 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 480 / 0.1313) = 302 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 302 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: A sample of 0.2 mol of ideal gas in a closed noble-gas power-conversion loop undergoes an isobaric expansion from state A (1.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B (3.6 × 10⁻³ m³), followed by an isochoric rise to 2.56 × 10⁵ Pa at state C. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, find the absolute temperature at B.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates PV / (nR) at the target state to obtain 347 K (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Charles's law ratio, multiplying T_A by V_A / V_B instead of V_B / V_A.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Stops after computing the initial temperature T_A = P_A V_A / (nR) without scaling by V_B / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the final temperature T_C at state C rather than the intermediate temperature T_B.

items.stem: A monatomic ideal gas (1.5 mol) in a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder transitions from state A (2.4 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B (4.8 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³) and then to state C (4.8 × 10⁵ Pa, 8.1 × 10⁻³ m³). Defining expansion work done by the gas as positive, calculate the total thermal energy absorbed by the gas over A → B → C.
items.workedSolution: Along A → B → C, work done by the gas is W_by = 0 + P_B(V_C − V_B) = 1.728 × 10³ J. Total internal energy change ΔU = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A) = 4.212 × 10³ J. Hence Q = ΔU + W_by = 5.94 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 5.94 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the positive expansion work done by the gas instead of adding Q = ΔU + W_by.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the total internal energy change ΔU_AC and omits the boundary work done during B → C.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the monatomic 3/2 factor in ΔU = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A).

items.stem: A thermally isolated sample of 0.75 mol of monatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) in a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder transitions adiabatically from state A (1.2 × 10⁵ Pa, 5.6 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B of volume 1.6 × 10⁻³ m³. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, calculate the gas pressure at state B.
items.workedSolution: For a monatomic adiabatic process, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 1.2 × 10⁵ × (5.6 × 10⁻³ / 1.6 × 10⁻³)^(5/3) = 9.68 × 10⁵ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P V^(5/3) = const to obtain 9.68 × 10⁵ Pa (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the adiabatic exponent, using 3/5 instead of γ = 5/3.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats the process as isothermal (P_A V_A = P_B V_B) rather than adiabatic (P_A V_A^(5/3) = P_B V_B^(5/3)).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the diatomic adiabatic index γ = 7/5 instead of γ = 5/3 for a monatomic gas.

items.stem: Maintained in thermal contact with a 600 K bath, 1.2 mol of ideal gas in a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity expands quasi-statically from 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 6.75 × 10⁻³ m³. Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine ΔS = Q / T for the gas.
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.2 × 8.31 × ln(6.75 × 10⁻³ / 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 15.0 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 15.0 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 logarithm log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of the natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Replaces ln(V_B / V_A) with the linear fractional change (V_B − V_A) / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes isothermal heat Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) without dividing by T to obtain ΔS = Q / T.

items.stem: Inside a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals, 0.6 mol of an ideal monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) performs a closed three-step cycle A → B → C → A: reversible adiabatic expansion from state A (8.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to volume 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ at B, isobaric compression from B to volume 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at C, and isochoric heating from C back to A. Taking work done by the gas as positive, what is the net work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: At B, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 2.520 × 10⁵ Pa. Adiabatic work W_AB = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 666.1 J, and isobaric compression work W_BC = P_B(V_C − V_B) = -378.0 J (W_CA = 0). Thus W_net = W_AB + W_BC = 288 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 288 J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the magnitude of the isobaric compression work P_B(V_B − V_C).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the adiabatic expansion work W_AB and forgets to subtract the isobaric compression work |W_BC|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_CA along the isochoric leg instead of net work W_net.

items.stem: A 0.55 kg charge of ethanol starts at 131 K and finishes at 199 K inside a vacuum-jacketed phase-equilibrium test cell while an electrical immersion heater of input power 450 W and thermal transfer efficiency 0.8 supplies energy. Using fusion temperature 159 K, specific heats 1120 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ (solid) and 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ (liquid), and latent heat 1.08 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹, find the overall elapsed time.
items.workedSolution: Effective thermal power P_eff = η P = 0.8 × 450 = 360.0 W. Total energy Q_tot = m c_solid ΔT_s + m L_f + m c_liquid ΔT_l = 1.303 × 10⁵ J, giving t_total = Q_tot / P_eff = 362 s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_eff = η P and divides required thermal energy to obtain 362 s (D).

items.stem: In a calorimetry run using a stirred insulated immersion calorimeter, a 0.85 kg cylinder of brass (c = 380 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 410 K is quenched in 0.22 kg of mineral oil (c = 1960 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 298 K. During mixing, 950 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. Find T_eq at thermal equilibrium.
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l) + 950, giving T_eq = 344.7 K. Therefore T_eq = 345 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 345 K (B).

items.stem: The Planck spectral curve shown corresponds to a vacuum-chamber blackbody radiometer target of radiating area 6.2 × 10¹⁸ m² and uniform blackbody temperature 3600 K, monitored by a radiometer 8.5 × 10¹⁰ m away. Taking σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, what is the radiant intensity received at distance d (neglecting intervening absorption)?
items.workedSolution: Radiated luminosity L = σ A T⁴ = 5.905 × 10²⁵ W. Intensity at distance d is I = L / (4π d²) = 5.905 × 10²⁵ / (4π × (8.5 × 10¹⁰)²) = 650 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the blackbody radiation law in SI units to obtain 650 W m⁻² (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides radiated power by disc area π d² instead of spherical shell area 4π d².

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the geometric factor 4π for isotropic spherical spreading in I = L / (4π d²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides by 4π d instead of 4π d², omitting the inverse-square exponent.

items.stem: In a planetary energy-balance study, an instrumented rooftop longwave-emissivity test slab of area 2.5 m² and infrared emissivity e = 0.78 is at surface temperature 373 K beneath a radiative environment at 278 K. Taking σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, what is the gross thermal power radiated per unit area (surface exitance) by this greybody surface?
items.workedSolution: Gross radiated intensity (exitance) M = e σ T⁴ = 0.78 × 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × (373)⁴ = 856 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates e σ T⁴ to obtain 856 W m⁻² (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats the surface as an ideal blackbody (e = 1) and omits the emissivity factor e.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides blackbody exitance σ T⁴ by emissivity e instead of multiplying by e.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by surface area A, reporting total radiated power in watts rather than power per unit area.

items.stem: Within a rigid stainless-steel vacuum-calibration tank of volume 0.05 m³, 1.2 mol of monatomic Helium-4 (He) (M = 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹) is maintained at 290 K as represented by the speed distribution curve. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), find v_rms of the gas particles.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 290 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 290 / 4.0 × 10⁻³) = 1.34 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 1.34 × 10³ m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: Monatomic Neon-20 (Ne) gas (molar mass 0.0202 kg mol⁻¹) inside an orbital satellite attitude-control propellant cylinder has the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed distribution shown at 180 K. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Calculate the internal energy per mole of the gas.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic gas, molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T = 1.5 × 8.31 × 180 = 2.24 × 10³ J mol⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 180 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 2.24 × 10³ J mol⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Includes only one translational degree of freedom (1/2 R T) instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses molar enthalpy C_p T = (5/2) R T instead of molar internal energy (3/2) R T.

items.stem: A sample of 1.5 mol of an ideal monatomic gas in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber expands isobarically at constant pressure 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa from volume 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³ (state A) to 9.9 × 10⁻³ m³ (state B). Taking thermal energy supplied to the gas and work done by the gas as positive, how much thermal energy Q is supplied to the gas during A → B?
items.workedSolution: Work done by the gas W_by = P(V_B − V_A) = 3.0 × 10⁵ × (9.9 × 10⁻³ − 4.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.620 × 10³ J. For a monatomic ideal gas, ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV = 2.430 × 10³ J. By the first law, Q = ΔU + W_by = (5/2) P ΔV = 4.05 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 4.05 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the boundary work W = P ΔV done by the gas and ignores the increase in internal energy ΔU.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the internal energy change ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV and omits the expansion work P ΔV.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV, computing ΔU + W = P ΔV + P ΔV = 2 P ΔV instead of (5/2) P ΔV.

items.stem: A heat-engine test rig (a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell) drives 1.5 mol of ideal monatomic gas around a rectangular cycle with upper pressure 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa, lower pressure 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa, minimum volume 1.8 × 10⁻³ m³, and maximum volume 3.6 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking net work done by the gas as positive, what is the net mechanical work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Net work done by the gas equals the enclosed rectangular area: W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = (3.0 × 10⁵ − 1.0 × 10⁵)(3.6 × 10⁻³ − 1.8 × 10⁻³) = 360 J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes netWorkJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 360 J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Applies an extra factor of one-half from misremembering the degrees-of-freedom or geometric prefactor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the expansion work along A → B and forgets to subtract the compression work along C → D.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes P_B V_B − P_D V_D instead of the enclosed rectangular loop area (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min).

items.stem: Inside a cryocooler compression cylinder containing monatomic working gas, 0.3 mol of ideal gas is held at a constant temperature of 520 K while expanding reversibly from V_A = 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 0.01575 m³. Taking work done by the gas as positive and R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, how much work is done by the gas?
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 520 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.3 × 8.31 × 520 × ln(0.01575 / 3.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.95 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 1.95 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds U = (3/2)nRT to isothermal work, overlooking that ΔU = 0 at constant temperature.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as remaining constant at P_A, computing P_A(V_B − V_A) instead of ∫ P dV = nRT ln(V_B / V_A).

items.stem: In a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals, 0.75 mol of monatomic ideal gas executes a reversible Carnot heat-engine cycle between a hot reservoir at 277 °C and a cold sink at 67 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15), expanding isothermally at the hot reservoir from V_A = 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the theoretical thermal efficiency η of this Carnot cycle?
items.workedSolution: Convert to kelvin: T_H = 550.15 K, T_C = 340.15 K. Carnot efficiency η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 1 − 340.15 / 550.15 = 0.382.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 0.382 (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Applies an extra factor of one-half from misremembering the degrees-of-freedom or geometric prefactor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates T_C / T_H without subtracting from 1.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes Celsius temperatures directly into 1 − θ_C / θ_H instead of converting to absolute kelvin temperatures.

items.stem: A 0.15 kg specimen of pure ethanol inside a precision constant-flux heating chamber is heated from 129 K (solid) to 204 K (liquid). Take melting point = 159 K, c_solid = 1120 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, and specific latent heat of fusion L_f = 1.08 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹. Find the total heat transferred to the specimen.
items.workedSolution: Sensible heating: Q_sens = 0.15 × 1120 × (159 − 129) + 0.15 × 2440 × (204 − 159) = 2.151 × 10⁴ J. Latent heat on plateau: Q_lat = mL = 0.15 × 1.08 × 10⁵ = 1.620 × 10⁴ J. Total Q = 3.77 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Sums sensible mcΔT stages and latent heat mL to obtain 3.77 × 10⁴ J (C).

items.stem: The temperature–time curve shows 1.1 kg of lead inside a solar-salt thermal-storage prototype module (heated between 583 K and 661 K; T_m = 600.6 K, c_solid = 128 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 147 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, L_f = 2.3 × 10⁴ J kg⁻¹) while an electrical immersion heater of input power 900 W and thermal transfer efficiency 0.75 supplies energy. Calculate the duration Δt of the horizontal phase-change plateau.
items.workedSolution: Effective thermal power P_eff = η P = 0.75 × 900 = 675.0 W. Plateau latent energy Q_f = m L_f = 2.530 × 10⁴ J, giving Δt_plateau = Q_f / P_eff = 37.5 s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_eff = η P and divides required thermal energy to obtain 37.5 s (C).

items.stem: Excess crushed ice (0.42 kg at 273.15 K; specific latent heat of fusion 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹) is tipped into 0.34 kg of tepid water at 301.15 K (specific heat 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) inside a calibrated heat-transfer bench vessel. Calculate the mass of ice converted into liquid water.
items.workedSolution: Maximum heat released by water cooling to 273.15 K is Q = 0.34 × 4180 × (301.15 − 273.15) = 3.979 × 10⁴ J, which is less than m_ice L_f = 1.403 × 10⁵ J. Mass melted Δm = Q / L_f = 0.119 kg.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δm = m_water c_water (T_water − 273.15) / L_f to obtain 0.119 kg (B).

items.stem: In a climate radiative-transfer model, a geostationary satellite nadir heat-rejection louver of area 2.5 m² and surface emissivity e = 0.78 is at 313 K while exchanging thermal infrared radiation with an effective surrounding environment at 255 K. Taking σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, what is the net rate of radiative energy loss P_net from the surface?
items.workedSolution: Net radiative power loss P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) = 0.78 × 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × 2.5 × ((313)⁴ − (255)⁴) = 594 W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) to obtain 594 W (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates e σ A (T − T_amb)⁴ instead of e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴), a classic fourth-power algebra error.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the greybody emissivity factor e (< 1) from P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates gross emitted power e σ A T⁴ and ignores incoming radiation absorbed from the surroundings at T_amb.

items.stem: In an atmospheric research dropsonde reference chamber of volume 0.012 m³, 0.35 mol of Helium-4 (He) (molar mass 4 g mol⁻¹) is held in thermal equilibrium at 420 K. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what pressure does the gas exert on the walls?
items.workedSolution: From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (0.35 × 8.31 × 420) / 0.012 = 1.02 × 10⁵ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 1.02 × 10⁵ Pa (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies nRT by volume V instead of dividing nRT by V.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts 273.15 from an already-kelvin temperature before applying pV = nRT.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the amount of substance n in p = nRT / V, solving for 1 mol instead of the given molar amount.

items.stem: Spectroscopic thermometry confirms that Argon-40 (Ar) atoms (molar mass 0.04 kg mol⁻¹) in a cryogenic buffer reservoir in a superconducting magnet rig are equilibrated at 137 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Use Boltzmann constant 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and elementary charge 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. Find the average translational kinetic energy of a single atom in eV.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 410.15 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 0.0531 eV (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates (1/2) k_B T / e for a single degree of freedom instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Applies an extra factor of one-half from misremembering the degrees-of-freedom or geometric prefactor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes k_B T / e and omits the 3/2 translational factor.

items.stem: The volume–temperature (V–T) diagram traces 0.5 mol of ideal gas inside a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder. Starting at A (2.2 × 10⁵ Pa, 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³), the gas expands at constant pressure to volume 0.0132 m³ at state B and is then heated at constant volume to 5.28 × 10⁵ Pa at state C (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). Calculate T_B.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates PV / (nR) at the target state to obtain 699 K (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Charles's law ratio, multiplying T_A by V_A / V_B instead of V_B / V_A.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Stops after computing the initial temperature T_A = P_A V_A / (nR) without scaling by V_B / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the final temperature T_C at state C rather than the intermediate temperature T_B.

items.stem: The diagram shows a closed four-leg cycle A → B → C → D → A for 0.4 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder, bounded by P_low = 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa, P_high = 5.4 × 10⁵ Pa, V_min = 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³, and V_max = 7.5 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the total thermal energy Q_in absorbed by the monatomic gas during the heating legs D → A and A → B?
items.workedSolution: Heat enters on D → A (isochoric, W = 0): Q_DA = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min = 1.620 × 10³ J, and on A → B (isobaric): Q_AB = (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 6.075 × 10³ J. Total Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = 7.70 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes heatInputJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 7.70 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Confuses net cycle heat Q_net = W_net with total heat input Q_in absorbed from the hot source.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Applies an extra factor of one-half from misremembering the degrees-of-freedom or geometric prefactor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Includes only the heat absorbed during isobaric expansion A → B and omits the isochoric heating D → A.

items.stem: The P–V diagram shows a rapid thermally insulated (adiabatic) expansion A → B of 1.5 mol of monatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) in a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity from (6.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³) to final volume 7.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). Determine the final pressure P_B.
items.workedSolution: For a monatomic adiabatic process, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 6.0 × 10⁵ × (2.0 × 10⁻³ / 7.0 × 10⁻³)^(5/3) = 7.44 × 10⁴ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P V^(5/3) = const to obtain 7.44 × 10⁴ Pa (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses the diatomic adiabatic index γ = 7/5 instead of γ = 5/3 for a monatomic gas.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats the process as isothermal (P_A V_A = P_B V_B) rather than adiabatic (P_A V_A^(5/3) = P_B V_B^(5/3)).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the adiabatic exponent, using 3/5 instead of γ = 5/3.

items.stem: A Carnot engine modelled in an insulated aerospace gas-accumulator cylinder uses 1.4 mol of ideal gas operating between a hot reservoir at 770 K and a cold sink at 350 K. During the high-temperature isothermal stage A → B, the volume increases from 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking net work done by the gas as positive (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹), what is the net work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) = 6.209 × 10³ J and η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 0.5455. Net work output W_net = η Q_H = nR(T_H − T_C) ln(V_B / V_A) = 3.39 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 3.39 × 10³ J (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the rejected heat Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) instead of net work Q_H − Q_C.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) without multiplying by Carnot efficiency (1 − T_C / T_H).

items.stem: Inside a closed noble-gas power-conversion loop, 0.4 mol of an ideal monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) performs a closed three-step cycle A → B → C → A: reversible adiabatic expansion from state A (6.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to volume 7.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at B, isobaric compression from B to volume 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at C, and isochoric heating from C back to A. Taking work done by the gas as positive, what is the net work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: At B, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 1.042 × 10⁵ Pa. Adiabatic work W_AB = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 1.266 × 10³ J, and isobaric compression work W_BC = P_B(V_C − V_B) = -520.8 J (W_CA = 0). Thus W_net = W_AB + W_BC = 745 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 745 J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the magnitude of the isobaric compression work P_B(V_B − V_C).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the adiabatic expansion work W_AB and forgets to subtract the isobaric compression work |W_BC|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_CA along the isochoric leg instead of net work W_net.

items.stem: During a timed run in a ceramic-lined materials characterization furnace, an electrical immersion heater of input power 1200 W and thermal transfer efficiency 0.85 supplies energy on 0.2 kg of lead between 563 K and 661 K. Given melting point 600.6 K, L_f = 2.3 × 10⁴ J kg⁻¹, c_s = 128 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, and c_l = 147 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine the constant-temperature arrest time.
items.workedSolution: Effective thermal power P_eff = η P = 0.85 × 1200 = 1.020 × 10³ W. Plateau latent energy Q_f = m L_f = 4.600 × 10³ J, giving Δt_plateau = Q_f / P_eff = 4.51 s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_eff = η P and divides required thermal energy to obtain 4.51 s (C).

items.stem: Inside a vacuum-insulated stainless-steel Dewar flask, 0.72 kg of ethanol (specific heat capacity 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 285 K receives a 0.48 kg copper specimen (c = 385 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 380 K. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. Calculate the equilibrium temperature of the mixture.
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l), giving T_eq = 294.0 K. Therefore T_eq = 294 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 294 K (B).

items.stem: Radiometric observations characterise a tungsten-halide national standards cavity radiator (ideal blackbody, area 2.8 × 10¹⁹ m², surface temperature 8800 K) from a separation d = 4.2 × 10¹¹ m. Taking σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, what is the total electromagnetic power radiated?
items.workedSolution: By the Stefan–Boltzmann law for a blackbody (e = 1), P = σ A T⁴ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × 2.8 × 10¹⁹ × (8800)⁴ = 9.52 × 10²⁷ W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the blackbody radiation law in SI units to obtain 9.52 × 10²⁷ W (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes surface exitance σ T⁴ (W m⁻²) and omits multiplication by surface area A.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses T² instead of T⁴ in the Stefan–Boltzmann law P = σ A T⁴.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses Celsius-shifted temperature (T − 273.15)⁴ instead of absolute kelvin temperature T⁴.

items.stem: An energy-budget sensor monitors a lunar mare regolith radiometry quadrat (area 6.5 m², greybody emissivity 0.95) maintained at 373 K within a radiative environment at 278 K. Using σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, calculate P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴).
items.workedSolution: Net radiative power loss P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) = 0.95 × 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × 6.5 × ((373)⁴ − (278)⁴) = 4.69 × 10³ W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) to obtain 4.69 × 10³ W (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates e σ A (T − T_amb)⁴ instead of e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴), a classic fourth-power algebra error.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the greybody emissivity factor e (< 1) from P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates gross emitted power e σ A T⁴ and ignores incoming radiation absorbed from the surroundings at T_amb.

items.stem: At 290 K, 0.8 mol of Argon-40 (Ar) with molar mass 0.04 kg mol⁻¹ fills an orbital satellite attitude-control propellant cylinder (capacity 0.05 m³). Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), calculate the root-mean-square speed marked v_rms on the distribution.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.04 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 290 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 290 / 0.04) = 425 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 425 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: 0.2 mol of ideal gas inside a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell follows path A → B → C on the volume–temperature (V–T) plot: an isobaric expansion from (2.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³) to V_B = 9.0 × 10⁻³ m³, then an isochoric pressure increase to P_C = 5.2 × 10⁵ Pa. Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine T_C.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates PV / (nR) at the target state to obtain 2.82 × 10³ K (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes T_B after the isobaric stage and omits the isochoric pressure ratio P_C / P_A.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses the initial volume V_A instead of V_B = V_C when evaluating T_C = P_C V_C / (nR).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Reports the final temperature converted to °C when the question and options specify kelvin.

items.stem: A monatomic ideal gas (1.2 mol) in a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell transitions from state A (1.2 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B (2.4 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³) and then to state C (2.4 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³). Defining expansion work done by the gas as positive, calculate the total thermal energy absorbed by the gas over A → B → C.
items.workedSolution: Along A → B → C, work done by the gas is W_by = 0 + P_B(V_C − V_B) = 480.0 J. Total internal energy change ΔU = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A) = 1.170 × 10³ J. Hence Q = ΔU + W_by = 1.65 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 1.65 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the positive expansion work done by the gas instead of adding Q = ΔU + W_by.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the total internal energy change ΔU_AC and omits the boundary work done during B → C.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the monatomic 3/2 factor in ΔU = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A).

items.stem: A thermally isolated sample of 0.4 mol of monatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) in a cryocooler compression cylinder containing monatomic working gas transitions adiabatically from state A (1.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 8.0 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B of volume 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, Taking work done on the gas as positive, how much mechanical work is done on the gas during A → B?
items.workedSolution: First find P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 1.008 × 10⁶ Pa. Since Q = 0 in an adiabatic process, W_on = +ΔU = (3/2)(P_B V_B − P_A V_A) = 1.82 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P V^(5/3) = const and Q = 0 to obtain 1.82 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as constant at P_A, computing P_A |V_B − V_A| instead of adiabatic work.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses the isothermal work formula P_A V_A |ln(V_B / V_A)| instead of adiabatic work.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in |ΔU| = (3/2)|P_B V_B − P_A V_A| when applying Q = 0 => |W| = |ΔU|.

items.stem: On the P–V diagram, 2.2 mol of an ideal gas in an insulated aerospace gas-accumulator cylinder undergoes a reversible isothermal expansion at 600 K from 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 0.01575 m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and expansion work by the gas as positive. Find W_AB.
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 600 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 2.2 × 8.31 × 600 × ln(0.01575 / 3.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.65 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 1.65 × 10⁴ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds U = (3/2)nRT to isothermal work, overlooking that ΔU = 0 at constant temperature.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as remaining constant at P_A, computing P_A(V_B − V_A) instead of ∫ P dV = nRT ln(V_B / V_A).

items.stem: Starting at state A (1.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³), 0.6 mol of monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) in a variable-volume optical pressure cell is compressed adiabatically to 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³, heated at constant volume to 2.218 × 10⁶ Pa, expanded adiabatically to 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³, and cooled at constant volume back to A. Find η.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic Otto cycle (γ = 5/3), η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1) = 1 − (1.2 × 10⁻³ / 4.8 × 10⁻³)^(2/3) = 0.603 (equivalently W_net / Q_in = 1.313 × 10³ / 2.177 × 10³ = 0.603).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 0.603 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses exponent 1 instead of γ − 1 = 2/3 in the Otto efficiency relation η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes Carnot efficiency 1 − T_A / T_C between extreme cycle temperatures instead of Otto efficiency.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Raises V_min / V_max to γ = 5/3 rather than γ − 1 = 2/3.

items.stem: A 0.65 kg specimen of pure aluminium inside a vacuum-jacketed phase-equilibrium test cell is heated from 914 K (solid) to 979 K (liquid). Take melting point = 933.5 K, c_solid = 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 1180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, and specific latent heat of fusion L_f = 3.97 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹. Find the total heat transferred to the specimen.

markScheme.criterion: Sums sensible mcΔT stages and latent heat mL to obtain 3.04 × 10⁵ J (D).

items.stem: In a calorimetry run using a closed-lid magnetic-stirrer calorimetry pot, a 0.48 kg cylinder of aluminium (c = 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 380 K is quenched in 0.72 kg of mineral oil (c = 1960 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 298 K. During mixing, 1250 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. What thermal energy does the cylinder give up?
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l) + 1250, giving T_eq = 316.5 K. Heat released by the solid Q_lost = m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = 2.74 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 2.74 × 10⁴ J (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the final equilibrium temperature is the unweighted midpoint (T_solid + T_liquid) / 2.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the heat gained by the liquid bath without adding the heat lost to the surroundings.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the solid cools all the way down to the initial bath temperature T_liquid instead of T_eq.

items.stem: In a double-walled vacuum Dewar mixing vessel, 0.24 kg of water cools from 297.15 K down to 273.15 K against 0.36 kg of melting ice initially at 273.15 K (c = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹; fusion enthalpy 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹). Find the melted ice mass.
items.workedSolution: Maximum heat released by water cooling to 273.15 K is Q = 0.24 × 4180 × (297.15 − 273.15) = 2.408 × 10⁴ J, which is less than m_ice L_f = 1.202 × 10⁵ J. Mass melted Δm = Q / L_f = 0.0721 kg.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δm = m_water c_water (T_water − 273.15) / L_f to obtain 0.0721 kg (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides available thermal energy by the latent heat of vaporization (2.26 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹) instead of fusion.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the dimensionless melted fraction Δm / m_ice instead of the melted mass Δm in kg.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the mass of unmelted ice remaining at 273.15 K rather than the mass of ice that melts.

items.stem: Telemetry from a sub-arctic tundra permafrost flux-tower footprint (area 2.5 m², emissivity 0.72) records a surface temperature of 282 K in surroundings at 240 K (σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴). Calculate the gross emitted intensity e σ T⁴ from the surface.
items.workedSolution: Gross radiated intensity (exitance) M = e σ T⁴ = 0.72 × 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × (282)⁴ = 258 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates e σ T⁴ to obtain 258 W m⁻² (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats the surface as an ideal blackbody (e = 1) and omits the emissivity factor e.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides blackbody exitance σ T⁴ by emissivity e instead of multiplying by e.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by surface area A, reporting total radiated power in watts rather than power per unit area.

items.stem: During an instrument check, a rigid stainless-steel vacuum-calibration tank of internal volume 0.045 m³ contains 2.8 mol of Argon-40 (Ar) (molar mass 0.04 kg mol⁻¹) at 310 K (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is the pressure inside the chamber?
items.workedSolution: From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (2.8 × 8.31 × 310) / 0.045 = 1.60 × 10⁵ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 1.60 × 10⁵ Pa (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies nRT by volume V instead of dividing nRT by V.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts 273.15 from an already-kelvin temperature before applying pV = nRT.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the amount of substance n in p = nRT / V, solving for 1 mol instead of the given molar amount.

items.stem: Inside a high-vacuum synchrotron beamline gas target, an ideal monatomic sample of Xenon-131 (Xe) (M = 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹) is in thermal equilibrium at 370 K. Use Boltzmann constant 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and elementary charge 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. Find the average translational kinetic energy of a single atom in eV.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 370 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 0.0479 eV (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates (1/2) k_B T / e for a single degree of freedom instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes k_B T / e and omits the 3/2 translational factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the 3/2 factor to 3 k_B T / e by omitting the 1/2 in kinetic energy.

items.stem: 0.75 mol of ideal gas inside an insulated aerospace gas-accumulator cylinder follows path A → B → C on the volume–temperature (V–T) plot: an isobaric expansion from (2.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³) to V_B = 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³, then an isochoric pressure increase to P_C = 6.24 × 10⁵ Pa. Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine T_C.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates PV / (nR) at the target state to obtain 601 K (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes T_B after the isobaric stage and omits the isochoric pressure ratio P_C / P_A.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Reports the final temperature converted to °C when the question and options specify kelvin.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the initial volume V_A instead of V_B = V_C when evaluating T_C = P_C V_C / (nR).

items.stem: Operating clockwise between 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³ and 8.0 × 10⁻³ m³ and between 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa and 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 0.2 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber completes cycle A → B → C → D → A. What is the total thermal energy Q_in absorbed by the monatomic gas during the heating legs D → A and A → B?
items.workedSolution: Heat enters on D → A (isochoric, W = 0): Q_DA = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min = 1.200 × 10³ J, and on A → B (isobaric): Q_AB = (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 3.000 × 10³ J. Total Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = 4.20 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes heatInputJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 4.20 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Confuses net cycle heat Q_net = W_net with total heat input Q_in absorbed from the hot source.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Includes only the heat absorbed during isobaric expansion A → B and omits the isochoric heating D → A.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic ΔU on both heating legs.

items.stem: In a closed noble-gas power-conversion loop coupled to a thermal reservoir at 450 K, 0.3 mol of an ideal gas expands reversibly and isothermally from V_A = 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 0.01225 m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the change in entropy ΔS of the gas?
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.3 × 8.31 × ln(0.01225 / 3.5 × 10⁻³) = 3.12 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 3.12 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 logarithm log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of the natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Replaces ln(V_B / V_A) with the linear fractional change (V_B − V_A) / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes isothermal heat Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) without dividing by T to obtain ΔS = Q / T.

items.stem: In a variable-volume optical pressure cell, 1.4 mol of monatomic ideal gas executes a reversible Carnot heat-engine cycle between a hot reservoir at 725 K and a cold sink at 290 K, expanding isothermally at the hot reservoir from V_A = 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the theoretical thermal efficiency η of this Carnot cycle?
items.workedSolution: Carnot efficiency η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 1 − 290 / 725 = 0.600.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 0.600 (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates T_C / T_H without subtracting from 1.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the isothermal volume ratio 1 − V_A / V_B instead of the reservoir temperature ratio 1 − T_C / T_H.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides ΔT by T_C instead of T_H when computing efficiency.

items.stem: The phase-change graph plots temperature against thermal energy transferred for 0.85 kg of water in a solar-salt thermal-storage prototype module warmed from 223 K to 318 K across its melting point at 273.15 K (c_solid = 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, specific latent heat of fusion L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹). Calculate the total thermal energy required.

markScheme.criterion: Sums sensible mcΔT stages and latent heat mL to obtain 5.33 × 10⁵ J (C).

items.stem: A 0.3 kg charge of ethanol starts at 121 K and finishes at 219 K inside a lagged laboratory phase-transition calorimeter while an electrical immersion heater of input power 320 W and thermal transfer efficiency 0.75 supplies energy. Using fusion temperature 159 K, specific heats 1120 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ (solid) and 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ (liquid), and latent heat 1.08 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹, find the overall elapsed time.
items.workedSolution: Effective thermal power P_eff = η P = 0.75 × 320 = 240.0 W. Total energy Q_tot = m c_solid ΔT_s + m L_f + m c_liquid ΔT_l = 8.909 × 10⁴ J, giving t_total = Q_tot / P_eff = 371 s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_eff = η P and divides required thermal energy to obtain 371 s (D).

items.stem: When 0.68 kg of warm water at 338.15 K in an expanded-polystyrene adiabatic quenching bath receives 0.035 kg of cold ice at 268.15 K, the ice warms to 273.15 K, melts completely (L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹), and mixes adiabatically. Using 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ for solid ice and 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ for liquid water, find the final temperature.
items.workedSolution: Energy to warm and melt all ice at 273.15 K: Q_1+2 = 0.035 × 2100 × (273.15 − 268.15) + 0.035 × 3.34 × 10⁵ = 1.206 × 10⁴ J. Energy balance with warm water: m_w c_w (338.15 − T_eq) = Q_1+2 + m_ice c_w (T_eq − 273.15), giving T_eq = 331 K.

markScheme.criterion: Includes sub-zero ice warming, fusion latent heat, and meltwater warming to obtain 331 K (B).

items.stem: Radiometric observations characterise a spherical main-sequence stellar photosphere (ideal blackbody, area 3.6 × 10¹⁸ m², surface temperature 3600 K) from a separation d = 8.5 × 10¹⁰ m. Taking Wien's constant b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K, what is the peak emission wavelength λ_max in nanometres?
items.workedSolution: By Wien's displacement law, λ_max = b / T = (2.90 × 10⁻³) / 3600 = 8.056 × 10⁻⁷ m = 806 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the blackbody radiation law in SI units to obtain 806 nm (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Wien's displacement law by dividing T by b instead of b by T.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts 273.15 from the kelvin temperature before applying Wien's law.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies Wien's constant b by T instead of dividing b by T.

items.stem: 1.6 mol of monatomic Krypton-84 (Kr) (molar mass 83.8 g mol⁻¹) fills a sealed quartz spectroscopy cell of volume 8.0 × 10⁻³ m³ at a steady temperature of 117 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Find the gas pressure.
items.workedSolution: Convert temperature to kelvin: T = 117 + 273.15 = 390.15 K. From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (1.6 × 8.31 × 390.15) / 8.0 × 10⁻³ = 6.48 × 10⁵ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 6.48 × 10⁵ Pa (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies nRT by volume V instead of dividing nRT by V.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes Celsius temperature θ directly into pV = nRT without converting to absolute temperature in kelvin.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the amount of substance n in p = nRT / V, solving for 1 mol instead of the given molar amount.

items.stem: In a semiconductor lithography purge canister (volume 0.025 m³), 0.3 mol of monatomic Xenon-131 (Xe) of molar mass 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹ is warmed from T₁ = 360 K to T₂ = 810 K, shifting the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed curve as plotted. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), determine v_rms at the higher temperature T₂.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 810 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 810 / 0.1313) = 392 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 392 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: 0.2 mol of ideal gas inside a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell follows path A → B → C on the volume–temperature (V–T) plot: an isobaric expansion from (2.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³) to V_B = 8.8 × 10⁻³ m³, then an isochoric pressure increase to P_C = 3.64 × 10⁵ Pa. Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine T_C.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates PV / (nR) at the target state to obtain 1.93 × 10³ K (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses the initial volume V_A instead of V_B = V_C when evaluating T_C = P_C V_C / (nR).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes T_B after the isobaric stage and omits the isochoric pressure ratio P_C / P_A.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Reports the final temperature converted to °C when the question and options specify kelvin.

items.stem: The P–V graph shows an isobaric compression of 1.2 mol of ideal monatomic gas inside a precision pneumatic actuator chamber sealed with a movable piston at 4.5 × 10⁵ Pa from V_A = 5.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³. Using the sign convention where work done on the gas is positive, determine the compression work done on the gas.
items.workedSolution: During isobaric compression from 5.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at 4.5 × 10⁵ Pa, work done on the gas W_on = −P(V_B − V_A) = 4.5 × 10⁵ × (5.5 × 10⁻³ − 2.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.35 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 1.35 × 10³ J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the magnitude of internal energy change |ΔU| = (3/2) P |ΔV| instead of boundary work P |ΔV|.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies pressure by initial volume V_A instead of the volume change |V_B − V_A|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the total heat rejected |Q| = (5/2) P |ΔV| rather than the mechanical work done on the gas.

items.stem: The P–V diagram shows a rapid thermally insulated (adiabatic) expansion A → B of 0.25 mol of monatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) in an insulated aerospace gas-accumulator cylinder from (4.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.6 × 10⁻³ m³) to final volume 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). Taking work done by the gas as positive, how much mechanical work is done by the gas during A → B?
items.workedSolution: First find P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 6.410 × 10⁴ Pa. Since Q = 0 in an adiabatic process, W_by = −ΔU = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 498 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P V^(5/3) = const and Q = 0 to obtain 498 J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in |ΔU| = (3/2)|P_B V_B − P_A V_A| when applying Q = 0 => |W| = |ΔU|.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the isothermal work formula P_A V_A |ln(V_B / V_A)| instead of adiabatic work.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as constant at P_A, computing P_A |V_B − V_A| instead of adiabatic work.

items.stem: Maintained in thermal contact with a 400 K bath, 0.3 mol of ideal gas in a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity expands quasi-statically from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine ΔS = Q / T for the gas.
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.3 × 8.31 × ln(4.0 × 10⁻³ / 2.0 × 10⁻³) = 1.73 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 1.73 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 logarithm log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of the natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Replaces ln(V_B / V_A) with the linear fractional change (V_B − V_A) / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes isothermal heat Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) without dividing by T to obtain ΔS = Q / T.

items.stem: Starting at state A (1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³), 0.25 mol of monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber is compressed adiabatically to 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³, heated at constant volume to 1.685 × 10⁶ Pa, expanded adiabatically to 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³, and cooled at constant volume back to A. Find η.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic Otto cycle (γ = 5/3), η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1) = 1 − (2.0 × 10⁻³ / 6.0 × 10⁻³)^(2/3) = 0.519 (equivalently W_net / Q_in = 1.167 × 10³ / 2.247 × 10³ = 0.519).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 0.519 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses exponent 1 instead of γ − 1 = 2/3 in the Otto efficiency relation η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes Carnot efficiency 1 − T_A / T_C between extreme cycle temperatures instead of Otto efficiency.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Raises V_min / V_max to γ = 5/3 rather than γ − 1 = 2/3.

items.stem: During a timed run in a metallurgical vacuum-induction melting pot, a Peltier extraction module rated at 600 W with coupling efficiency 0.9 removes thermal energy on 0.55 kg of water between 333 K and 255 K. Given melting point 273.15 K, L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹, c_s = 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, and c_l = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine the constant-temperature arrest time.
items.workedSolution: Effective thermal power P_eff = η P = 0.9 × 600 = 540.0 W. Plateau latent energy Q_f = m L_f = 1.837 × 10⁵ J, giving Δt_plateau = Q_f / P_eff = 340 s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_eff = η P and divides required thermal energy to obtain 340 s (C).

items.stem: Inside a calibrated heat-transfer bench vessel, 0.32 kg of ethanol (specific heat capacity 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 290 K receives a 0.36 kg brass specimen (c = 380 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 510 K. During mixing, 650 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. Calculate the equilibrium temperature of the mixture.
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l) + 650, giving T_eq = 322.1 K. Therefore T_eq = 322 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 322 K (B).

items.stem: Operating at 1800 K with effective blackbody emissivity 1 and area 3.2 × 10⁻³ m², an isothermal silicon-carbide calibration cavity irradiates a sensor located 3.5 m away in vacuum. Taking σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, what is the total electromagnetic power radiated?
items.workedSolution: By the Stefan–Boltzmann law for a blackbody (e = 1), P = σ A T⁴ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × 3.2 × 10⁻³ × (1800)⁴ = 1.90 × 10³ W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the blackbody radiation law in SI units to obtain 1.90 × 10³ W (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses T² instead of T⁴ in the Stefan–Boltzmann law P = σ A T⁴.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses Celsius-shifted temperature (T − 273.15)⁴ instead of absolute kelvin temperature T⁴.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes surface exitance σ T⁴ (W m⁻²) and omits multiplication by surface area A.

items.stem: An energy-budget sensor monitors a coastal upwelling sea-surface calibration zone (area 4 m², greybody emissivity 0.64) maintained at 310 K within a radiative environment at 268 K. Using σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, calculate P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴).
items.workedSolution: Net radiative power loss P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) = 0.64 × 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × 4 × ((310)⁴ − (268)⁴) = 592 W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) to obtain 592 W (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates e σ A (T − T_amb)⁴ instead of e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴), a classic fourth-power algebra error.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the greybody emissivity factor e (< 1) from P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates gross emitted power e σ A T⁴ and ignores incoming radiation absorbed from the surroundings at T_amb.

items.stem: An experiment records the molecular speed distribution of 0.5 mol of Helium-4 (He) gas (molar mass 4 g mol⁻¹) occupying 0.025 m³ in a high-vacuum synchrotron beamline gas target at 360 K (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²)). Which value equals the rms speed of the atoms?
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 360 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 360 / 4.0 × 10⁻³) = 1.50 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 1.50 × 10³ m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: Monatomic Neon-20 (Ne) gas (molar mass 0.0202 kg mol⁻¹) inside a thermostatted noble-gas reference bulb has the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed distribution shown at 310 K. Use Boltzmann constant 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and elementary charge 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the mean translational kinetic energy per atom in electronvolts?

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 310 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 0.0401 eV (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates (1/2) k_B T / e for a single degree of freedom instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes k_B T / e and omits the 3/2 translational factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the 3/2 factor to 3 k_B T / e by omitting the 1/2 in kinetic energy.

items.stem: A monatomic ideal gas (1.5 mol) in a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity transitions from state A (1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B (3.75 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³) and then to state C (3.75 × 10⁵ Pa, 0.0144 m³). Defining expansion work done by the gas as positive, calculate the total thermal energy absorbed by the gas over A → B → C.
items.workedSolution: Along A → B → C, work done by the gas is W_by = 0 + P_B(V_C − V_B) = 3.712 × 10³ J. Total internal energy change ΔU = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A) = 7.088 × 10³ J. Hence Q = ΔU + W_by = 1.08 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 1.08 × 10⁴ J (D).

options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the positive expansion work done by the gas instead of adding Q = ΔU + W_by.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the total internal energy change ΔU_AC and omits the boundary work done during B → C.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the monatomic 3/2 factor in ΔU = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A).

items.stem: A heat-engine test rig (a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell) drives 0.8 mol of ideal monatomic gas around a rectangular cycle with upper pressure 6.3 × 10⁵ Pa, lower pressure 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa, minimum volume 2.4 × 10⁻³ m³, and maximum volume 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking net work done by the gas as positive, what is the net mechanical work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Net work done by the gas equals the enclosed rectangular area: W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = (6.3 × 10⁵ − 1.8 × 10⁵)(6.0 × 10⁻³ − 2.4 × 10⁻³) = 1.62 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes netWorkJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 1.62 × 10³ J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the expansion work along A → B and forgets to subtract the compression work along C → D.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies the enclosed loop area by an extraneous 3/2 internal-energy factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes P_B V_B − P_D V_D instead of the enclosed rectangular loop area (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min).

items.stem: Maintained in thermal contact with a 450 K bath, 0.6 mol of ideal gas in a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder expands quasi-statically from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 9.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine ΔS = Q / T for the gas.
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.6 × 8.31 × ln(9.0 × 10⁻³ / 2.0 × 10⁻³) = 7.50 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 7.50 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 logarithm log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of the natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Replaces ln(V_B / V_A) with the linear fractional change (V_B − V_A) / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes isothermal heat Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) without dividing by T to obtain ΔS = Q / T.

items.stem: The diagram shows a reversible Carnot cycle A → B → C → D → A for 1.4 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber coupled to a hot reservoir at 608 K and a cold sink at 380 K, with isothermal expansion from 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 8.75 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what magnitude of thermal energy Q_C is rejected to the cold sink per cycle?
items.workedSolution: During isothermal compression C → D at T_C = 380 K, V_C / V_D = V_B / V_A, so heat rejected to the cold sink is Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) = 5.54 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 5.54 × 10³ J (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A) in Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes net work W_net = Q_H − Q_C instead of the rejected heat Q_C.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the heat absorbed Q_H from the hot reservoir instead of the heat Q_C rejected to the cold sink.

markScheme.criterion: Sums sensible mcΔT stages and latent heat mL to obtain 8.45 × 10³ J (D).

items.stem: The temperature–time curve shows 0.3 kg of aluminium inside a thermal-energy-storage phase-change capsule (heated between 906 K and 959 K; T_m = 933.5 K, c_solid = 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 1180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, L_f = 3.97 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹) while an electrical immersion heater of input power 1600 W and thermal transfer efficiency 0.8 supplies energy. Calculate the total duration of the process.
items.workedSolution: Effective thermal power P_eff = η P = 0.8 × 1600 = 1.280 × 10³ W. Total energy Q_tot = m c_solid ΔT_s + m L_f + m c_liquid ΔT_l = 1.356 × 10⁵ J, giving t_total = Q_tot / P_eff = 106 s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_eff = η P and divides required thermal energy to obtain 106 s (D).

items.stem: Sub-freezing ice (0.045 kg at 263.15 K; c_ice = 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) is stirred into 0.48 kg of water (348.15 K; c_water = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) inside a lagged benchtop thermal-equilibrium chamber. Given T_m = 273.15 K and L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹, determine the steady final temperature once melting finishes.
items.workedSolution: Energy to warm and melt all ice at 273.15 K: Q_1+2 = 0.045 × 2100 × (273.15 − 263.15) + 0.045 × 3.34 × 10⁵ = 1.598 × 10⁴ J. Energy balance with warm water: m_w c_w (348.15 − T_eq) = Q_1+2 + m_ice c_w (T_eq − 273.15), giving T_eq = 334 K.

markScheme.criterion: Includes sub-zero ice warming, fusion latent heat, and meltwater warming to obtain 334 K (B).

items.stem: In a planetary energy-balance study, a horizontal basaltic planetary regolith tile of area 4 m² and infrared emissivity e = 0.84 is at surface temperature 343 K beneath a radiative environment at 268 K. Taking σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, what is the gross thermal power radiated per unit area (surface exitance) by this greybody surface?
items.workedSolution: Gross radiated intensity (exitance) M = e σ T⁴ = 0.84 × 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × (343)⁴ = 659 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates e σ T⁴ to obtain 659 W m⁻² (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats the surface as an ideal blackbody (e = 1) and omits the emissivity factor e.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides blackbody exitance σ T⁴ by emissivity e instead of multiplying by e.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies by surface area A, reporting total radiated power in watts rather than power per unit area.

items.stem: In a cryogenic buffer reservoir in a superconducting magnet rig of volume 0.016 m³, 0.15 mol of Helium-4 (He) (molar mass 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹) is held in thermal equilibrium at 27 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what pressure does the gas exert on the walls?
items.workedSolution: Convert temperature to kelvin: T = 27 + 273.15 = 300.15 K. From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (0.15 × 8.31 × 300.15) / 0.016 = 2.34 × 10⁴ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 2.34 × 10⁴ Pa (C).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes Celsius temperature θ directly into pV = nRT without converting to absolute temperature in kelvin.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the amount of substance n in p = nRT / V, solving for 1 mol instead of the given molar amount.

items.stem: A low-density plasma-free Argon-40 (Ar) sample (M = 0.04 kg mol⁻¹) is held in an ion-propulsion xenon feed manifold at 820 K. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, What is the molar internal energy of this ideal monatomic gas?
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic gas, molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T = 1.5 × 8.31 × 820 = 1.02 × 10⁴ J mol⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 820 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 1.02 × 10⁴ J mol⁻¹ (C).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses molar enthalpy C_p T = (5/2) R T instead of molar internal energy (3/2) R T.

items.stem: On the pressure–temperature (P–T) diagram, 0.35 mol of an ideal gas in a precision pneumatic actuator chamber sealed with a movable piston starts at state A (2.2 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³), expands at constant pressure to 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ at state B, and is then heated at constant volume to a final pressure of 3.52 × 10⁵ Pa at state C. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the final temperature T_C at state C?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates PV / (nR) at the target state to obtain 363 K (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reports the final temperature converted to °C when the question and options specify kelvin.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes T_B after the isobaric stage and omits the isochoric pressure ratio P_C / P_A.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the initial volume V_A instead of V_B = V_C when evaluating T_C = P_C V_C / (nR).

items.stem: Operating clockwise between 2.4 × 10⁻³ m³ and 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³ and between 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa and 5.4 × 10⁵ Pa, 0.2 mol of monatomic ideal gas in an insulated aerospace gas-accumulator cylinder completes cycle A → B → C → D → A. Taking net work done by the gas as positive, what is the net mechanical work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Net work done by the gas equals the enclosed rectangular area: W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = (5.4 × 10⁵ − 1.8 × 10⁵)(4.8 × 10⁻³ − 2.4 × 10⁻³) = 864 J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes netWorkJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 864 J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Applies an extra factor of one-half from misremembering the degrees-of-freedom or geometric prefactor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the expansion work along A → B and forgets to subtract the compression work along C → D.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes P_B V_B − P_D V_D instead of the enclosed rectangular loop area (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min).

items.stem: The P–V diagram shows a rapid thermally insulated (adiabatic) expansion A → B of 1.5 mol of monatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) in a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity from (4.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³) to final volume 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). Determine the final pressure P_B.
items.workedSolution: For a monatomic adiabatic process, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 4.0 × 10⁵ × (3.0 × 10⁻³ / 6.0 × 10⁻³)^(5/3) = 1.26 × 10⁵ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P V^(5/3) = const to obtain 1.26 × 10⁵ Pa (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses the diatomic adiabatic index γ = 7/5 instead of γ = 5/3 for a monatomic gas.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats the process as isothermal (P_A V_A = P_B V_B) rather than adiabatic (P_A V_A^(5/3) = P_B V_B^(5/3)).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the adiabatic exponent, using 3/5 instead of γ = 5/3.

items.stem: In a frictionless piston-cylinder assembly on a thermodynamics test bench, 0.75 mol of monatomic ideal gas executes a reversible Carnot heat-engine cycle between a hot reservoir at 627 °C and a cold sink at 47 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15), expanding isothermally at the hot reservoir from V_A = 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 2.4 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the theoretical thermal efficiency η of this Carnot cycle?
items.workedSolution: Convert to kelvin: T_H = 900.15 K, T_C = 320.15 K. Carnot efficiency η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 1 − 320.15 / 900.15 = 0.644.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 0.644 (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates T_C / T_H without subtracting from 1.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes Celsius temperatures directly into 1 − θ_C / θ_H instead of converting to absolute kelvin temperatures.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides ΔT by T_C instead of T_H when computing efficiency.

items.stem: A closed reciprocating loop (a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell) carries 0.25 mol of monatomic ideal gas (adiabatic index 5/3) around Otto cycle A → B → C → D → A between volume limits 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ and 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³, with initial pressure P_A = 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa and peak pressure P_C = 1.647 × 10⁶ Pa. Determine its thermal efficiency.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic Otto cycle (γ = 5/3), η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1) = 1 − (2.0 × 10⁻³ / 6.0 × 10⁻³)^(2/3) = 0.519 (equivalently W_net / Q_in = 1.400 × 10³ / 2.696 × 10³ = 0.519).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 0.519 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses exponent 1 instead of γ − 1 = 2/3 in the Otto efficiency relation η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes Carnot efficiency 1 − T_A / T_C between extreme cycle temperatures instead of Otto efficiency.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Raises V_min / V_max to γ = 5/3 rather than γ − 1 = 2/3.

items.stem: In an automated cryostat sample holder, a Peltier extraction module rated at 1200 W with coupling efficiency 0.8 removes thermal energy as a 0.55 kg sample of water goes from 313 K to 235 K across its 273.15 K fusion point (c_solid = 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹). How long does the isothermal freezing plateau last?
items.workedSolution: Effective thermal power P_eff = η P = 0.8 × 1200 = 960.0 W. Plateau latent energy Q_f = m L_f = 1.837 × 10⁵ J, giving Δt_plateau = Q_f / P_eff = 191 s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_eff = η P and divides required thermal energy to obtain 191 s (C).
