options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies time by efficiency η instead of dividing energy by effective power η P.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides thermal energy by the nominal electrical rating P rather than the effective thermal power η P.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the total multi-stage duration rather than the isothermal fusion plateau duration alone.

items.stem: A heated copper block of mass 0.65 kg and specific heat capacity 385 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 380 K is plunged into 0.42 kg of water (c = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 290 K inside a double-walled vacuum Dewar mixing vessel. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. How much thermal energy is released by the copper block in reaching equilibrium?
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l), giving T_eq = 301.2 K. Heat released by the solid Q_lost = m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = 1.97 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 1.97 × 10⁴ J (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses a mass-only weighted average temperature, ignoring the difference in specific heat capacities.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the final equilibrium temperature is the unweighted midpoint (T_solid + T_liquid) / 2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the solid cools all the way down to the initial bath temperature T_liquid instead of T_eq.

items.stem: Operating at 1200 K with effective blackbody emissivity 1 and area 1.5 × 10⁻³ m², a nearby solar-type star modelled as an ideal spherical radiator irradiates a sensor located 1.5 m away in vacuum. Taking Wien's constant b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K, what is the peak emission wavelength λ_max in nanometres?
items.workedSolution: By Wien's displacement law, λ_max = b / T = (2.90 × 10⁻³) / 1200 = 2.417 × 10⁻⁶ m = 2.42 × 10³ nm.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the blackbody radiation law in SI units to obtain 2.42 × 10³ nm (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Wien's displacement law by dividing T by b instead of b by T.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts 273.15 from the kelvin temperature before applying Wien's law.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies Wien's constant b by T instead of dividing b by T.

items.stem: In a climate radiative-transfer model, an arid continental land-surface test plot of area 18 m² and surface emissivity e = 0.92 is at 296 K while exchanging thermal infrared radiation with an effective surrounding environment at 268 K. Taking σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, what is the net rate of radiative energy loss P_net from the surface?
items.workedSolution: Net radiative power loss P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) = 0.92 × 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × 18 × ((296)⁴ − (268)⁴) = 2.36 × 10³ W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) to obtain 2.36 × 10³ W (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates e σ A (T − T_amb)⁴ instead of e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴), a classic fourth-power algebra error.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the greybody emissivity factor e (< 1) from P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates gross emitted power e σ A T⁴ and ignores incoming radiation absorbed from the surroundings at T_amb.

items.stem: In a thermostatted noble-gas reference bulb (volume 0.04 m³), 1.2 mol of monatomic Argon-40 (Ar) of molar mass 40 g mol⁻¹ is warmed from T₁ = 550 K to T₂ = 1238 K, shifting the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed curve as plotted. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), determine v_rms at the higher temperature T₂.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.04 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 1238 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 1238 / 0.04) = 878 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 878 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: The volume–temperature (V–T) diagram traces 0.35 mol of ideal gas inside a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity. Starting at A (1.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³), the gas expands at constant pressure to volume 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³ at state B and is then heated at constant volume to 2.56 × 10⁵ Pa at state C (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). Calculate T_B.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates PV / (nR) at the target state to obtain 275 K (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Charles's law ratio, multiplying T_A by V_A / V_B instead of V_B / V_A.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Stops after computing the initial temperature T_A = P_A V_A / (nR) without scaling by V_B / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the final temperature T_C at state C rather than the intermediate temperature T_B.

items.stem: The P–V graph shows an isobaric compression of 0.25 mol of ideal monatomic gas inside a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals at 4.5 × 10⁵ Pa from V_A = 6.3 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³. Using the sign convention where work done on the gas is positive, determine the compression work done on the gas.
items.workedSolution: During isobaric compression from 6.3 × 10⁻³ m³ to 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at 4.5 × 10⁵ Pa, work done on the gas W_on = −P(V_B − V_A) = 4.5 × 10⁵ × (6.3 × 10⁻³ − 3.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.26 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 1.26 × 10³ J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the magnitude of internal energy change |ΔU| = (3/2) P |ΔV| instead of boundary work P |ΔV|.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies pressure by initial volume V_A instead of the volume change |V_B − V_A|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the total heat rejected |Q| = (5/2) P |ΔV| rather than the mechanical work done on the gas.

items.stem: The P–V diagram shows a rapid thermally insulated (adiabatic) expansion A → B of 0.5 mol of monatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) in a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder from (4.8 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to final volume 8.75 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). Determine the final pressure P_B.
items.workedSolution: For a monatomic adiabatic process, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 4.8 × 10⁵ × (2.5 × 10⁻³ / 8.75 × 10⁻³)^(5/3) = 5.95 × 10⁴ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P V^(5/3) = const to obtain 5.95 × 10⁴ Pa (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses the diatomic adiabatic index γ = 7/5 instead of γ = 5/3 for a monatomic gas.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats the process as isothermal (P_A V_A = P_B V_B) rather than adiabatic (P_A V_A^(5/3) = P_B V_B^(5/3)).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the adiabatic exponent, using 3/5 instead of γ = 5/3.

items.stem: On the P–V diagram, 0.6 mol of an ideal gas in an insulated aerospace gas-accumulator cylinder undergoes a reversible isothermal expansion at 400 K from 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 0.0225 m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and expansion work by the gas as positive. Find W_AB.
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 400 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.6 × 8.31 × 400 × ln(0.0225 / 5.0 × 10⁻³) = 3.00 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 3.00 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds U = (3/2)nRT to isothermal work, overlooking that ΔU = 0 at constant temperature.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as remaining constant at P_A, computing P_A(V_B − V_A) instead of ∫ P dV = nRT ln(V_B / V_A).

items.stem: A closed reciprocating loop (a variable-volume optical pressure cell) carries 1.2 mol of monatomic ideal gas (adiabatic index 5/3) around Otto cycle A → B → C → D → A between volume limits 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ and 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³, with initial pressure P_A = 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa and peak pressure P_C = 1.437 × 10⁶ Pa. Determine its thermal efficiency.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic Otto cycle (γ = 5/3), η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1) = 1 − (1.2 × 10⁻³ / 3.0 × 10⁻³)^(2/3) = 0.457 (equivalently W_net / Q_in = 727.5 / 1.592 × 10³ = 0.457).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 0.457 (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Applies an extra factor of one-half from misremembering the degrees-of-freedom or geometric prefactor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses exponent 1 instead of γ − 1 = 2/3 in the Otto efficiency relation η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Raises V_min / V_max to γ = 5/3 rather than γ − 1 = 2/3.

items.stem: Calorimetric heating carries 0.45 kg of water in a metallurgical vacuum-induction melting pot from an initial solid temperature of 243 K up to 358 K as liquid. Using 273.15 K for the melting point, specific heat capacities 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ (solid) and 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ (liquid), and specific latent heat of fusion L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹, determine the total enthalpy input.

markScheme.criterion: Sums sensible mcΔT stages and latent heat mL to obtain 3.38 × 10⁵ J (C).

items.stem: Inside an expanded-polystyrene adiabatic quenching bath, 0.22 kg of ethanol (specific heat capacity 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 302 K receives a 0.48 kg aluminium specimen (c = 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 475 K. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. Calculate the equilibrium temperature of the mixture.
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l), giving T_eq = 379.1 K. Therefore T_eq = 379 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 379 K (B).

items.stem: Inside a low-heat-capacity polymeric calorimetry beaker, 0.035 kg of ice initially at 263.15 K is added to 0.58 kg of liquid water at 318.15 K. Take melting point T_m = 273.15 K, c_ice = 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_water = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, and L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹. Neglecting external heat losses, what is the final equilibrium temperature T_eq?
items.workedSolution: Energy to warm and melt all ice at 273.15 K: Q_1+2 = 0.035 × 2100 × (273.15 − 263.15) + 0.035 × 3.34 × 10⁵ = 1.243 × 10⁴ J. Energy balance with warm water: m_w c_w (318.15 − T_eq) = Q_1+2 + m_ice c_w (T_eq − 273.15), giving T_eq = 311 K.

markScheme.criterion: Includes sub-zero ice warming, fusion latent heat, and meltwater warming to obtain 311 K (B).

items.stem: An energy-budget sensor monitors an orbital spacecraft thermal-control radiator panel (area 4 m², greybody emissivity 0.72) maintained at 336 K within a radiative environment at 278 K. Using σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, calculate P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴).
items.workedSolution: Net radiative power loss P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) = 0.72 × 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × 4 × ((336)⁴ − (278)⁴) = 1.11 × 10³ W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) to obtain 1.11 × 10³ W (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates e σ A (T − T_amb)⁴ instead of e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴), a classic fourth-power algebra error.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the greybody emissivity factor e (< 1) from P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates gross emitted power e σ A T⁴ and ignores incoming radiation absorbed from the surroundings at T_amb.

items.stem: Engineers charge a high-vacuum synchrotron beamline gas target (capacity 0.032 m³) with 0.65 mol of Argon-40 (Ar) of molar mass 40 g mol⁻¹ at an equilibrium temperature of 147 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15) (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). Determine the density of the confined gas.
items.workedSolution: Total gas mass m = nM = 0.65 × 0.04 = 0.02600 kg. Density ρ = m / V = 0.02600 / 0.032 = 0.813 kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Applies ρ = nM / V in SI units to obtain 0.813 kg m⁻³ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies total gas mass nM by container volume V instead of dividing by V.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes molar concentration n / V (mol m⁻³) and omits multiplication by molar mass M.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Leaves molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of converting to kg mol⁻¹, overestimating density by a factor of 1000.

items.stem: A low-density plasma-free Xenon-131 (Xe) sample (M = 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹) is held in an atmospheric research dropsonde reference chamber at 260 K. Use molar gas constant R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Calculate the internal energy per mole of the gas.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic gas, molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T = 1.5 × 8.31 × 260 = 3.24 × 10³ J mol⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 260 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 3.24 × 10³ J mol⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Includes only one translational degree of freedom (1/2 R T) instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses molar enthalpy C_p T = (5/2) R T instead of molar internal energy (3/2) R T.

items.stem: Starting from state A (1.1 × 10⁵ Pa, 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³) in a cryocooler compression cylinder containing monatomic working gas, 1.2 mol of ideal gas expands isobarically to 0.011 m³ (state B) and is heated isochorically until the pressure reaches 2.64 × 10⁵ Pa (state C). Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, find the temperature in state C.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates PV / (nR) at the target state to obtain 291 K (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Reports the final temperature converted to °C when the question and options specify kelvin.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes T_B after the isobaric stage and omits the isochoric pressure ratio P_C / P_A.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the initial volume V_A instead of V_B = V_C when evaluating T_C = P_C V_C / (nR).

items.stem: A heat-engine test rig (a variable-volume optical pressure cell) drives 0.5 mol of ideal monatomic gas around a rectangular cycle with upper pressure 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa, lower pressure 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa, minimum volume 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³, and maximum volume 0.016 m³. What is the thermal efficiency η = W_net / Q_in of this rectangular monatomic-gas cycle?
items.workedSolution: W_net = (3.0 × 10⁵ − 1.2 × 10⁵)(0.016 − 4.0 × 10⁻³) = 2.160 × 10³ J. Heat enters on D → A and A → B: Q_in = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min + (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 1.008 × 10⁴ J. Efficiency η = W_net / Q_in = 0.214.

markScheme.criterion: Computes thermalEfficiency correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 0.214 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides W_net by Q_AB alone, neglecting the heat input Q_DA on the isochoric leg D → A.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits internal energy gain ΔU_AB when computing total heat input Q_in.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the Carnot efficiency 1 − T_min / T_max between extreme corner temperatures instead of the actual cycle efficiency W_net / Q_in.

items.stem: On the P–V diagram, 0.6 mol of an ideal gas in a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell undergoes a reversible isothermal expansion at 450 K from 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 0.01575 m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and expansion work by the gas as positive. Find W_AB.
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 450 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.6 × 8.31 × 450 × ln(0.01575 / 3.5 × 10⁻³) = 3.37 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 3.37 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds U = (3/2)nRT to isothermal work, overlooking that ΔU = 0 at constant temperature.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as remaining constant at P_A, computing P_A(V_B − V_A) instead of ∫ P dV = nRT ln(V_B / V_A).

items.stem: The diagram shows a reversible Carnot cycle A → B → C → D → A for 0.75 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder coupled to a hot reservoir at 627 °C and a cold sink at 87 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15), with isothermal expansion from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what magnitude of thermal energy Q_C is rejected to the cold sink per cycle?
items.workedSolution: During isothermal compression C → D at T_C = 360.15 K, V_C / V_D = V_B / V_A, so heat rejected to the cold sink is Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) = 2.06 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 2.06 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A) in Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes net work W_net = Q_H − Q_C instead of the rejected heat Q_C.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the heat absorbed Q_H from the hot reservoir instead of the heat Q_C rejected to the cold sink.

items.stem: Starting at 184 K in a thermal-energy-storage phase-change capsule, 1.25 kg of ethanol absorbs heat, crosses its 351 K boiling point (specific latent heat of vaporization L_v = 8.46 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹), and finishes as vapour at 381 K. With c_liquid = 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ and c_vapour = 1600 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, how much energy was supplied?
items.workedSolution: Sensible heating: Q_sens = 1.25 × 2440 × (351 − 184) + 1.25 × 1600 × (381 − 351) = 5.694 × 10⁵ J. Latent heat on plateau: Q_lat = mL = 1.25 × 8.46 × 10⁵ = 1.058 × 10⁶ J. Total Q = 1.63 × 10⁶ J.

markScheme.criterion: Sums sensible mcΔT stages and latent heat mL to obtain 1.63 × 10⁶ J (D).

items.stem: In a ceramic-lined materials characterization furnace, an electrical immersion heater of input power 320 W and thermal transfer efficiency 0.75 supplies energy as a 0.3 kg sample of lead goes from 563 K to 626 K across its 600.6 K fusion point (c_solid = 128 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 147 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, L_f = 2.3 × 10⁴ J kg⁻¹). How long does the isothermal melting plateau last?
items.workedSolution: Effective thermal power P_eff = η P = 0.75 × 320 = 240.0 W. Plateau latent energy Q_f = m L_f = 6.900 × 10³ J, giving Δt_plateau = Q_f / P_eff = 28.8 s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_eff = η P and divides required thermal energy to obtain 28.8 s (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies time by efficiency η instead of dividing energy by effective power η P.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides thermal energy by the nominal electrical rating P rather than the effective thermal power η P.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the total multi-stage duration rather than the isothermal fusion plateau duration alone.

items.stem: Inside a well-insulated copper-lined laboratory calorimeter, 0.035 kg of ice initially at 253.15 K is added to 0.48 kg of liquid water at 338.15 K. Take melting point T_m = 273.15 K, c_ice = 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_water = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, and L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹. Neglecting external heat losses, what is the final equilibrium temperature T_eq?
items.workedSolution: Energy to warm and melt all ice at 273.15 K: Q_1+2 = 0.035 × 2100 × (273.15 − 253.15) + 0.035 × 3.34 × 10⁵ = 1.316 × 10⁴ J. Energy balance with warm water: m_w c_w (338.15 − T_eq) = Q_1+2 + m_ice c_w (T_eq − 273.15), giving T_eq = 328 K.

markScheme.criterion: Includes sub-zero ice warming, fusion latent heat, and meltwater warming to obtain 328 K (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Applies an extra factor of one-half from misremembering the degrees-of-freedom or geometric prefactor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Introduces an extraneous integer factor when rearranging the governing thermal relation.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Introduces an extraneous integer factor when rearranging the governing thermal relation.

items.stem: Modelled as an ideal blackbody (emissivity = 1), a luminous A-type stellar photosphere has surface area 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ m², absolute surface temperature 2600 K, and is observed from a distance d = 1.5 m. Taking σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, what is the radiant intensity received at distance d (neglecting intervening absorption)?
items.workedSolution: Radiated luminosity L = σ A T⁴ = 647.8 W. Intensity at distance d is I = L / (4π d²) = 647.8 / (4π × (1.5)²) = 22.9 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the blackbody radiation law in SI units to obtain 22.9 W m⁻² (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides by 4π d instead of 4π d², omitting the inverse-square exponent.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Divides radiated power by disc area π d² instead of spherical shell area 4π d².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the geometric factor 4π for isotropic spherical spreading in I = L / (4π d²).

items.stem: 2.2 mol of monatomic Krypton-84 (Kr) (molar mass 0.0838 kg mol⁻¹) fills a thick-walled titanium deep-sea pressure housing of volume 0.024 m³ at a steady temperature of 240 K. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Find the gas pressure.
items.workedSolution: From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (2.2 × 8.31 × 240) / 0.024 = 1.83 × 10⁵ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 1.83 × 10⁵ Pa (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies nRT by volume V instead of dividing nRT by V.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts 273.15 from an already-kelvin temperature before applying pV = nRT.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the amount of substance n in p = nRT / V, solving for 1 mol instead of the given molar amount.

items.stem: An experiment records the molecular speed distribution of 0.5 mol of Xenon-131 (Xe) gas (molar mass 131.3 g mol⁻¹) occupying 0.04 m³ in a sealed borosilicate acoustic-thermometry sphere at 250 K (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²)). Which value equals the rms speed of the atoms?
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 250 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 250 / 0.1313) = 218 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 218 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: In a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals, 0.5 mol of an ideal gas starts at state A with pressure 1.1 × 10⁵ Pa and volume 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³. As shown on the pressure–temperature (P–T) diagram, the gas expands isobarically from A to state B of volume 9.0 × 10⁻³ m³, before undergoing isochoric heating from B to state C at 1.54 × 10⁵ Pa. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the temperature T_B at state B?

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates PV / (nR) at the target state to obtain 238 K (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Charles's law ratio, multiplying T_A by V_A / V_B instead of V_B / V_A.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Stops after computing the initial temperature T_A = P_A V_A / (nR) without scaling by V_B / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the final temperature T_C at state C rather than the intermediate temperature T_B.

items.stem: A sample of 0.4 mol of an ideal monatomic gas in a closed noble-gas power-conversion loop expands isobarically at constant pressure 4.5 × 10⁵ Pa from volume 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (state A) to 4.4 × 10⁻³ m³ (state B). Taking thermal energy supplied to the gas and work done by the gas as positive, how much thermal energy Q is supplied to the gas during A → B?
items.workedSolution: Work done by the gas W_by = P(V_B − V_A) = 4.5 × 10⁵ × (4.4 × 10⁻³ − 2.0 × 10⁻³) = 1.080 × 10³ J. For a monatomic ideal gas, ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV = 1.620 × 10³ J. By the first law, Q = ΔU + W_by = (5/2) P ΔV = 2.70 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 2.70 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the boundary work W = P ΔV done by the gas and ignores the increase in internal energy ΔU.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the internal energy change ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV and omits the expansion work P ΔV.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV, computing ΔU + W = P ΔV + P ΔV = 2 P ΔV instead of (5/2) P ΔV.

items.stem: Inside a frictionless piston-cylinder assembly on a thermodynamics test bench, 0.4 mol of an ideal monatomic gas (adiabatic index γ = 5/3) initially at P_A = 6.0 × 10⁵ Pa and V_A = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ is reversibly and adiabatically expanded to V_B = 0.01 m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the final pressure P_B in state B?
items.workedSolution: For a monatomic adiabatic process, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 6.0 × 10⁵ × (2.5 × 10⁻³ / 0.01)^(5/3) = 5.95 × 10⁴ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P V^(5/3) = const to obtain 5.95 × 10⁴ Pa (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses the diatomic adiabatic index γ = 7/5 instead of γ = 5/3 for a monatomic gas.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats the process as isothermal (P_A V_A = P_B V_B) rather than adiabatic (P_A V_A^(5/3) = P_B V_B^(5/3)).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the adiabatic exponent, using 3/5 instead of γ = 5/3.

items.stem: In a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder coupled to a thermal reservoir at 280 K, 0.6 mol of an ideal gas expands reversibly and isothermally from V_A = 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 3.6 × 10⁻³ m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the change in entropy ΔS of the gas?
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.6 × 8.31 × ln(3.6 × 10⁻³ / 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 4.37 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 4.37 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 logarithm log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of the natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Replaces ln(V_B / V_A) with the linear fractional change (V_B − V_A) / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes isothermal heat Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) without dividing by T to obtain ΔS = Q / T.

items.stem: Inside a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity, 0.6 mol of an ideal monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) performs a closed three-step cycle A → B → C → A: reversible adiabatic expansion from state A (6.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³) to volume 8.0 × 10⁻³ m³ at B, isobaric compression from B to volume 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ at C, and isochoric heating from C back to A. Taking work done by the gas as positive, what is the net work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: At B, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 6.449 × 10⁴ Pa. Adiabatic work W_AB = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 1.176 × 10³ J, and isobaric compression work W_BC = P_B(V_C − V_B) = -386.9 J (W_CA = 0). Thus W_net = W_AB + W_BC = 789 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 789 J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the magnitude of the isobaric compression work P_B(V_B − V_C).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the adiabatic expansion work W_AB and forgets to subtract the isobaric compression work |W_BC|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_CA along the isochoric leg instead of net work W_net.

items.stem: The temperature–time curve shows 0.2 kg of aluminium inside a guarded electrical immersion-heating vessel (heated between 916 K and 994 K; T_m = 933.5 K, c_solid = 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 1180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, L_f = 3.97 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹) while an electrical immersion heater of input power 320 W and thermal transfer efficiency 0.9 supplies energy. Calculate the total duration of the process.
items.workedSolution: Effective thermal power P_eff = η P = 0.9 × 320 = 288.0 W. Total energy Q_tot = m c_solid ΔT_s + m L_f + m c_liquid ΔT_l = 9.683 × 10⁴ J, giving t_total = Q_tot / P_eff = 336 s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_eff = η P and divides required thermal energy to obtain 336 s (D).

items.stem: A heated brass block of mass 0.36 kg and specific heat capacity 380 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 440 K is plunged into 0.72 kg of water (c = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 285 K inside a lagged benchtop thermal-equilibrium chamber. During mixing, 950 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. What is the final thermal equilibrium temperature T_eq?
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l) + 950, giving T_eq = 291.4 K. Therefore T_eq = 291 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 291 K (B).

items.stem: Modelled as an ideal blackbody (emissivity = 1), an incandescent refractory-metal calibration sphere has surface area 3.6 × 10¹⁸ m², absolute surface temperature 5500 K, and is observed from a distance d = 6.8 × 10¹¹ m. Taking Wien's constant b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K, what is the peak emission wavelength λ_max in nanometres?
items.workedSolution: By Wien's displacement law, λ_max = b / T = (2.90 × 10⁻³) / 5500 = 5.273 × 10⁻⁷ m = 527 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the blackbody radiation law in SI units to obtain 527 nm (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Wien's displacement law by dividing T by b instead of b by T.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts 273.15 from the kelvin temperature before applying Wien's law.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies Wien's constant b by T instead of dividing b by T.

items.stem: In a climate radiative-transfer model, a polar sea-ice radiative-balance monitoring sector of area 1.2 m² and surface emissivity e = 0.95 is at 298 K while exchanging thermal infrared radiation with an effective surrounding environment at 240 K. Taking σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, what is the net rate of radiative energy loss P_net from the surface?
items.workedSolution: Net radiative power loss P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) = 0.95 × 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × 1.2 × ((298)⁴ − (240)⁴) = 295 W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) to obtain 295 W (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates e σ A (T − T_amb)⁴ instead of e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴), a classic fourth-power algebra error.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the greybody emissivity factor e (< 1) from P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates gross emitted power e σ A T⁴ and ignores incoming radiation absorbed from the surroundings at T_amb.

items.stem: In an atmospheric research dropsonde reference chamber (volume 0.05 m³), 0.3 mol of monatomic Helium-4 (He) of molar mass 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹ is warmed from T₁ = 320 K to T₂ = 576 K, shifting the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed curve as plotted. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), determine v_rms at the higher temperature T₂.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 576 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 576 / 4.0 × 10⁻³) = 1.89 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 1.89 × 10³ m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: Thermalised Neon-20 (Ne) vapour of molar mass 0.0202 kg mol⁻¹ fills a rigid stainless-steel vacuum-calibration tank at a uniform temperature of 327 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Calculate the internal energy per mole of the gas.
items.workedSolution: T = 327 + 273.15 = 600.15 K. For an ideal monatomic gas, molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T = 1.5 × 8.31 × 600.15 = 7.48 × 10³ J mol⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 600.15 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 7.48 × 10³ J mol⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Includes only one translational degree of freedom (1/2 R T) instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses molar enthalpy C_p T = (5/2) R T instead of molar internal energy (3/2) R T.

items.stem: The P–V graph shows an isobaric compression of 0.6 mol of ideal monatomic gas inside a variable-volume optical pressure cell at 4.5 × 10⁵ Pa from V_A = 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³. Using the sign convention where work done on the gas is positive, determine the compression work done on the gas.
items.workedSolution: During isobaric compression from 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at 4.5 × 10⁵ Pa, work done on the gas W_on = −P(V_B − V_A) = 4.5 × 10⁵ × (4.5 × 10⁻³ − 2.5 × 10⁻³) = 900 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 900 J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the magnitude of internal energy change |ΔU| = (3/2) P |ΔV| instead of boundary work P |ΔV|.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies pressure by initial volume V_A instead of the volume change |V_B − V_A|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the total heat rejected |Q| = (5/2) P |ΔV| rather than the mechanical work done on the gas.

items.stem: Operating clockwise between 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ and 9.0 × 10⁻³ m³ and between 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa and 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.5 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber completes cycle A → B → C → D → A. What is the total thermal energy Q_in absorbed by the monatomic gas during the heating legs D → A and A → B?
items.workedSolution: Heat enters on D → A (isochoric, W = 0): Q_DA = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min = 810.0 J, and on A → B (isobaric): Q_AB = (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 4.500 × 10³ J. Total Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = 5.31 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes heatInputJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 5.31 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Confuses net cycle heat Q_net = W_net with total heat input Q_in absorbed from the hot source.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic ΔU on both heating legs.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Includes only the heat absorbed during isobaric expansion A → B and omits the isochoric heating D → A.

items.stem: A thermal bath keeps 0.6 mol of ideal gas in a precision pneumatic actuator chamber sealed with a movable piston at 400 K during a reversible expansion from 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is the thermal energy Q supplied to the gas (equal to work done by the gas)?
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 400 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.6 × 8.31 × 400 × ln(3.0 × 10⁻³ / 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.38 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 1.38 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as remaining constant at P_A, computing P_A(V_B − V_A) instead of ∫ P dV = nRT ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Adds U = (3/2)nRT to isothermal work, overlooking that ΔU = 0 at constant temperature.

items.stem: A Carnot engine modelled in a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity uses 0.3 mol of ideal gas operating between a hot reservoir at 427 °C and a cold sink at 67 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). During the high-temperature isothermal stage A → B, the volume increases from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking net work done by the gas as positive (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹), what is the net work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.210 × 10³ J and η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 0.5142. Net work output W_net = η Q_H = nR(T_H − T_C) ln(V_B / V_A) = 622 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 622 J (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the rejected heat Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) instead of net work Q_H − Q_C.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) without multiplying by Carnot efficiency (1 − T_C / T_H).

items.stem: The phase-change graph plots temperature against thermal energy transferred for 0.85 kg of aluminium in a sealed industrial distillation reboiler test cell warmed from 884 K to 999 K across its melting point at 933.5 K (c_solid = 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 1180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, specific latent heat of fusion L_f = 3.97 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹). Calculate the total thermal energy required.

markScheme.criterion: Sums sensible mcΔT stages and latent heat mL to obtain 4.41 × 10⁵ J (D).

items.stem: During a timed run in a spacecraft latent-heat thermal-buffer canister, a Peltier extraction module rated at 1600 W with coupling efficiency 0.75 removes thermal energy on 0.2 kg of water between 333 K and 245 K. Given melting point 273.15 K, L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹, c_s = 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, and c_l = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine the constant-temperature arrest time.
items.workedSolution: Effective thermal power P_eff = η P = 0.75 × 1600 = 1.200 × 10³ W. Plateau latent energy Q_f = m L_f = 6.680 × 10⁴ J, giving Δt_plateau = Q_f / P_eff = 55.7 s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_eff = η P and divides required thermal energy to obtain 55.7 s (C).

items.stem: In a thermally isolated materials-testing bath, 0.34 kg of water cools from 301.15 K down to 273.15 K against 0.3 kg of melting ice initially at 273.15 K (c = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹; fusion enthalpy 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹). Find the melted ice mass.
items.workedSolution: Maximum heat released by water cooling to 273.15 K is Q = 0.34 × 4180 × (301.15 − 273.15) = 3.979 × 10⁴ J, which is less than m_ice L_f = 1.002 × 10⁵ J. Mass melted Δm = Q / L_f = 0.119 kg.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates Δm = m_water c_water (T_water − 273.15) / L_f to obtain 0.119 kg (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides available thermal energy by the latent heat of vaporization (2.26 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹) instead of fusion.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes the mass of unmelted ice remaining at 273.15 K rather than the mass of ice that melts.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the dimensionless melted fraction Δm / m_ice instead of the melted mass Δm in kg.

items.stem: An energy-budget sensor monitors a selectively coated solar-thermal collector plate (area 6.5 m², greybody emissivity 0.78) maintained at 343 K within a radiative environment at 268 K. Using σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, calculate P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴).
items.workedSolution: Net radiative power loss P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) = 0.78 × 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × 6.5 × ((343)⁴ − (268)⁴) = 2.50 × 10³ W.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) to obtain 2.50 × 10³ W (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates e σ A (T − T_amb)⁴ instead of e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴), a classic fourth-power algebra error.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the greybody emissivity factor e (< 1) from P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates gross emitted power e σ A T⁴ and ignores incoming radiation absorbed from the surroundings at T_amb.

items.stem: Inside an ion-propulsion xenon feed manifold of internal volume 0.032 m³, 0.35 mol of ideal Helium-4 (He) gas (molar mass 4 g mol⁻¹) is maintained at 460 K. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what is the mass density of the gas?

markScheme.criterion: Applies ρ = nM / V in SI units to obtain 0.0437 kg m⁻³ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies total gas mass nM by container volume V instead of dividing by V.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes molar concentration n / V (mol m⁻³) and omits multiplication by molar mass M.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Leaves molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of converting to kg mol⁻¹, overestimating density by a factor of 1000.

items.stem: Spectroscopic thermometry confirms that Argon-40 (Ar) atoms (molar mass 0.04 kg mol⁻¹) in a sealed quartz spectroscopy cell are equilibrated at 820 K. Use Boltzmann constant 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and elementary charge 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. Determine the mean kinetic energy per atom expressed in eV.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 820 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 0.106 eV (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates (1/2) k_B T / e for a single degree of freedom instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes k_B T / e and omits the 3/2 translational factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the 3/2 factor to 3 k_B T / e by omitting the 1/2 in kinetic energy.

items.stem: A sample of 0.35 mol of ideal gas in a closed noble-gas power-conversion loop undergoes an isobaric expansion from state A (1.4 × 10⁵ Pa, 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B (9.0 × 10⁻³ m³), followed by an isochoric rise to 3.36 × 10⁵ Pa at state C. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, find the absolute temperature at B.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates PV / (nR) at the target state to obtain 433 K (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Charles's law ratio, multiplying T_A by V_A / V_B instead of V_B / V_A.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Stops after computing the initial temperature T_A = P_A V_A / (nR) without scaling by V_B / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the final temperature T_C at state C rather than the intermediate temperature T_B.

items.stem: In a frictionless piston-cylinder assembly on a thermodynamics test bench, 0.5 mol of a monatomic ideal gas executes a clockwise closed cycle A → B → C → D → A between pressures 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa and 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa and volumes 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³ and 0.012 m³ (A → B isobaric expansion at 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa, B → C isochoric cooling, C → D isobaric compression at 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, D → A isochoric heating). What is the thermal efficiency η = W_net / Q_in of this rectangular monatomic-gas cycle?
items.workedSolution: W_net = (3.0 × 10⁵ − 1.5 × 10⁵)(0.012 − 4.0 × 10⁻³) = 1.200 × 10³ J. Heat enters on D → A and A → B: Q_in = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min + (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 6.900 × 10³ J. Efficiency η = W_net / Q_in = 0.174.

markScheme.criterion: Computes thermalEfficiency correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 0.174 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides W_net by Q_AB alone, neglecting the heat input Q_DA on the isochoric leg D → A.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits internal energy gain ΔU_AB when computing total heat input Q_in.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the Carnot efficiency 1 − T_min / T_max between extreme corner temperatures instead of the actual cycle efficiency W_net / Q_in.

items.stem: A thermally isolated sample of 0.4 mol of monatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) in a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder transitions adiabatically from state A (1.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 3.2 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B of volume 1.6 × 10⁻³ m³. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, calculate the gas pressure at state B.
items.workedSolution: For a monatomic adiabatic process, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 1.6 × 10⁵ × (3.2 × 10⁻³ / 1.6 × 10⁻³)^(5/3) = 5.08 × 10⁵ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P V^(5/3) = const to obtain 5.08 × 10⁵ Pa (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts the adiabatic exponent, using 3/5 instead of γ = 5/3.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Treats the process as isothermal (P_A V_A = P_B V_B) rather than adiabatic (P_A V_A^(5/3) = P_B V_B^(5/3)).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the diatomic adiabatic index γ = 7/5 instead of γ = 5/3 for a monatomic gas.

items.stem: The diagram shows a reversible Carnot cycle A → B → C → D → A for 1 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a cryocooler compression cylinder containing monatomic working gas coupled to a hot reservoir at 537 K and a cold sink at 290 K, with isothermal expansion from 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what magnitude of thermal energy Q_C is rejected to the cold sink per cycle?
items.workedSolution: During isothermal compression C → D at T_C = 290 K, V_C / V_D = V_B / V_A, so heat rejected to the cold sink is Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.67 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 1.67 × 10³ J (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A) in Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes net work W_net = Q_H − Q_C instead of the rejected heat Q_C.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the heat absorbed Q_H from the hot reservoir instead of the heat Q_C rejected to the cold sink.

items.stem: A closed heat engine (a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals) takes 1.2 mol of monatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) from A (5.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³) adiabatically to V_B = 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³, compresses it at constant pressure back to V_C = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³, and heats it isochorically back to A. Find the net work done by the gas per cycle (work by gas positive).
items.workedSolution: At B, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 1.732 × 10⁵ Pa. Adiabatic work W_AB = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 763.2 J, and isobaric compression work W_BC = P_B(V_C − V_B) = -433.1 J (W_CA = 0). Thus W_net = W_AB + W_BC = 330 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 330 J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the magnitude of the isobaric compression work P_B(V_B − V_C).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the adiabatic expansion work W_AB and forgets to subtract the isobaric compression work |W_BC|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_CA along the isochoric leg instead of net work W_net.

items.stem: In a precision constant-flux heating chamber, an electrical immersion heater of input power 750 W and thermal transfer efficiency 0.85 supplies energy as a 0.75 kg sample of ethanol goes from 141 K to 184 K across its 159 K fusion point (c_solid = 1120 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, L_f = 1.08 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹). What total time elapses for the complete temperature change?
items.workedSolution: Effective thermal power P_eff = η P = 0.85 × 750 = 637.5 W. Total energy Q_tot = m c_solid ΔT_s + m L_f + m c_liquid ΔT_l = 1.419 × 10⁵ J, giving t_total = Q_tot / P_eff = 223 s.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_eff = η P and divides required thermal energy to obtain 223 s (D).

items.stem: In a calorimetry run using a low-heat-capacity polymeric calorimetry beaker, a 0.28 kg cylinder of copper (c = 385 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 475 K is quenched in 0.32 kg of mineral oil (c = 1960 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 298 K. During mixing, 950 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. Find T_eq at thermal equilibrium.
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l) + 950, giving T_eq = 322.7 K. Therefore T_eq = 323 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 323 K (B).

items.stem: The Planck spectral curve shown corresponds to a vacuum-chamber blackbody radiometer target of radiating area 1.8 × 10¹⁸ m² and uniform blackbody temperature 5500 K, monitored by a radiometer 6.8 × 10¹¹ m away. Taking σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, what is the radiant intensity received at distance d (neglecting intervening absorption)?
items.workedSolution: Radiated luminosity L = σ A T⁴ = 9.339 × 10²⁵ W. Intensity at distance d is I = L / (4π d²) = 9.339 × 10²⁵ / (4π × (6.8 × 10¹¹)²) = 16.1 W m⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the blackbody radiation law in SI units to obtain 16.1 W m⁻² (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides radiated power by disc area π d² instead of spherical shell area 4π d².

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the geometric factor 4π for isotropic spherical spreading in I = L / (4π d²).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides by 4π d instead of 4π d², omitting the inverse-square exponent.

items.stem: The figure displays Maxwell–Boltzmann speed distributions for 1.5 mol of monatomic Neon-20 (Ne) (molar mass 20.2 g mol⁻¹) sealed in a cryogenic buffer reservoir in a superconducting magnet rig of rigid volume 0.05 m³ at T₁ = 360 K (solid curve) and after heating to T₂ = 648 K (dashed curve). Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²).

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_rms = √(3RT₁ / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹.
Scales v_rms by √(T₂ / T₁) or re-evaluates √(3RT₂ / M).

parts.prompt: Calculate the root-mean-square speed v_rms of the Neon-20 (Ne) atoms at T₁ = 360 K.
Calculate the gas pressure inside the vessel at T₁ = 360 K.
Determine the new root-mean-square speed of the atoms when heated to T₂ = 648 K.

items.stem: The P–V diagram shows 0.6 mol of an ideal monatomic gas in a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder taken from state A (1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B (4.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³) at constant volume, and then from state B to state C (4.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 0.0144 m³) at constant pressure. Throughout this question, take expansion work done by the gas and thermal energy supplied to the gas as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) Work is done only along B → C: W_by = 4.5 × 10⁵(0.0144 − 4.5 × 10⁻³) = 4.46 × 10³ J. (b) ΔU_AC = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A) = 8.71 × 10³ J. (c) Total heat supplied Q = ΔU_AC + W_by = 1.32 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies W_AB = 0 and computes P_B(V_C − V_B).
Sums ΔU_AC and W_by to obtain total heat supplied.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical work done by the gas along path A → B → C.
Calculate the total change in internal energy ΔU of the monatomic gas between state A and state C.
workingSteps: For a monatomic ideal gas, U = (3/2) PV, so ΔU_AC = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A).

parts.prompt: Determine the total thermal energy Q supplied to the gas over the complete path A → B → C.
workingSteps: By the first law of thermodynamics, Q = ΔU_AC + W_by = 8.708 × 10³ + 4.455 × 10³ = 1.32 × 10⁴ J.

items.stem: Inside a closed noble-gas power-conversion loop immersed in a constant-temperature bath at 310 K, 0.3 mol of an ideal monatomic gas expands reversibly along isotherm A → B from V_A = 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 0.01575 m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and expansion work done by the gas as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) P_B = nRT / V_B = 4.91 × 10⁴ Pa. (b) W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.16 × 10³ J. (c) Since ΔU = 0, Q = W_by and ΔS = Q / T = 3.75 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses ΔS = Q / T with Q = W_by.

parts.prompt: Calculate the final pressure P_B of the gas in state B.
Calculate the work done by the gas during the reversible isothermal expansion A → B.
Determine the change in entropy ΔS of the gas during A → B.
workingSteps: Since ΔU = 0 for an ideal gas isotherm, Q = W_by.

items.stem: A 1.25 kg batch of water sealed inside an insulated differential thermal analysis crucible absorbs thermal energy to rise from 243 K (solid) through its 273.15 K melting point to 318 K (liquid), with specific heats 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ and 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ and specific latent heat of fusion L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) Q_sens = m c_solid ΔT₁ + m c_liquid ΔT₂ = 3.13 × 10⁵ J. (b) Plateau latent energy Q_lat = m L = 4.18 × 10⁵ J. (c) Total thermal energy Q_total = Q_sens + Q_lat = 7.31 × 10⁵ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates m c₁ ΔT₁ + m c₂ ΔT₂.
Evaluates m L on the phase-change plateau.

Calculate the thermal energy absorbed during the isothermal phase change at 273.15 K.
Determine the total thermal energy supplied to heat the sample from 243 K to 318 K.

items.stem: Inside a lagged benchtop thermal-equilibrium chamber, 0.065 kg of solid ice initially at 253.15 K is mixed with 0.68 kg of warm liquid water at 328.15 K. External heat losses are negligible. Take T_m = 273.15 K, c_ice = 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_water = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, and L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) Q_lat = m_ice L_f = 2.17 × 10⁴ J. (b) Full enthalpy balance yields T_eq = 316 K. (c) Heat released by warm water = 3.59 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Balances ice warming, melting, and meltwater warming against warm water cooling.

parts.prompt: Calculate the latent thermal energy required solely to melt all the ice once it reaches 273.15 K.
Calculate the final thermal equilibrium temperature T_eq of the water.
workingSteps: m_water c_water (328.15 − T_eq) = m_ice c_ice (273.15 − 253.15) + Q_lat + m_ice c_water (T_eq − 273.15).

parts.prompt: Determine the total thermal energy released by the initially warm water.

items.stem: During a calibration experiment, a sealed quartz spectroscopy cell of internal volume 0.032 m³ is filled with 0.25 mol of ideal Neon-20 (Ne) gas of molar mass 20.2 g mol⁻¹ and stabilised at 17 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Use R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) p = nRT / V = (0.25 × 8.31 × 290.15) / 0.032 = 1.88 × 10⁴ Pa. (b) Single-atom mass m = M / N_A = 0 kg. (c) Density ρ = nM / V = 0.158 kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes Kelvin temperature into p = nRT / V.
Converts molar mass to kg mol⁻¹ and divides by Avogadro constant.
Evaluates ρ = nM / V in SI units.

parts.prompt: Calculate the pressure exerted by the gas on the walls of the vessel.
Determine the mass of a single Neon-20 (Ne) atom in kilograms.
Calculate the macroscopic density of the gas inside the vessel.

items.stem: A pure monatomic sample of Krypton-84 (Kr) (molar mass 0.0838 kg mol⁻¹) inside a thick-walled titanium deep-sea pressure housing is maintained in thermal equilibrium at 57 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Take k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) E_k,avg = (3/2) k_B T = 0 J. (b) Dividing by 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C gives 0.0427 eV. (c) v_rms = √(3RT / M) = 313 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_k = (3/2) k_B T in kelvin.
Divides energy in joules by elementary charge e.

parts.prompt: Calculate the mean translational kinetic energy of a single atom in joules.
Convert this mean translational kinetic energy into electronvolts.
Determine the root-mean-square speed of the Krypton-84 (Kr) atoms.

items.stem: A closed-loop test cylinder (a cryocooler compression cylinder containing monatomic working gas) carries 0.5 mol of monatomic ideal gas clockwise around cycle A → B → C → D → A between volume limits 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ and 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³ and pressure limits 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa and 3.6 × 10⁵ Pa (with A at 3.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ and B at 3.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³). Define work done by the gas as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = 864 J. (b) Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min + (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 3.67 × 10³ J. (c) η = W_net / Q_in = 0.235.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates enclosed loop area (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min).
Identifies heat input on both D → A (isochoric) and A → B (isobaric).
Uses monatomic factors (3/2) on D → A and (5/2) on A → B.
Divides W_net from (a) by Q_in from (b).

parts.prompt: Calculate the net mechanical work W_net done by the gas in one complete cycle.
Calculate the total thermal energy Q_in supplied to the monatomic gas during the heating stages D → A and A → B.

items.stem: A sealed sample of 0.25 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity follows path A → B → C on the P–V diagram: state A is at (1.2 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³), state B is at (3.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³), and state C is at (3.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³). Use the convention where work done by the gas is positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) Work is done only along B → C: W_by = 3.6 × 10⁵(4.8 × 10⁻³ − 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.19 × 10³ J. (b) ΔU_AC = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A) = 2.32 × 10³ J. (c) Total heat supplied Q = ΔU_AC + W_by = 3.51 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies W_AB = 0 and computes P_B(V_C − V_B).
Sums ΔU_AC and W_by to obtain total heat supplied.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical work done by the gas along path A → B → C.
Calculate the total change in internal energy ΔU of the monatomic gas between state A and state C.
workingSteps: For a monatomic ideal gas, U = (3/2) PV, so ΔU_AC = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A).

parts.prompt: Determine the total thermal energy Q supplied to the gas over the complete path A → B → C.
workingSteps: By the first law of thermodynamics, Q = ΔU_AC + W_by = 2.322 × 10³ + 1.188 × 10³ = 3.51 × 10³ J.

items.stem: A closed three-leg heat-engine cycle A → B → C → A in a frictionless piston-cylinder assembly on a thermodynamics test bench uses 0.4 mol of monatomic gas (γ = 5/3): starting from P_A = 5.5 × 10⁵ Pa and V_A = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³, the gas expands adiabatically to 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (B), is compressed at constant pressure to 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ (C), and is heated at constant volume back to A (work by gas positive).
items.workedSolution: (a) Adiabatic relation gives P_B = 1.73 × 10⁵ Pa. (b) Isochoric heat input Q_in = 1.41 × 10³ J. (c) By cyclic energy conservation ΔU_cycle = 0, W_net = Q_in − Q_out = 330 J.

parts.prompt: Determine the net mechanical work W_net done by the gas per cycle.
workingSteps: Heat rejected on isobaric leg B → C is Q_out = (5/2) P_B (V_B − V_C) = 1.083 × 10³ J; W_net = Q_in − Q_out = 330 J.

items.stem: A 0.85 kg iron specimen (c = 450 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) heated to 410 K is immersed in 0.42 kg of mineral oil (c = 1960 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 285 K inside an expanded-polystyrene adiabatic quenching bath. While reaching thermal equilibrium, 650 J of thermal energy is lost to the surroundings.
items.workedSolution: (a) Solving the enthalpy balance yields T_eq = 324 K. (b) Heat released by the hot solid Q_lost = m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = 3.29 × 10⁴ J. (c) Heat gained by the mineral oil Q_liq = m_l c_liq (T_eq − T_l) = 3.22 × 10⁴ J.

items.stem: Inside an undergraduate physics thermal-mixing apparatus, 0.24 kg of liquid water at 293.15 K is mixed adiabatically with an excess 0.24 kg charge of melting ice at 273.15 K (specific heat of water 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹; specific latent heat of fusion 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹).
items.workedSolution: (a) Q_water = m_water c_water (293.15 − 273.15) = 2.01 × 10⁴ J, which is below m_ice L_f. (b) Melted mass Δm = Q_water / L_f = 0.0601 kg. (c) Melted fraction f = Δm / m_ice = 0.250.

markScheme.criterion: Divides Δm by initial ice mass m_ice.

items.stem: A sample of 0.25 mol of monatomic Xenon-131 (Xe) gas (molar mass 131.3 g mol⁻¹) is sealed inside a semiconductor lithography purge canister of constant volume 0.075 m³ at 310 K. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) p = nRT / V = (0.25 × 8.31 × 310) / 0.075 = 8.59 × 10³ Pa. (b) Single-atom mass m = M / N_A = 0 kg. (c) Density ρ = nM / V = 0.438 kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes Kelvin temperature into p = nRT / V.
Converts molar mass to kg mol⁻¹ and divides by Avogadro constant.
Evaluates ρ = nM / V in SI units.

parts.prompt: Calculate the pressure exerted by the gas on the walls of the vessel.
Determine the mass of a single Xenon-131 (Xe) atom in kilograms.
Calculate the macroscopic density of the gas inside the vessel.

items.stem: Inside a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity, 1.2 mol of ideal gas starts in state A (1.1 × 10⁵ Pa, 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³). As plotted on the volume–temperature (V–T) axes, the gas first expands at constant pressure to V_B = 7.5 × 10⁻³ m³ (state B) and is then heated at constant volume to P_C = 1.54 × 10⁵ Pa (state C). Use R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) T_A = P_A V_A / (nR) = 33.1 K. (b) Isobaric expansion gives T_B = T_A (V_B / V_A) = 82.7 K. (c) Isochoric heating gives T_C = T_B (P_C / P_A) = 116 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies V_B / T_B = V_A / T_A or P_A V_B / (nR).
Applies P_C / T_C = P_B / T_B or P_C V_B / (nR).

parts.prompt: Calculate the initial temperature T_A of the gas in state A.
Determine the temperature T_B at the end of the isobaric expansion A → B.
workingSteps: By Charles's law at constant pressure, T_B = T_A (V_B / V_A) = 82.7 K.

parts.prompt: Calculate the final temperature T_C in state C after the isochoric stage B → C.
workingSteps: At constant volume V_C = V_B, T_C = T_B (P_C / P_B) = (1.54 × 10⁵ × 7.5 × 10⁻³) / (1.2 × 8.31) = 116 K.

items.stem: Inside a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder, 0.5 mol of an ideal monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) is thermally insulated from its surroundings and undergoes a reversible adiabatic expansion from state A (P_A = 4.8 × 10⁵ Pa, V_A = 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B of volume V_B = 9.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses T_B = P_B V_B / (nR) or T_A (V_A / V_B)^(2/3).
Sets Q = 0 and evaluates |(3/2)(P_B V_B − P_A V_A)|.

parts.prompt: Calculate the final pressure P_B of the gas in state B.
Determine the absolute temperature T_B of the gas in state B.
Using the first law of thermodynamics, calculate the work done by the gas (taking work done by the gas as positive) during A → B.

items.stem: Inside a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder, 1 mol of monatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) completes the three-step cycle A → B → C → A shown on the P–V diagram: reversible adiabatic expansion from A (4.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to V_B = 7.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at B, isobaric compression at P_B back to V_C = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at C, and isochoric heating from C back to A. Take work done by the gas as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) Adiabatic relation gives P_B = 7.21 × 10⁴ Pa. (b) Isochoric heat input Q_in = 1.42 × 10³ J. (c) By cyclic energy conservation ΔU_cycle = 0, W_net = Q_in − Q_out = 516 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P V^(5/3) = const along A → B.
Uses Q_in = (3/2) ΔP V on the isochoric heating leg.
Evaluates W_net = Q_in − Q_out (or sums leg works).

parts.prompt: Calculate the pressure P_B of the gas at state B.
Calculate the thermal energy Q_in absorbed by the gas during the isochoric heating leg.
workingSteps: On C → A (constant V = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³, P_C = P_B), Q_in = ΔU_CA = (3/2)(P_A − P_B) V_A = 1.42 × 10³ J.

parts.prompt: Determine the net mechanical work W_net done by the gas per cycle.
workingSteps: Heat rejected on isobaric leg B → C is Q_out = (5/2) P_B (V_B − V_C) = 901.4 J; W_net = Q_in − Q_out = 516 J.

items.stem: A 0.16 kg copper cup (specific heat 385 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) inside a lagged benchtop thermal-equilibrium chamber contains 0.72 kg of ethanol (2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) equilibrated at 294 K. Engineers transfer a 0.18 kg glass sample (840 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 510 K into the liquid with zero external heat loss.
items.workedSolution: (a) Solving the enthalpy balance yields T_eq = 311 K. (b) Heat released by the hot solid Q_lost = m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = 3.02 × 10⁴ J. (c) Heat gained by the ethanol Q_liq = m_l c_liq (T_eq − T_l) = 2.91 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Sets up full calorimetry heat-balance equation.

items.stem: A sample of 1.5 mol of Neon-20 (Ne) (molar mass 0.0202 kg mol⁻¹) occupies 0.015 m³ within an ion-propulsion xenon feed manifold. The solid curve shows its speed distribution at T₁ = 410 K and the dashed curve at T₂ = 1025 K (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²)).

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_rms = √(3RT₁ / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹.
Scales v_rms by √(T₂ / T₁) or re-evaluates √(3RT₂ / M).

parts.prompt: Calculate the root-mean-square speed v_rms of the Neon-20 (Ne) atoms at T₁ = 410 K.
Calculate the gas pressure inside the vessel at T₁ = 410 K.
Determine the new root-mean-square speed of the atoms when heated to T₂ = 1025 K.

items.stem: A sealed sample of 0.4 mol of monatomic ideal gas in an insulated aerospace gas-accumulator cylinder follows path A → B → C on the P–V diagram: state A is at (2.4 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³), state B is at (6.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³), and state C is at (6.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 3.3 × 10⁻³ m³). Use the convention where work done by the gas is positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) Work is done only along B → C: W_by = 6.0 × 10⁵(3.3 × 10⁻³ − 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.08 × 10³ J. (b) ΔU_AC = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A) = 2.43 × 10³ J. (c) Total heat supplied Q = ΔU_AC + W_by = 3.51 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies W_AB = 0 and computes P_B(V_C − V_B).
Sums ΔU_AC and W_by to obtain total heat supplied.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical work done by the gas along path A → B → C.
Calculate the total change in internal energy ΔU of the monatomic gas between state A and state C.
workingSteps: For a monatomic ideal gas, U = (3/2) PV, so ΔU_AC = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A).

parts.prompt: Determine the total thermal energy Q supplied to the gas over the complete path A → B → C.
workingSteps: By the first law of thermodynamics, Q = ΔU_AC + W_by = 2.430 × 10³ + 1.080 × 10³ = 3.51 × 10³ J.

items.stem: Inside a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell immersed in a constant-temperature bath at 450 K, 1.6 mol of an ideal monatomic gas expands reversibly along isotherm A → B from V_A = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and expansion work done by the gas as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) P_B = nRT / V_B = 1.20 × 10⁶ Pa. (b) W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 4.15 × 10³ J. (c) Since ΔU = 0, Q = W_by and ΔS = Q / T = 9.22 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses ΔS = Q / T with Q = W_by.

parts.prompt: Calculate the final pressure P_B of the gas in state B.
Calculate the work done by the gas during the reversible isothermal expansion A → B.
Determine the change in entropy ΔS of the gas during A → B.
workingSteps: Since ΔU = 0 for an ideal gas isotherm, Q = W_by.

items.stem: In a sealed industrial distillation reboiler test cell, 0.85 kg of ethanol is heated continuously from 184 K in the liquid state to 396 K in the vapour state across its boiling point at 351 K. Use c_liquid = 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_vapour = 1600 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, and specific latent heat of vaporization L_v = 8.46 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) Q_sens = m c_liquid ΔT₁ + m c_vapour ΔT₂ = 4.08 × 10⁵ J. (b) Plateau latent energy Q_lat = m L = 7.19 × 10⁵ J. (c) Total thermal energy Q_total = Q_sens + Q_lat = 1.13 × 10⁶ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates m c₁ ΔT₁ + m c₂ ΔT₂.
Evaluates m L on the phase-change plateau.

items.stem: Engineers monitor 2.8 mol of Neon-20 (Ne) (M = 0.0202 kg mol⁻¹) confined within a thick-walled titanium deep-sea pressure housing of volume 0.06 m³ at an equilibrium temperature of 380 K (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹).
items.workedSolution: (a) p = nRT / V = (2.8 × 8.31 × 380) / 0.06 = 1.47 × 10⁵ Pa. (b) Single-atom mass m = M / N_A = 0 kg. (c) Density ρ = nM / V = 0.943 kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes Kelvin temperature into p = nRT / V.
Converts molar mass to kg mol⁻¹ and divides by Avogadro constant.
Evaluates ρ = nM / V in SI units.

items.stem: Within a laser-interferometer gas-cell enclosure, low-pressure monatomic Krypton-84 (Kr) gas (M = 0.0838 kg mol⁻¹) is held at 370 K. Data: k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹, 1 eV = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) E_k,avg = (3/2) k_B T = 0 J. (b) Dividing by 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C gives 0.0479 eV. (c) v_rms = √(3RT / M) = 332 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_k = (3/2) k_B T in kelvin.
Divides energy in joules by elementary charge e.

parts.prompt: Calculate the mean translational kinetic energy of a single atom in joules.

Determine the root-mean-square speed of the Krypton-84 (Kr) atoms.

items.stem: In a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder, 1 mol of an ideal monatomic gas undergoes the clockwise closed heat-engine cycle A → B → C → D → A: isobaric expansion A → B at 2.5 × 10⁵ Pa from 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 0.01 m³, isochoric cooling B → C to 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa, isobaric compression C → D at 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa back to 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³, and isochoric heating D → A to 2.5 × 10⁵ Pa. Take work done by the gas as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = 900 J. (b) Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min + (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 4.65 × 10³ J. (c) η = W_net / Q_in = 0.194.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates enclosed loop area (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min).
Identifies heat input on both D → A (isochoric) and A → B (isobaric).
Uses monatomic factors (3/2) on D → A and (5/2) on A → B.
Divides W_net from (a) by Q_in from (b).

parts.prompt: Calculate the net mechanical work W_net done by the gas in one complete cycle.
Calculate the total thermal energy Q_in supplied to the monatomic gas during the heating stages D → A and A → B.
Determine the thermal efficiency η of this cycle.

items.stem: A reversible Carnot heat engine in a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder uses 0.3 mol of an ideal monatomic gas operating between a hot reservoir at 527 °C and a cold sink at 67 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). During the hot isothermal expansion A → B, the gas expands from V_A = 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and net work done by the gas as positive.

markScheme.criterion: Converts temperatures to kelvin and applies 1 − T_C / T_H.
Multiplies η by Q_H (or evaluates Q_H − Q_C).

parts.prompt: Calculate the thermal efficiency η of the Carnot cycle.
Calculate the thermal energy Q_H absorbed from the hot reservoir during the isothermal expansion A → B.
Determine the net mechanical work W_net done by the gas per cycle.

items.stem: The recorded temperature–time trace tracks 0.2 kg of aluminium inside a precision constant-flux heating chamber between 906 K and 959 K while an electrical immersion heater of input power 900 W and thermal transfer efficiency 0.9 supplies energy (T_m = 933.5 K, L_f = 3.97 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹, c_s = 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_l = 1180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹).
items.workedSolution: (a) P_eff = η P = 810 W. (b) Δt_f = m L_f / P_eff = 98.0 s. (c) Total energy Q_total = 9.037 × 10⁴ J, giving t_total = Q_total / P_eff = 112 s.

markScheme.criterion: Multiplies heater power P by efficiency η.
Computes Q_total and divides by P_eff.

items.stem: Modelled as an ideal blackbody (emissivity = 1), an incandescent refractory-metal calibration sphere has radiating surface area 1.8 × 10¹⁸ m² and surface temperature 8800 K. Its thermal spectrum is shown in the figure, and a detector is positioned at distance d = 6.8 × 10¹¹ m. Take b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴.
items.workedSolution: (a) λ_max = b / T = 3.30 × 10⁻⁷ m. (b) P = σ A T⁴ = 6.12 × 10²⁶ W. (c) I = P / (4π d²) = 105 W m⁻².

Use R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²).

items.stem: Inside a variable-volume optical pressure cell, 1.5 mol of monatomic ideal gas undergoes two sequential processes plotted on the P–V graph: isochoric heating from A (1.2 × 10⁵ Pa, 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to B (2.4 × 10⁵ Pa, 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³), followed by isobaric expansion to C (2.4 × 10⁵ Pa, 0.0112 m³). items.workedSolution: (a) Work is done only along B → C: W_by = 2.4 × 10⁵(0.0112 − 3.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.85 × 10³ J. (b) ΔU_AC = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A) = 3.40 × 10³ J. (c) Total heat supplied Q = ΔU_AC + W_by = 5.25 × 10³ J.

parts.prompt: Determine the total thermal energy Q supplied to the gas over the complete path A → B → C.

items.stem: Inside a frictionless piston-cylinder assembly on a thermodynamics test bench, 0.25 mol of monatomic ideal gas undergoes two sequential processes plotted on the P–V graph: isochoric heating from A (2.4 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to B (3.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³), followed by isobaric expansion to C (3.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 3.9 × 10⁻³ m³). Take work done by the gas and heat transferred into the gas as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) Work is done only along B → C: W_by = 3.6 × 10⁵(3.9 × 10⁻³ − 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 864 J. (b) ΔU_AC = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A) = 1.57 × 10³ J. (c) Total heat supplied Q = ΔU_AC + W_by = 2.43 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies W_AB = 0 and computes P_B(V_C − V_B).
Sums ΔU_AC and W_by to obtain total heat supplied.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical work done by the gas along path A → B → C.
Calculate the total change in internal energy ΔU of the monatomic gas between state A and state C.
workingSteps: For a monatomic ideal gas, U = (3/2) PV, so ΔU_AC = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A).

parts.prompt: Determine the total thermal energy Q supplied to the gas over the complete path A → B → C.
workingSteps: By the first law of thermodynamics, Q = ΔU_AC + W_by = 1.566 × 10³ + 864.0 = 2.43 × 10³ J.

items.stem: Coupled thermally to a 310 K reservoir, 1.2 mol of ideal gas confined in a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals expands slowly from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ at A to 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³ at B (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹; define work done by the gas as positive).
items.workedSolution: (a) P_B = nRT / V_B = 5.15 × 10⁵ Pa. (b) W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 3.40 × 10³ J. (c) Since ΔU = 0, Q = W_by and ΔS = Q / T = 11.0 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses ΔS = Q / T with Q = W_by.

parts.prompt: Calculate the final pressure P_B of the gas in state B.
Calculate the work done by the gas during the reversible isothermal expansion A → B.
Determine the change in entropy ΔS of the gas during A → B.
workingSteps: Since ΔU = 0 for an ideal gas isotherm, Q = W_by.

items.stem: The heating curve shows how the temperature of a 0.45 kg sample of pure lead in an adiabatic micro-calorimeter ampoule varies with thermal energy supplied from 561 K (solid) to 646 K (liquid). Data for lead: melting point = 600.6 K, c_solid = 128 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 147 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, and specific latent heat of fusion L_f = 2.3 × 10⁴ J kg⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) Q_sens = m c_solid ΔT₁ + m c_liquid ΔT₂ = 5.28 × 10³ J. (b) Plateau latent energy Q_lat = m L = 1.04 × 10⁴ J. (c) Total thermal energy Q_total = Q_sens + Q_lat = 1.56 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates m c₁ ΔT₁ + m c₂ ΔT₂.
Evaluates m L on the phase-change plateau.

items.stem: During a latent-heat experiment in a well-insulated copper-lined laboratory calorimeter, 0.035 kg of cold ice (268.15 K, c = 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) melts completely after immersion in 0.68 kg of water (348.15 K, c = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹), with T_m = 273.15 K, L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹, and zero heat loss to the room.
items.workedSolution: (a) Q_lat = m_ice L_f = 1.17 × 10⁴ J. (b) Full enthalpy balance yields T_eq = 340 K. (c) Heat released by warm water = 2.19 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Balances ice warming, melting, and meltwater warming against warm water cooling.

parts.prompt: Calculate the latent thermal energy required solely to melt all the ice once it reaches 273.15 K.
Calculate the final thermal equilibrium temperature T_eq of the water.
workingSteps: m_water c_water (348.15 − T_eq) = m_ice c_ice (273.15 − 268.15) + Q_lat + m_ice c_water (T_eq − 273.15).

parts.prompt: Determine the total thermal energy released by the initially warm water.

items.stem: Within a laser-interferometer gas-cell enclosure (fixed capacity 0.016 m³), 2.2 mol of pure Neon-20 (Ne) gas with molar mass 20.2 g mol⁻¹ rests in thermal equilibrium at 87 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) p = nRT / V = (2.2 × 8.31 × 360.15) / 0.016 = 4.12 × 10⁵ Pa. (b) Single-atom mass m = M / N_A = 0 kg. (c) Density ρ = nM / V = 2.78 kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes Kelvin temperature into p = nRT / V.
Converts molar mass to kg mol⁻¹ and divides by Avogadro constant.
Evaluates ρ = nM / V in SI units.

items.stem: Within a semiconductor lithography purge canister, low-pressure monatomic Krypton-84 (Kr) gas (M = 0.0838 kg mol⁻¹) is held at 440 K. Data: k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹, 1 eV = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) E_k,avg = (3/2) k_B T = 0 J. (b) Dividing by 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C gives 0.0569 eV. (c) v_rms = √(3RT / M) = 362 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_k = (3/2) k_B T in kelvin.
Divides energy in joules by elementary charge e.

items.stem: The diagram illustrates a reversible rectangular heat-engine cycle A → B → C → D → A executed by 0.2 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a precision pneumatic actuator chamber sealed with a movable piston, operating between P_low = 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa and P_high = 3.6 × 10⁵ Pa and between V_min = 1.8 × 10⁻³ m³ and V_max = 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³. Take expansion work by the gas as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = 648 J. (b) Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min + (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 3.08 × 10³ J. (c) η = W_net / Q_in = 0.211.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates enclosed loop area (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min).
Identifies heat input on both D → A (isochoric) and A → B (isobaric).
Uses monatomic factors (3/2) on D → A and (5/2) on A → B.
Divides W_net from (a) by Q_in from (b).

Multiplies η by Q_H (or evaluates Q_H − Q_C).

parts.prompt: Calculate the thermal efficiency η of the Carnot cycle.
Calculate the thermal energy Q_H absorbed from the hot reservoir during the isothermal expansion A → B.
Determine the net mechanical work W_net done by the gas per cycle.

items.stem: In an enthalpy-rate experiment using a guarded electrical immersion-heating vessel, an electrical immersion heater of input power 900 W and thermal transfer efficiency 0.75 supplies energy on a 0.75 kg sample of aluminium, changing its temperature from 896 K to 959 K across its 933.5 K phase boundary. Adopt c_solid = 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 1180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, and L_f = 3.97 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) P_eff = η P = 675 W. (b) Δt_f = m L_f / P_eff = 441 s. (c) Total energy Q_total = 3.456 × 10⁵ J, giving t_total = Q_total / P_eff = 512 s.

markScheme.criterion: Multiplies heater power P by efficiency η.
Computes Q_total and divides by P_eff.
