items.stem: The P–V diagram shows 0.4 mol of an ideal monatomic gas in a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder taken from state A (1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B (3.75 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³) at constant volume, and then from state B to state C (3.75 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³) at constant pressure. Throughout this question, take expansion work done by the gas and thermal energy supplied to the gas as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) Work is done only along B → C: W_by = 3.75 × 10⁵(4.5 × 10⁻³ − 2.5 × 10⁻³) = 750 J. (b) ΔU_AC = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A) = 1.97 × 10³ J. (c) Total heat supplied Q = ΔU_AC + W_by = 2.72 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies W_AB = 0 and computes P_B(V_C − V_B).
Sums ΔU_AC and W_by to obtain total heat supplied.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical work done by the gas along path A → B → C.
Calculate the total change in internal energy ΔU of the monatomic gas between state A and state C.
workingSteps: For a monatomic ideal gas, U = (3/2) PV, so ΔU_AC = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A).

parts.prompt: Determine the total thermal energy Q supplied to the gas over the complete path A → B → C.
workingSteps: By the first law of thermodynamics, Q = ΔU_AC + W_by = 1.969 × 10³ + 750.0 = 2.72 × 10³ J.

items.stem: The P–V graph shows an adiabatic path A → B for 0.25 mol of monatomic ideal gas (adiabatic exponent γ = 5/3) confined in a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals. At state A, the pressure is 3.2 × 10⁵ Pa and the volume is 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³; at state B, the volume is 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹).

markScheme.criterion: Uses T_B = P_B V_B / (nR) or T_A (V_A / V_B)^(2/3).
Sets Q = 0 and evaluates |(3/2)(P_B V_B − P_A V_A)|.

parts.prompt: Calculate the final pressure P_B of the gas in state B.
Determine the absolute temperature T_B of the gas in state B.
Using the first law of thermodynamics, calculate the work done by the gas (taking work done by the gas as positive) during A → B.

items.stem: On the P–V diagram for a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder, 1.2 mol of ideal monatomic gas (adiabatic index 5/3) undergoes adiabatic expansion A → B from (5.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to 0.01 m³, followed by isobaric compression B → C to 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ and isochoric regeneration C → A. Adopt positive work for expansion by the gas.
items.workedSolution: (a) Adiabatic relation gives P_B = 5.46 × 10⁴ Pa. (b) Isochoric heat input Q_in = 1.86 × 10³ J. (c) By cyclic energy conservation ΔU_cycle = 0, W_net = Q_in − Q_out = 835 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P V^(5/3) = const along A → B.
Uses Q_in = (3/2) ΔP V on the isochoric heating leg.
Evaluates W_net = Q_in − Q_out (or sums leg works).

parts.prompt: Calculate the pressure P_B of the gas at state B.
Calculate the thermal energy Q_in absorbed by the gas during the isochoric heating leg.
workingSteps: On C → A (constant V = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³, P_C = P_B), Q_in = ΔU_CA = (3/2)(P_A − P_B) V_A = 1.86 × 10³ J.

parts.prompt: Determine the net mechanical work W_net done by the gas per cycle.
workingSteps: Heat rejected on isobaric leg B → C is Q_out = (5/2) P_B (V_B − V_C) = 1.023 × 10³ J; W_net = Q_in − Q_out = 835 J.

items.stem: Inside a thick-walled cork-lagged enthalpy cell, a copper calorimeter vessel of mass 0.16 kg (c_cup = 385 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) holds 0.55 kg of water (c_liq = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹), both initially at 294 K. A 0.28 kg iron block (c_s = 450 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 440 K is lowered into the bath; heat loss to the outside air is negligible.
items.workedSolution: (a) Solving the enthalpy balance yields T_eq = 301 K. (b) Heat released by the hot solid Q_lost = m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = 1.75 × 10⁴ J. (c) Heat gained by the water Q_liq = m_l c_liq (T_eq − T_l) = 1.70 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Sets up full calorimetry heat-balance equation.

workingSteps: m_s c_s (440 − T_eq) = (m_l c_liq + m_cup c_cup)(T_eq − 294).

parts.prompt: Calculate the thermal energy released by the iron block.
Determine the thermal energy absorbed specifically by the water.

items.stem: In an infrared energy-balance investigation, a deep-space probe aluminium-kapton radiator fin of surface area 12 m² and greybody emissivity e = 0.92 has a uniform temperature of 298 K while exchanging radiation with an ambient environment at 240 K. Take b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴.
items.workedSolution: (a) λ_max = b / T = 9.73 × 10⁻⁶ m. (b) Gross emitted power P_emitted = e σ A T⁴ = 4.94 × 10³ W. (c) Net radiative loss P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) = 2.86 × 10³ W.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_emitted = e σ A T⁴.

parts.prompt: Calculate the peak infrared wavelength λ_max emitted by the surface.
Calculate the gross thermal power emitted by the greybody surface.
Determine the net rate of radiative thermal energy loss to the 240 K surroundings.
workingSteps: P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) = 2.86 × 10³ W.

items.stem: Optical Doppler broadening probes Helium-4 (He) gas (molar mass 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹) equilibrated at 57 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15) inside a thick-walled titanium deep-sea pressure housing (k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹).
items.workedSolution: (a) E_k,avg = (3/2) k_B T = 0 J. (b) Dividing by 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C gives 0.0427 eV. (c) v_rms = √(3RT / M) = 1.43 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_k = (3/2) k_B T in kelvin.
Divides energy in joules by elementary charge e.

parts.prompt: Calculate the mean translational kinetic energy of a single atom in joules.
Convert this mean translational kinetic energy into electronvolts.
Determine the root-mean-square speed of the Helium-4 (He) atoms.

items.stem: A closed-loop test cylinder (a cryocooler compression cylinder containing monatomic working gas) carries 0.2 mol of monatomic ideal gas clockwise around cycle A → B → C → D → A between volume limits 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³ and 0.012 m³ and pressure limits 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa and 3.75 × 10⁵ Pa (with A at 3.75 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³ and B at 3.75 × 10⁵ Pa, 0.012 m³). Define work done by the gas as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = 1.80 × 10³ J. (b) Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min + (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 8.85 × 10³ J. (c) η = W_net / Q_in = 0.203.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates enclosed loop area (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min).
Identifies heat input on both D → A (isochoric) and A → B (isobaric).
Uses monatomic factors (3/2) on D → A and (5/2) on A → B.
Divides W_net from (a) by Q_in from (b).

parts.prompt: Calculate the net mechanical work W_net done by the gas in one complete cycle.
Calculate the total thermal energy Q_in supplied to the monatomic gas during the heating stages D → A and A → B.
Determine the thermal efficiency η of this cycle.

items.stem: A reversible Carnot heat engine in a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder uses 1.4 mol of an ideal monatomic gas operating between a hot reservoir at 427 °C and a cold sink at 67 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). During the hot isothermal expansion A → B, the gas expands from V_A = 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and net work done by the gas as positive.

markScheme.criterion: Converts temperatures to kelvin and applies 1 − T_C / T_H.
Multiplies η by Q_H (or evaluates Q_H − Q_C).

parts.prompt: Calculate the thermal efficiency η of the Carnot cycle.
Calculate the thermal energy Q_H absorbed from the hot reservoir during the isothermal expansion A → B.
Determine the net mechanical work W_net done by the gas per cycle.

items.stem: Thermal analysis of 0.15 kg of ethanol in a high-purity zone-refining crucible records the three-segment temperature–energy profile from 139 K to 244 K (melting point 159 K; c_solid = 1120 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹; c_liquid = 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹; specific latent heat of fusion L_f = 1.08 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹).
items.workedSolution: (a) Q_sens = m c_solid ΔT₁ + m c_liquid ΔT₂ = 3.45 × 10⁴ J. (b) Plateau latent energy Q_lat = m L = 1.62 × 10⁴ J. (c) Total thermal energy Q_total = Q_sens + Q_lat = 5.07 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates m c₁ ΔT₁ + m c₂ ΔT₂.
Evaluates m L on the phase-change plateau.

items.stem: Zero heat enters a precision isothermal-jacket mixing cup while 0.24 kg of water initially at 301.15 K equilibrates against 0.18 kg of 273.15 K ice (4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ for liquid water; L_f = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹).

items.stem: Engineers monitor 0.35 mol of Xenon-131 (Xe) (M = 131.3 g mol⁻¹) confined within an orbital satellite attitude-control propellant cylinder of volume 0.045 m³ at an equilibrium temperature of 340 K (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹).
items.workedSolution: (a) p = nRT / V = (0.35 × 8.31 × 340) / 0.045 = 2.20 × 10⁴ Pa. (b) Single-atom mass m = M / N_A = 0 kg. (c) Density ρ = nM / V = 1.02 kg m⁻³.

items.stem: An ideal gas sample (1.5 mol) confined in a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder is taken from state A (1.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B (0.0132 m³) isobarically, and then from state B to state C (2.56 × 10⁵ Pa) isochorically, as illustrated on the pressure–volume (P–V) graph (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹).
items.workedSolution: (a) T_A = P_A V_A / (nR) = 77.0 K. (b) Isobaric expansion gives T_B = T_A (V_B / V_A) = 169 K. (c) Isochoric heating gives T_C = T_B (P_C / P_A) = 271 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies V_B / T_B = V_A / T_A or P_A V_B / (nR).

parts.prompt: Calculate the initial temperature T_A of the gas in state A.
Determine the temperature T_B at the end of the isobaric expansion A → B.
workingSteps: By Charles's law at constant pressure, T_B = T_A (V_B / V_A) = 169 K.

parts.prompt: Calculate the final temperature T_C in state C after the isochoric stage B → C.
workingSteps: At constant volume V_C = V_B, T_C = T_B (P_C / P_B) = (2.56 × 10⁵ × 0.0132) / (1.5 × 8.31) = 271 K.

items.stem: The P–V graph shows an adiabatic path A → B for 0.4 mol of monatomic ideal gas (adiabatic exponent γ = 5/3) confined in a closed noble-gas power-conversion loop. At state A, the pressure is 1.4 × 10⁵ Pa and the volume is 4.2 × 10⁻³ m³; at state B, the volume is 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹).

markScheme.criterion: Uses T_B = P_B V_B / (nR) or T_A (V_A / V_B)^(2/3).
Sets Q = 0 and evaluates |(3/2)(P_B V_B − P_A V_A)|.

parts.prompt: Calculate the final pressure P_B of the gas in state B.
Determine the absolute temperature T_B of the gas in state B.

items.stem: Inside a frictionless piston-cylinder assembly on a thermodynamics test bench, 0.25 mol of monatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) completes the three-step cycle A → B → C → A shown on the P–V diagram: reversible adiabatic expansion from A (5.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³) to V_B = 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ at B, isobaric compression at P_B back to V_C = 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ at C, and isochoric heating from C back to A. Take work done by the gas as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) Adiabatic relation gives P_B = 1.19 × 10⁵ Pa. (b) Isochoric heat input Q_in = 775 J. (c) By cyclic energy conservation ΔU_cycle = 0, W_net = Q_in − Q_out = 238 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P V^(5/3) = const along A → B.
Uses Q_in = (3/2) ΔP V on the isochoric heating leg.
Evaluates W_net = Q_in − Q_out (or sums leg works).

parts.prompt: Calculate the pressure P_B of the gas at state B.
Calculate the thermal energy Q_in absorbed by the gas during the isochoric heating leg.
workingSteps: On C → A (constant V = 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³, P_C = P_B), Q_in = ΔU_CA = (3/2)(P_A − P_B) V_A = 775 J.

parts.prompt: Determine the net mechanical work W_net done by the gas per cycle.
workingSteps: Heat rejected on isobaric leg B → C is Q_out = (5/2) P_B (V_B − V_C) = 537.5 J; W_net = Q_in − Q_out = 238 J.

items.stem: Inside a well-insulated copper-lined laboratory calorimeter, 0.32 kg of mineral oil (specific heat 1960 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 298 K quenches a 0.18 kg piece of glass (840 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 510 K; 650 J leaks to the ambient air before equilibrium is reached.
items.workedSolution: (a) Solving the enthalpy balance yields T_eq = 338 K. (b) Heat released by the hot solid Q_lost = m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = 2.60 × 10⁴ J. (c) Heat gained by the mineral oil Q_liq = m_l c_liq (T_eq − T_l) = 2.53 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Sets up full calorimetry heat-balance equation.

Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²).

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_rms = √(3RT₁ / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹.

items.stem: The P–V diagram shows 1.2 mol of an ideal monatomic gas in a cryocooler compression cylinder containing monatomic working gas taken from state A (1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B (4.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³) at constant volume, and then from state B to state C (4.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 6.5 × 10⁻³ m³) at constant pressure. Throughout this question, take expansion work done by the gas and thermal energy supplied to the gas as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) Work is done only along B → C: W_by = 4.5 × 10⁵(6.5 × 10⁻³ − 2.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.80 × 10³ J. (b) ΔU_AC = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A) = 3.82 × 10³ J. (c) Total heat supplied Q = ΔU_AC + W_by = 5.62 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies W_AB = 0 and computes P_B(V_C − V_B).
Sums ΔU_AC and W_by to obtain total heat supplied.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical work done by the gas along path A → B → C.
Calculate the total change in internal energy ΔU of the monatomic gas between state A and state C.
workingSteps: For a monatomic ideal gas, U = (3/2) PV, so ΔU_AC = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A).

parts.prompt: Determine the total thermal energy Q supplied to the gas over the complete path A → B → C.
workingSteps: By the first law of thermodynamics, Q = ΔU_AC + W_by = 3.825 × 10³ + 1.800 × 10³ = 5.62 × 10³ J.

items.stem: At fixed temperature T = 600 K, 0.85 mol of ideal gas inside a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber follows reversible isothermal curve A → B from 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³. Adopt R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and positive expansion work by the gas.
items.workedSolution: (a) P_B = nRT / V_B = 9.42 × 10⁵ Pa. (b) W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 4.66 × 10³ J. (c) Since ΔU = 0, Q = W_by and ΔS = Q / T = 7.76 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses ΔS = Q / T with Q = W_by.

parts.prompt: Calculate the final pressure P_B of the gas in state B.
Calculate the work done by the gas during the reversible isothermal expansion A → B.
Determine the change in entropy ΔS of the gas during A → B.
workingSteps: Since ΔU = 0 for an ideal gas isotherm, Q = W_by.

items.stem: The heating curve shows how the temperature of a 0.45 kg sample of pure aluminium in a lagged laboratory phase-transition calorimeter varies with thermal energy supplied from 894 K (solid) to 964 K (liquid). Data for aluminium: melting point = 933.5 K, c_solid = 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 1180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, and specific latent heat of fusion L_f = 3.97 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) Q_sens = m c_solid ΔT₁ + m c_liquid ΔT₂ = 3.22 × 10⁴ J. (b) Plateau latent energy Q_lat = m L = 1.79 × 10⁵ J. (c) Total thermal energy Q_total = Q_sens + Q_lat = 2.11 × 10⁵ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates m c₁ ΔT₁ + m c₂ ΔT₂.
Evaluates m L on the phase-change plateau.

items.workedSolution: (a) p = nRT / V = (0.45 × 8.31 × 310) / 0.024 = 4.83 × 10⁴ Pa. (b) Single-atom mass m = M / N_A = 0 kg. (c) Density ρ = nM / V = 0.379 kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes Kelvin temperature into p = nRT / V.
Converts molar mass to kg mol⁻¹ and divides by Avogadro constant.
Evaluates ρ = nM / V in SI units.

parts.prompt: Calculate the pressure exerted by the gas on the walls of the vessel.
Determine the mass of a single Neon-20 (Ne) atom in kilograms.
Calculate the macroscopic density of the gas inside the vessel.

items.stem: Optical Doppler broadening probes Krypton-84 (Kr) gas (molar mass 0.0838 kg mol⁻¹) equilibrated at 97 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15) inside a sealed borosilicate acoustic-thermometry sphere (k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹).
items.workedSolution: (a) E_k,avg = (3/2) k_B T = 0 J. (b) Dividing by 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C gives 0.0479 eV. (c) v_rms = √(3RT / M) = 332 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_k = (3/2) k_B T in kelvin.
Divides energy in joules by elementary charge e.

parts.prompt: Calculate the mean translational kinetic energy of a single atom in joules.
Convert this mean translational kinetic energy into electronvolts.
Determine the root-mean-square speed of the Krypton-84 (Kr) atoms.

items.stem: A closed-loop test cylinder (a closed noble-gas power-conversion loop) carries 0.2 mol of monatomic ideal gas clockwise around cycle A → B → C → D → A between volume limits 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ and 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³ and pressure limits 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa and 3.6 × 10⁵ Pa (with A at 3.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ and B at 3.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³). Define work done by the gas as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = 648 J. (b) Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min + (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 3.56 × 10³ J. (c) η = W_net / Q_in = 0.182.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates enclosed loop area (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min).
Identifies heat input on both D → A (isochoric) and A → B (isobaric).
Uses monatomic factors (3/2) on D → A and (5/2) on A → B.
Divides W_net from (a) by Q_in from (b).

parts.prompt: Calculate the net mechanical work W_net done by the gas in one complete cycle.
Calculate the total thermal energy Q_in supplied to the monatomic gas during the heating stages D → A and A → B.
Determine the thermal efficiency η of this cycle.

items.stem: Operating between a hot reservoir at 703 K and a cold sink at 380 K, 0.5 mol of ideal gas in a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell executes an ideal Carnot power cycle whose high-temperature isothermal leg A → B expands from 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ to 4.2 × 10⁻³ m³. Use R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and take work done by the gas as positive.

markScheme.criterion: Converts temperatures to kelvin and applies 1 − T_C / T_H.
Multiplies η by Q_H (or evaluates Q_H − Q_C).

parts.prompt: Calculate the thermal efficiency η of the Carnot cycle.
Calculate the thermal energy Q_H absorbed from the hot reservoir during the isothermal expansion A → B.
Determine the net mechanical work W_net done by the gas per cycle.

items.stem: Inside a sealed industrial distillation reboiler test cell, an electrical immersion heater of input power 1600 W and thermal transfer efficiency 0.8 supplies energy while a 0.4 kg sample of ethanol transitions from 121 K to 199 K as plotted on the temperature–time graph. Use melting point T_m = 159 K, c_solid = 1120 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, c_liquid = 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, and L_f = 1.08 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) P_eff = η P = 1.28 × 10³ W. (b) Δt_f = m L_f / P_eff = 33.8 s. (c) Total energy Q_total = 9.926 × 10⁴ J, giving t_total = Q_total / P_eff = 77.5 s.

markScheme.criterion: Multiplies heater power P by efficiency η.
Computes Q_total and divides by P_eff.

parts.prompt: Calculate the effective rate of thermal energy transfer P_eff to/from the ethanol sample.
Calculate the duration of the isothermal melting plateau at 159 K.
Determine the total time required for the temperature to change from 121 K to 199 K.
workingSteps: Q_total = m c_solid (159 − 121) + m L_f + m c_liquid (199 − 159) = 9.926 × 10⁴ J.

items.stem: At 6200 K, a metrological Planckian reference source acts as an ideal blackbody emitter with total area 3.6 × 10¹⁸ m² illuminating an instrument aperture 4.2 × 10¹¹ m away. Adopt b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴.
items.workedSolution: (a) λ_max = b / T = 4.68 × 10⁻⁷ m. (b) P = σ A T⁴ = 3.02 × 10²⁶ W. (c) I = P / (4π d²) = 136 W m⁻².

parts.prompt: Calculate the peak emission wavelength λ_max (in metres) of the blackbody spectrum.
Calculate the total electromagnetic power radiated by the source.
Determine the radiant intensity incident on the detector at distance d = 4.2 × 10¹¹ m.

items.stem: A sample of 0.3 mol of Krypton-84 (Kr) (molar mass 0.0838 kg mol⁻¹) occupies 0.05 m³ within an ion-propulsion xenon feed manifold. The solid curve shows its speed distribution at T₁ = 410 K and the dashed curve at T₂ = 738 K (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²)).

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_rms = √(3RT₁ / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹.
Scales v_rms by √(T₂ / T₁) or re-evaluates √(3RT₂ / M).

parts.prompt: Calculate the root-mean-square speed v_rms of the Krypton-84 (Kr) atoms at T₁ = 410 K.
Calculate the gas pressure inside the vessel at T₁ = 410 K.
Determine the new root-mean-square speed of the atoms when heated to T₂ = 738 K.

items.stem: A sealed sample of 0.25 mol of monatomic ideal gas in an insulated aerospace gas-accumulator cylinder follows path A → B → C on the P–V diagram: state A is at (1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³), state B is at (3.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³), and state C is at (3.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 8.0 × 10⁻³ m³). Use the convention where work done by the gas is positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) Work is done only along B → C: W_by = 3.0 × 10⁵(8.0 × 10⁻³ − 2.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.65 × 10³ J. (b) ΔU_AC = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A) = 3.04 × 10³ J. (c) Total heat supplied Q = ΔU_AC + W_by = 4.69 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies W_AB = 0 and computes P_B(V_C − V_B).
Sums ΔU_AC and W_by to obtain total heat supplied.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical work done by the gas along path A → B → C.
Calculate the total change in internal energy ΔU of the monatomic gas between state A and state C.
workingSteps: For a monatomic ideal gas, U = (3/2) PV, so ΔU_AC = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A).

parts.prompt: Determine the total thermal energy Q supplied to the gas over the complete path A → B → C.
workingSteps: By the first law of thermodynamics, Q = ΔU_AC + W_by = 3.038 × 10³ + 1.650 × 10³ = 4.69 × 10³ J.

items.stem: The P–V graph shows an adiabatic path A → B for 0.75 mol of monatomic ideal gas (adiabatic exponent γ = 5/3) confined in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber. At state A, the pressure is 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa and the volume is 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³; at state B, the volume is 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹).
items.workedSolution: (a) P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 3.17 × 10⁵ Pa. (b) T_B = P_B V_B / (nR) = 127 K. (c) With Q = 0, W_on = ΔU = 441 J.

markScheme.criterion: Uses T_B = P_B V_B / (nR) or T_A (V_A / V_B)^(2/3).
Sets Q = 0 and evaluates |(3/2)(P_B V_B − P_A V_A)|.

parts.prompt: Calculate the final pressure P_B of the gas in state B.
Determine the absolute temperature T_B of the gas in state B.
Using the first law of thermodynamics, calculate the work done on the gas (taking work done on the gas as positive) during A → B.
workingSteps: W_on = ΔU = (3/2)(P_B V_B − P_A V_A) = 441 J.

items.stem: Engineers test 1 mol of ideal monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) in a precision pneumatic actuator chamber sealed with a movable piston over a four-stage Otto cycle starting at A (1.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³), compressing adiabatically to B (2.0 × 10⁻³ m³), heating at fixed volume to C (5.715 × 10⁵ Pa), expanding adiabatically to D (4.0 × 10⁻³ m³), and returning isochorically to A. Define expansion work by the gas as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) Adiabatic relation gives P_B = 3.17 × 10⁵ Pa. (b) Isochoric heat input Q_in = 762 J. (c) By cyclic energy conservation ΔU_cycle = 0, W_net = Q_in − Q_out = 282 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P V^(5/3) = const along A → B.
Uses Q_in = (3/2) ΔP V on the isochoric heating leg.
Evaluates W_net = Q_in − Q_out (or sums leg works).

parts.prompt: Calculate the pressure P_B of the gas at state B.
Calculate the thermal energy Q_in absorbed by the gas during the isochoric heating leg.
workingSteps: On B → C (constant V = 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³), Q_in = ΔU_BC = (3/2)(P_C − P_B) V_B = 762 J.

parts.prompt: Determine the net mechanical work W_net done by the gas per cycle.
workingSteps: P_D = P_C (V_B / V_D)^(5/3); Q_out = (3/2)(P_D − P_A) V_A = 480.0 J; W_net = Q_in − Q_out = 282 J.

items.stem: Inside a precision isothermal-jacket mixing cup, 0.32 kg of mineral oil (specific heat 1960 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 302 K quenches a 0.65 kg piece of iron (450 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 380 K; 1250 J leaks to the ambient air before equilibrium is reached.
items.workedSolution: (a) Solving the enthalpy balance yields T_eq = 325 K. (b) Heat released by the hot solid Q_lost = m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = 1.60 × 10⁴ J. (c) Heat gained by the mineral oil Q_liq = m_l c_liq (T_eq − T_l) = 1.47 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Sets up full calorimetry heat-balance equation.

parts.prompt: Calculate the final thermal equilibrium temperature T_eq of the system.
Calculate the thermal energy released by the iron block.
Determine the thermal energy absorbed specifically by the mineral oil.

items.stem: In an infrared energy-balance investigation, a dark oceanic mixed-layer surface patch of surface area 2.5 m² and greybody emissivity e = 0.78 has a uniform temperature of 343 K while exchanging radiation with an ambient environment at 268 K. Take b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴.
items.workedSolution: (a) λ_max = b / T = 8.45 × 10⁻⁶ m. (b) Gross emitted power P_emitted = e σ A T⁴ = 1.53 × 10³ W. (c) Net radiative loss P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) = 960 W.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_emitted = e σ A T⁴.

parts.prompt: Calculate the peak infrared wavelength λ_max emitted by the surface.
Calculate the gross thermal power emitted by the greybody surface.
Determine the net rate of radiative thermal energy loss to the 268 K surroundings.
workingSteps: P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) = 960 W.

items.stem: In a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder, 1.5 mol of an ideal monatomic gas undergoes the clockwise closed heat-engine cycle A → B → C → D → A: isobaric expansion A → B at 2.4 × 10⁵ Pa from 1.8 × 10⁻³ m³ to 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³, isochoric cooling B → C to 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa, isobaric compression C → D at 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa back to 1.8 × 10⁻³ m³, and isochoric heating D → A to 2.4 × 10⁵ Pa. Take work done by the gas as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = 324 J. (b) Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min + (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 1.94 × 10³ J. (c) η = W_net / Q_in = 0.167.

State A has volume 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ and state B has volume 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, work done by gas positive).

items.stem: Thermal analysis of 1.25 kg of lead in an automated cryostat sample holder records the three-segment temperature–energy profile from 561 K to 686 K (melting point 600.6 K; c_solid = 128 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹; c_liquid = 147 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹; specific latent heat of fusion L_f = 2.3 × 10⁴ J kg⁻¹).
items.workedSolution: (a) Q_sens = m c_solid ΔT₁ + m c_liquid ΔT₂ = 2.20 × 10⁴ J. (b) Plateau latent energy Q_lat = m L = 2.88 × 10⁴ J. (c) Total thermal energy Q_total = Q_sens + Q_lat = 5.08 × 10⁴ J.

Calculate the thermal energy absorbed during the isothermal phase change at 600.6 K.

items.stem: A 0.8 kg water bath at 318.15 K inside a stirred insulated immersion calorimeter receives 0.065 kg of sub-zero ice initially at 263.15 K under adiabatic conditions. Use 273.15 K for the ice point, specific heat capacities 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ (ice) and 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ (water), and fusion latent heat 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) Q_lat = m_ice L_f = 2.17 × 10⁴ J. (b) Full enthalpy balance yields T_eq = 308 K. (c) Heat released by warm water = 3.26 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Balances ice warming, melting, and meltwater warming against warm water cooling.

parts.prompt: Calculate the latent thermal energy required solely to melt all the ice once it reaches 273.15 K.
Calculate the final thermal equilibrium temperature T_eq of the water.
workingSteps: m_water c_water (318.15 − T_eq) = m_ice c_ice (273.15 − 263.15) + Q_lat + m_ice c_water (T_eq − 273.15).

parts.prompt: Determine the total thermal energy released by the initially warm water.

items.stem: Within a thermostatted noble-gas reference bulb (fixed capacity 0.075 m³), 0.65 mol of pure Xenon-131 (Xe) gas with molar mass 131.3 g mol⁻¹ rests in thermal equilibrium at 67 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) p = nRT / V = (0.65 × 8.31 × 340.15) / 0.075 = 2.45 × 10⁴ Pa. (b) Single-atom mass m = M / N_A = 0 kg. (c) Density ρ = nM / V = 1.14 kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes Kelvin temperature into p = nRT / V.
Converts molar mass to kg mol⁻¹ and divides by Avogadro constant.
Evaluates ρ = nM / V in SI units.

parts.prompt: Calculate the pressure exerted by the gas on the walls of the vessel.
Determine the mass of a single Xenon-131 (Xe) atom in kilograms.
Calculate the macroscopic density of the gas inside the vessel.

items.stem: Inside an insulated aerospace gas-accumulator cylinder, 0.35 mol of ideal gas starts in state A (2.2 × 10⁵ Pa, 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³). As plotted on the volume–temperature (V–T) axes, the gas first expands at constant pressure to V_B = 9.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (state B) and is then heated at constant volume to P_C = 3.52 × 10⁵ Pa (state C). Use R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) T_A = P_A V_A / (nR) = 454 K. (b) Isobaric expansion gives T_B = T_A (V_B / V_A) = 681 K. (c) Isochoric heating gives T_C = T_B (P_C / P_A) = 1.09 × 10³ K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies V_B / T_B = V_A / T_A or P_A V_B / (nR).
Applies P_C / T_C = P_B / T_B or P_C V_B / (nR).

parts.prompt: Calculate the initial temperature T_A of the gas in state A.
Determine the temperature T_B at the end of the isobaric expansion A → B.
workingSteps: By Charles's law at constant pressure, T_B = T_A (V_B / V_A) = 681 K.

parts.prompt: Calculate the final temperature T_C in state C after the isochoric stage B → C.

items.stem: The P–V graph shows an adiabatic path A → B for 1.5 mol of monatomic ideal gas (adiabatic exponent γ = 5/3) confined in a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell. At state A, the pressure is 7.5 × 10⁵ Pa and the volume is 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³; at state B, the volume is 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹).

markScheme.criterion: Uses T_B = P_B V_B / (nR) or T_A (V_A / V_B)^(2/3).
Sets Q = 0 and evaluates |(3/2)(P_B V_B − P_A V_A)|.

parts.prompt: Calculate the final pressure P_B of the gas in state B.
Determine the absolute temperature T_B of the gas in state B.
Using the first law of thermodynamics, calculate the work done by the gas (taking work done by the gas as positive) during A → B.

items.stem: The P–V diagram shows an idealised Otto cycle A → B → C → D → A executed by 1.2 mol of monatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) inside a cryocooler compression cylinder containing monatomic working gas. State A is at (1.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 0.01 m³). The gas is compressed adiabatically to V_B = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ (state B), heated isochorically to P_C = 2.621 × 10⁶ Pa (state C), expanded adiabatically to V_D = 0.01 m³ (state D), and cooled isochorically back to A. Take work done by the gas as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) Adiabatic relation gives P_B = 1.01 × 10⁶ Pa. (b) Isochoric heat input Q_in = 6.05 × 10³ J. (c) By cyclic energy conservation ΔU_cycle = 0, W_net = Q_in − Q_out = 3.65 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P V^(5/3) = const along A → B.
Uses Q_in = (3/2) ΔP V on the isochoric heating leg.
Evaluates W_net = Q_in − Q_out (or sums leg works).

parts.prompt: Calculate the pressure P_B of the gas at state B.
Calculate the thermal energy Q_in absorbed by the gas during the isochoric heating leg.
workingSteps: On B → C (constant V = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³), Q_in = ΔU_BC = (3/2)(P_C − P_B) V_B = 6.05 × 10³ J.

parts.prompt: Determine the net mechanical work W_net done by the gas per cycle.

items.stem: Inside a sealed foam-insulated metallurgical quench tank, a copper calorimeter vessel of mass 0.16 kg (c_cup = 385 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) holds 0.42 kg of ethanol (c_liq = 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹), both initially at 302 K. A 0.28 kg glass block (c_s = 840 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 510 K is lowered into the bath; heat loss to the outside air is negligible.
items.workedSolution: (a) Solving the enthalpy balance yields T_eq = 339 K. (b) Heat released by the hot solid Q_lost = m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = 4.02 × 10⁴ J. (c) Heat gained by the ethanol Q_liq = m_l c_liq (T_eq − T_l) = 3.79 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Sets up full calorimetry heat-balance equation.

parts.prompt: Calculate the final thermal equilibrium temperature T_eq of the system.
workingSteps: m_s c_s (510 − T_eq) = (m_l c_liq + m_cup c_cup)(T_eq − 302).

parts.prompt: Calculate the thermal energy released by the glass block.
Determine the thermal energy absorbed specifically by the ethanol.

items.stem: At 2600 K, an exoplanet host star in radiative equilibrium acts as an ideal blackbody emitter with total area 3.2 × 10⁻³ m² illuminating an instrument aperture 1.5 m away. Adopt b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴.

parts.prompt: Calculate the peak emission wavelength λ_max (in metres) of the blackbody spectrum.
Calculate the total electromagnetic power radiated by the source.
Determine the radiant intensity incident on the detector at distance d = 1.5 m.

items.stem: A sample of 2 mol of Neon-20 (Ne) (molar mass 20.2 g mol⁻¹) occupies 0.08 m³ within a laser-interferometer gas-cell enclosure. The solid curve shows its speed distribution at T₁ = 290 K and the dashed curve at T₂ = 725 K (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²)).

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_rms = √(3RT₁ / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹.
Scales v_rms by √(T₂ / T₁) or re-evaluates √(3RT₂ / M).

parts.prompt: Calculate the root-mean-square speed v_rms of the Neon-20 (Ne) atoms at T₁ = 290 K.
Calculate the gas pressure inside the vessel at T₁ = 290 K.
Determine the new root-mean-square speed of the atoms when heated to T₂ = 725 K.

items.stem: A sealed sample of 0.8 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder follows path A → B → C on the P–V diagram: state A is at (1.8 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³), state B is at (5.4 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³), and state C is at (5.4 × 10⁵ Pa, 5.5 × 10⁻³ m³). Use the convention where work done by the gas is positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) Work is done only along B → C: W_by = 5.4 × 10⁵(5.5 × 10⁻³ − 2.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.62 × 10³ J. (b) ΔU_AC = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A) = 3.78 × 10³ J. (c) Total heat supplied Q = ΔU_AC + W_by = 5.40 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies W_AB = 0 and computes P_B(V_C − V_B).
Sums ΔU_AC and W_by to obtain total heat supplied.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total mechanical work done by the gas along path A → B → C.
Calculate the total change in internal energy ΔU of the monatomic gas between state A and state C.
workingSteps: For a monatomic ideal gas, U = (3/2) PV, so ΔU_AC = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A).

parts.prompt: Determine the total thermal energy Q supplied to the gas over the complete path A → B → C.
workingSteps: By the first law of thermodynamics, Q = ΔU_AC + W_by = 3.780 × 10³ + 1.620 × 10³ = 5.40 × 10³ J.

items.stem: Inside a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity immersed in a constant-temperature bath at 450 K, 0.45 mol of an ideal monatomic gas expands reversibly along isotherm A → B from V_A = 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 0.0225 m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and expansion work done by the gas as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) P_B = nRT / V_B = 7.48 × 10⁴ Pa. (b) W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 2.53 × 10³ J. (c) Since ΔU = 0, Q = W_by and ΔS = Q / T = 5.62 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Uses ΔS = Q / T with Q = W_by.

parts.prompt: Calculate the final pressure P_B of the gas in state B.
Calculate the work done by the gas during the reversible isothermal expansion A → B.
Determine the change in entropy ΔS of the gas during A → B.
workingSteps: Since ΔU = 0 for an ideal gas isotherm, Q = W_by.

items.stem: Thermal analysis of 0.45 kg of water in a ceramic-lined materials characterization furnace records the three-segment temperature–energy profile from 298 K to 403 K (boiling point 373.15 K; c_liquid = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹; c_vapour = 2010 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹; specific latent heat of vaporization L_v = 2.26 × 10⁶ J kg⁻¹).
items.workedSolution: (a) Q_sens = m c_liquid ΔT₁ + m c_vapour ΔT₂ = 1.68 × 10⁵ J. (b) Plateau latent energy Q_lat = m L = 1.02 × 10⁶ J. (c) Total thermal energy Q_total = Q_sens + Q_lat = 1.19 × 10⁶ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates m c₁ ΔT₁ + m c₂ ΔT₂.
Evaluates m L on the phase-change plateau.

workingSteps: m_water c_water (338.15 − T_eq) = m_ice c_ice (273.15 − 268.15) + Q_lat + m_ice c_water (T_eq − 273.15).

parts.prompt: Determine the total thermal energy released by the initially warm water.

items.stem: In an infrared energy-balance investigation, a Martian mid-latitude rocky plain element of surface area 6.5 m² and greybody emissivity e = 0.95 has a uniform temperature of 326 K while exchanging radiation with an ambient environment at 268 K. Take b = 2.90 × 10⁻³ m K and σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴.
items.workedSolution: (a) λ_max = b / T = 8.90 × 10⁻⁶ m. (b) Gross emitted power P_emitted = e σ A T⁴ = 3.95 × 10³ W. (c) Net radiative loss P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) = 2.15 × 10³ W.

markScheme.criterion: Uses P_emitted = e σ A T⁴.

parts.prompt: Calculate the peak infrared wavelength λ_max emitted by the surface.
Calculate the gross thermal power emitted by the greybody surface.
Determine the net rate of radiative thermal energy loss to the 268 K surroundings.
workingSteps: P_net = e σ A (T⁴ − T_amb⁴) = 2.15 × 10³ W.

items.stem: During an instrument check, a thermostatted noble-gas reference bulb of internal volume 8.0 × 10⁻³ m³ contains 1.6 mol of Argon-40 (Ar) (molar mass 40 g mol⁻¹) at 227 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15) (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is the pressure inside the chamber?
items.workedSolution: Convert temperature to kelvin: T = 227 + 273.15 = 500.15 K. From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (1.6 × 8.31 × 500.15) / 8.0 × 10⁻³ = 8.31 × 10⁵ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 8.31 × 10⁵ Pa (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies nRT by volume V instead of dividing nRT by V.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes Celsius temperature θ directly into pV = nRT without converting to absolute temperature in kelvin.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the amount of substance n in p = nRT / V, solving for 1 mol instead of the given molar amount.

items.stem: Monatomic Argon-40 (Ar) gas (molar mass 0.04 kg mol⁻¹) inside a high-vacuum synchrotron beamline gas target has the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed distribution shown at 440 K. Take k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the mean translational kinetic energy per atom in electronvolts?

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 440 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 0.0569 eV (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates (1/2) k_B T / e for a single degree of freedom instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes k_B T / e and omits the 3/2 translational factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the 3/2 factor to 3 k_B T / e by omitting the 1/2 in kinetic energy.

items.stem: In a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity, 0.4 mol of a monatomic ideal gas executes a clockwise closed cycle A → B → C → D → A between pressures 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa and 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa and volumes 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ and 0.012 m³ (A → B isobaric expansion at 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa, B → C isochoric cooling, C → D isobaric compression at 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa, D → A isochoric heating). Taking net work done by the gas as positive, what is the net mechanical work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Net work done by the gas equals the enclosed rectangular area: W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = (3.0 × 10⁵ − 1.0 × 10⁵)(0.012 − 3.0 × 10⁻³) = 1.80 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes netWorkJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 1.80 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the expansion work along A → B and forgets to subtract the compression work along C → D.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes P_B V_B − P_D V_D instead of the enclosed rectangular loop area (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min).

items.stem: In a variable-volume optical pressure cell, 0.75 mol of monatomic ideal gas executes a reversible Carnot heat-engine cycle between a hot reservoir at 572 K and a cold sink at 260 K, expanding isothermally at the hot reservoir from V_A = 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the theoretical thermal efficiency η of this Carnot cycle?
items.workedSolution: Carnot efficiency η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 1 − 260 / 572 = 0.545.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 0.545 (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates T_C / T_H without subtracting from 1.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses the isothermal volume ratio 1 − V_A / V_B instead of the reservoir temperature ratio 1 − T_C / T_H.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides ΔT by T_C instead of T_H when computing efficiency.

items.stem: On the P–V plot for a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder, 1.2 mol of monatomic working gas (γ = 5/3) expands adiabatically from (5.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³) at A to 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³ at B, returns to 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ isobarically at C, and regains 5.5 × 10⁵ Pa isochorically. Defining work by the gas as positive, calculate W_net.
items.workedSolution: At B, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 5.457 × 10⁴ Pa. Adiabatic work W_AB = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 597.1 J, and isobaric compression work W_BC = P_B(V_C − V_B) = -196.4 J (W_CA = 0). Thus W_net = W_AB + W_BC = 401 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 401 J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the magnitude of the isobaric compression work P_B(V_B − V_C).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the adiabatic expansion work W_AB and forgets to subtract the isobaric compression work |W_BC|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_CA along the isochoric leg instead of net work W_net.

items.stem: A heated copper block of mass 0.18 kg and specific heat capacity 385 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 410 K is plunged into 0.22 kg of water (c = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 290 K inside a well-insulated copper-lined laboratory calorimeter. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. What is the final thermal equilibrium temperature T_eq?
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l), giving T_eq = 298.4 K. Therefore T_eq = 298 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 298 K (B).

items.stem: In a semiconductor lithography purge canister (volume 0.04 m³), 0.3 mol of monatomic Argon-40 (Ar) of molar mass 0.04 kg mol⁻¹ is warmed from T₁ = 550 K to T₂ = 825 K, shifting the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed curve as plotted. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), determine v_rms at the higher temperature T₂.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.04 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 825 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 825 / 0.04) = 717 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 717 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: The P–V graph shows an isobaric compression of 1.5 mol of ideal monatomic gas inside a precision pneumatic actuator chamber sealed with a movable piston at 5.4 × 10⁵ Pa from V_A = 3.9 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³. Using the sign convention where work done on the gas is positive, determine the compression work done on the gas.
items.workedSolution: During isobaric compression from 3.9 × 10⁻³ m³ to 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at 5.4 × 10⁵ Pa, work done on the gas W_on = −P(V_B − V_A) = 5.4 × 10⁵ × (3.9 × 10⁻³ − 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.30 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 1.30 × 10³ J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the magnitude of internal energy change |ΔU| = (3/2) P |ΔV| instead of boundary work P |ΔV|.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies pressure by initial volume V_A instead of the volume change |V_B − V_A|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the total heat rejected |Q| = (5/2) P |ΔV| rather than the mechanical work done on the gas.

items.stem: A thermal bath keeps 1.2 mol of ideal gas in a variable-volume optical pressure cell at 400 K during a reversible expansion from 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 3.6 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is the thermal energy Q supplied to the gas (equal to work done by the gas)?
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 400 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.2 × 8.31 × 400 × ln(3.6 × 10⁻³ / 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 3.49 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 3.49 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as remaining constant at P_A, computing P_A(V_B − V_A) instead of ∫ P dV = nRT ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Adds U = (3/2)nRT to isothermal work, overlooking that ΔU = 0 at constant temperature.

items.stem: In a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber, 0.6 mol of an ideal monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) executes an idealised four-leg Otto cycle A → B → C → D → A: adiabatic compression from (1.2 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³) at A to V_B = 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ at B, isochoric heating to P_C = 2.661 × 10⁶ Pa at C, adiabatic expansion back to V_D = 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³ at D, and isochoric cooling to A. What is the thermal efficiency η of this cycle?
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic Otto cycle (γ = 5/3), η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1) = 1 − (1.2 × 10⁻³ / 4.8 × 10⁻³)^(2/3) = 0.603 (equivalently W_net / Q_in = 1.576 × 10³ / 2.613 × 10³ = 0.603).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 0.603 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses exponent 1 instead of γ − 1 = 2/3 in the Otto efficiency relation η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes Carnot efficiency 1 − T_A / T_C between extreme cycle temperatures instead of Otto efficiency.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Raises V_min / V_max to γ = 5/3 rather than γ − 1 = 2/3.

items.stem: Inside a double-walled vacuum Dewar mixing vessel, 0.32 kg of ethanol (specific heat capacity 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 285 K receives a 0.48 kg aluminium specimen (c = 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 380 K. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. Calculate the equilibrium temperature of the mixture.
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l), giving T_eq = 318.8 K. Therefore T_eq = 319 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 319 K (B).

items.stem: A sample of 2.2 mol of monatomic Argon-40 (Ar) (M = 40 g mol⁻¹) occupies an orbital satellite attitude-control propellant cylinder of fixed volume 0.045 m³ at 520 K. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, calculate the bulk density ρ of the gas.
items.workedSolution: Total gas mass m = nM = 2.2 × 0.04 = 0.08800 kg. Density ρ = m / V = 0.08800 / 0.045 = 1.96 kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Applies ρ = nM / V in SI units to obtain 1.96 kg m⁻³ (B).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Leaves molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of converting to kg mol⁻¹, overestimating density by a factor of 1000.

items.stem: Inside a thermostatted noble-gas reference bulb, an ideal monatomic sample of Xenon-131 (Xe) (M = 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹) is in thermal equilibrium at 260 K. Given k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and 1 eV = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, What is the mean translational kinetic energy per atom in electronvolts?

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 260 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 0.0336 eV (C).

items.stem: The diagram shows a closed four-leg cycle A → B → C → D → A for 1 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals, bounded by P_low = 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa, P_high = 4.2 × 10⁵ Pa, V_min = 2.4 × 10⁻³ m³, and V_max = 7.2 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the thermal efficiency η = W_net / Q_in of this rectangular monatomic-gas cycle?
items.workedSolution: W_net = (4.2 × 10⁵ − 1.2 × 10⁵)(7.2 × 10⁻³ − 2.4 × 10⁻³) = 1.440 × 10³ J. Heat enters on D → A and A → B: Q_in = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min + (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 6.120 × 10³ J. Efficiency η = W_net / Q_in = 0.235.

markScheme.criterion: Computes thermalEfficiency correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 0.235 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides W_net by Q_AB alone, neglecting the heat input Q_DA on the isochoric leg D → A.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits internal energy gain ΔU_AB when computing total heat input Q_in.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the Carnot efficiency 1 − T_min / T_max between extreme corner temperatures instead of the actual cycle efficiency W_net / Q_in.

items.stem: Maintained in thermal contact with a 600 K bath, 2.2 mol of ideal gas in a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder expands quasi-statically from 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 7.5 × 10⁻³ m³. Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine ΔS = Q / T for the gas.
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 2.2 × 8.31 × ln(7.5 × 10⁻³ / 2.5 × 10⁻³) = 20.1 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 20.1 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 logarithm log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of the natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Replaces ln(V_B / V_A) with the linear fractional change (V_B − V_A) / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes isothermal heat Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) without dividing by T to obtain ΔS = Q / T.

items.stem: The diagram shows a reversible Carnot cycle A → B → C → D → A for 0.5 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber coupled to a hot reservoir at 537 K and a cold sink at 290 K, with isothermal expansion from 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ to 4.2 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what magnitude of thermal energy Q_C is rejected to the cold sink per cycle?
items.workedSolution: During isothermal compression C → D at T_C = 290 K, V_C / V_D = V_B / V_A, so heat rejected to the cold sink is Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.51 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 1.51 × 10³ J (C).

items.stem: A sample of 0.6 mol of an ideal monatomic gas in a cryocooler compression cylinder containing monatomic working gas expands isobarically at constant pressure 6.0 × 10⁵ Pa from volume 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ (state A) to 8.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (state B). Taking thermal energy supplied to the gas and work done by the gas as positive, how much thermal energy Q is supplied to the gas during A → B?
items.workedSolution: Work done by the gas W_by = P(V_B − V_A) = 6.0 × 10⁵ × (8.0 × 10⁻³ − 2.5 × 10⁻³) = 3.300 × 10³ J. For a monatomic ideal gas, ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV = 4.950 × 10³ J. By the first law, Q = ΔU + W_by = (5/2) P ΔV = 8.25 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 8.25 × 10³ J (D).

items.stem: Inside a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber, 0.45 mol of ideal gas is held at a constant temperature of 520 K while expanding reversibly from V_A = 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 6.75 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking work done by the gas as positive and R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, how much work is done by the gas?
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 520 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.45 × 8.31 × 520 × ln(6.75 × 10⁻³ / 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 2.92 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 2.92 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds U = (3/2)nRT to isothermal work, overlooking that ΔU = 0 at constant temperature.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as remaining constant at P_A, computing P_A(V_B − V_A) instead of ∫ P dV = nRT ln(V_B / V_A).

items.stem: The P–V diagram shows an ideal Otto cycle for 1 mol of monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) in a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell, compressing adiabatically from V_max = 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (at 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa) to V_min = 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³, heating isochorically to 1.373 × 10⁶ Pa, expanding adiabatically to 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³, and cooling isochorically back to state A. Calculate the cycle efficiency η = W_net / Q_in.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic Otto cycle (γ = 5/3), η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1) = 1 − (2.0 × 10⁻³ / 6.0 × 10⁻³)^(2/3) = 0.519 (equivalently W_net / Q_in = 1.167 × 10³ / 2.247 × 10³ = 0.519).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 0.519 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses exponent 1 instead of γ − 1 = 2/3 in the Otto efficiency relation η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes Carnot efficiency 1 − T_A / T_C between extreme cycle temperatures instead of Otto efficiency.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Raises V_min / V_max to γ = 5/3 rather than γ − 1 = 2/3.

items.stem: A heated brass block of mass 0.28 kg and specific heat capacity 380 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 410 K is plunged into 0.42 kg of water (c = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 285 K inside a precision isothermal-jacket mixing cup. During mixing, 1600 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. How much thermal energy is released by the brass block in reaching equilibrium?
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l) + 1600, giving T_eq = 291.3 K. Heat released by the solid Q_lost = m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = 1.26 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 1.26 × 10⁴ J (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the final equilibrium temperature is the unweighted midpoint (T_solid + T_liquid) / 2.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the heat gained by the liquid bath without adding the heat lost to the surroundings.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the solid cools all the way down to the initial bath temperature T_liquid instead of T_eq.

items.stem: In a thermostatted noble-gas reference bulb (volume 0.08 m³), 0.8 mol of monatomic Helium-4 (He) of molar mass 4 g mol⁻¹ is warmed from T₁ = 290 K to T₂ = 435 K, shifting the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed curve as plotted. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), determine v_rms at the higher temperature T₂.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 435 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 435 / 4.0 × 10⁻³) = 1.65 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 1.65 × 10³ m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: Inside a sealed borosilicate acoustic-thermometry sphere, an ideal monatomic sample of Neon-20 (Ne) (M = 0.0202 kg mol⁻¹) is in thermal equilibrium at 187 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Use Boltzmann constant 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and elementary charge 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. Find the average translational kinetic energy of a single atom in eV.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 460.15 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 0.0595 eV (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates (1/2) k_B T / e for a single degree of freedom instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses temperature in °C rather than absolute temperature in kelvin.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes k_B T / e and omits the 3/2 translational factor.

items.stem: The P–V graph shows an isobaric compression of 0.4 mol of ideal monatomic gas inside a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals at 3.6 × 10⁵ Pa from V_A = 5.2 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Using the sign convention where work done on the gas is positive, determine the compression work done on the gas.
items.workedSolution: During isobaric compression from 5.2 × 10⁻³ m³ to 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ at 3.6 × 10⁵ Pa, work done on the gas W_on = −P(V_B − V_A) = 3.6 × 10⁵ × (5.2 × 10⁻³ − 2.0 × 10⁻³) = 1.15 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 1.15 × 10³ J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the magnitude of internal energy change |ΔU| = (3/2) P |ΔV| instead of boundary work P |ΔV|.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies pressure by initial volume V_A instead of the volume change |V_B − V_A|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the total heat rejected |Q| = (5/2) P |ΔV| rather than the mechanical work done on the gas.

items.stem: In a closed noble-gas power-conversion loop, 0.2 mol of a monatomic ideal gas executes a clockwise closed cycle A → B → C → D → A between pressures 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa and 3.6 × 10⁵ Pa and volumes 2.4 × 10⁻³ m³ and 7.2 × 10⁻³ m³ (A → B isobaric expansion at 3.6 × 10⁵ Pa, B → C isochoric cooling, C → D isobaric compression at 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa, D → A isochoric heating). What is the total thermal energy Q_in absorbed by the monatomic gas during the heating legs D → A and A → B?
items.workedSolution: Heat enters on D → A (isochoric, W = 0): Q_DA = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min = 864.0 J, and on A → B (isobaric): Q_AB = (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 4.320 × 10³ J. Total Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = 5.18 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes heatInputJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 5.18 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Confuses net cycle heat Q_net = W_net with total heat input Q_in absorbed from the hot source.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic ΔU on both heating legs.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Includes only the heat absorbed during isobaric expansion A → B and omits the isochoric heating D → A.

items.stem: The P–V curve shows a reversible isothermal expansion at 280 K of 1.6 mol of ideal gas inside a frictionless piston-cylinder assembly on a thermodynamics test bench from volume 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 7.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). Calculate the entropy increase ΔS of the gas.
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.6 × 8.31 × ln(7.0 × 10⁻³ / 2.0 × 10⁻³) = 16.7 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 16.7 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 logarithm log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of the natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Replaces ln(V_B / V_A) with the linear fractional change (V_B − V_A) / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes isothermal heat Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) without dividing by T to obtain ΔS = Q / T.

items.stem: A Carnot engine modelled in a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell uses 1 mol of ideal gas operating between a hot reservoir at 608 K and a cold sink at 380 K. During the high-temperature isothermal stage A → B, the volume increases from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 7.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking net work done by the gas as positive (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹), what is the net work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) = 6.330 × 10³ J and η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 0.3750. Net work output W_net = η Q_H = nR(T_H − T_C) ln(V_B / V_A) = 2.37 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 2.37 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the rejected heat Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) instead of net work Q_H − Q_C.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) without multiplying by Carnot efficiency (1 − T_C / T_H).

items.stem: Engineers charge a high-vacuum synchrotron beamline gas target (capacity 0.045 m³) with 1.6 mol of Helium-4 (He) of molar mass 4 g mol⁻¹ at an equilibrium temperature of 87 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15) (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). Determine the density of the confined gas.
items.workedSolution: Total gas mass m = nM = 1.6 × 4.0 × 10⁻³ = 6.400 × 10⁻³ kg. Density ρ = m / V = 6.400 × 10⁻³ / 0.045 = 0.142 kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Applies ρ = nM / V in SI units to obtain 0.142 kg m⁻³ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies total gas mass nM by container volume V instead of dividing by V.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes molar concentration n / V (mol m⁻³) and omits multiplication by molar mass M.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Leaves molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of converting to kg mol⁻¹, overestimating density by a factor of 1000.

items.stem: Monatomic Argon-40 (Ar) gas (molar mass 0.04 kg mol⁻¹) inside an atmospheric research dropsonde reference chamber has the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed distribution shown at 440 K. Use molar gas constant R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the molar internal energy of this ideal monatomic gas?
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic gas, molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T = 1.5 × 8.31 × 440 = 5.48 × 10³ J mol⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 440 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 5.48 × 10³ J mol⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Includes only one translational degree of freedom (1/2 R T) instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses molar enthalpy C_p T = (5/2) R T instead of molar internal energy (3/2) R T.

items.stem: A heat-engine test rig (a variable-volume optical pressure cell) drives 1 mol of ideal monatomic gas around a rectangular cycle with upper pressure 3.6 × 10⁵ Pa, lower pressure 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa, minimum volume 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³, and maximum volume 8.0 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the thermal efficiency η = W_net / Q_in of this rectangular monatomic-gas cycle?
items.workedSolution: W_net = (3.6 × 10⁵ − 1.8 × 10⁵)(8.0 × 10⁻³ − 4.0 × 10⁻³) = 720.0 J. Heat enters on D → A and A → B: Q_in = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min + (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 4.680 × 10³ J. Efficiency η = W_net / Q_in = 0.154.

markScheme.criterion: Computes thermalEfficiency correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 0.154 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides W_net by Q_AB alone, neglecting the heat input Q_DA on the isochoric leg D → A.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits internal energy gain ΔU_AB when computing total heat input Q_in.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the Carnot efficiency 1 − T_min / T_max between extreme corner temperatures instead of the actual cycle efficiency W_net / Q_in.

items.stem: The diagram shows a reversible Carnot cycle A → B → C → D → A for 0.75 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder coupled to a hot reservoir at 527 °C and a cold sink at 47 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15), with isothermal expansion from 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 8.75 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what magnitude of thermal energy Q_C is rejected to the cold sink per cycle?
items.workedSolution: During isothermal compression C → D at T_C = 320.15 K, V_C / V_D = V_B / V_A, so heat rejected to the cold sink is Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) = 2.50 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 2.50 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A) in Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes net work W_net = Q_H − Q_C instead of the rejected heat Q_C.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the heat absorbed Q_H from the hot reservoir instead of the heat Q_C rejected to the cold sink.

items.stem: The P–V diagram shows an ideal Otto cycle for 0.8 mol of monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) in a precision pneumatic actuator chamber sealed with a movable piston, compressing adiabatically from V_max = 3.75 × 10⁻³ m³ (at 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa) to V_min = 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³, heating isochorically to 1.013 × 10⁶ Pa, expanding adiabatically to 3.75 × 10⁻³ m³, and cooling isochorically back to state A. Calculate the cycle efficiency η = W_net / Q_in.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic Otto cycle (γ = 5/3), η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1) = 1 − (1.5 × 10⁻³ / 3.75 × 10⁻³)^(2/3) = 0.457 (equivalently W_net / Q_in = 568.4 / 1.243 × 10³ = 0.457).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 0.457 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses exponent 1 instead of γ − 1 = 2/3 in the Otto efficiency relation η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes Carnot efficiency 1 − T_A / T_C between extreme cycle temperatures instead of Otto efficiency.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Raises V_min / V_max to γ = 5/3 rather than γ − 1 = 2/3.

items.stem: In a calorimetry run using a sealed foam-insulated metallurgical quench tank, a 0.65 kg cylinder of copper (c = 385 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 510 K is quenched in 0.32 kg of mineral oil (c = 1960 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 298 K. During mixing, 1250 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. Find T_eq at thermal equilibrium.
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l) + 1250, giving T_eq = 357.0 K. Therefore T_eq = 357 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 357 K (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Applies an extra factor of one-half from misremembering the degrees-of-freedom or geometric prefactor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Takes the unweighted arithmetic mean of the two initial temperatures, ignoring both masses and specific heat capacities.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Weights initial temperatures by mass alone and ignores the much larger specific heat capacity of the liquid.

items.stem: An experiment records the molecular speed distribution of 1.2 mol of Argon-40 (Ar) gas (molar mass 40 g mol⁻¹) occupying 0.025 m³ in a sealed borosilicate acoustic-thermometry sphere at 480 K (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²)). Which value equals the rms speed of the atoms?
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.04 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 480 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 480 / 0.04) = 547 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 547 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: A sample of 0.8 mol of an ideal monatomic gas in a closed noble-gas power-conversion loop expands isobarically at constant pressure 6.0 × 10⁵ Pa from volume 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (state A) to 6.4 × 10⁻³ m³ (state B). Taking thermal energy supplied to the gas and work done by the gas as positive, how much thermal energy Q is supplied to the gas during A → B?
items.workedSolution: Work done by the gas W_by = P(V_B − V_A) = 6.0 × 10⁵ × (6.4 × 10⁻³ − 2.0 × 10⁻³) = 2.640 × 10³ J. For a monatomic ideal gas, ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV = 3.960 × 10³ J. By the first law, Q = ΔU + W_by = (5/2) P ΔV = 6.60 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 6.60 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the boundary work W = P ΔV done by the gas and ignores the increase in internal energy ΔU.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the internal energy change ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV and omits the expansion work P ΔV.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV, computing ΔU + W = P ΔV + P ΔV = 2 P ΔV instead of (5/2) P ΔV.

items.stem: In a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder coupled to a thermal reservoir at 520 K, 0.6 mol of an ideal gas expands reversibly and isothermally from V_A = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 7.5 × 10⁻³ m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the change in entropy ΔS of the gas?
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.6 × 8.31 × ln(7.5 × 10⁻³ / 2.5 × 10⁻³) = 5.48 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 5.48 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 logarithm log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of the natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Replaces ln(V_B / V_A) with the linear fractional change (V_B − V_A) / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes isothermal heat Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) without dividing by T to obtain ΔS = Q / T.

items.stem: A closed heat engine (a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity) takes 1 mol of monatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) from A (6.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³) adiabatically to V_B = 3.6 × 10⁻³ m³, compresses it at constant pressure back to V_C = 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³, and heats it isochorically back to A. Find the net work done by the gas per cycle (work by gas positive).
items.workedSolution: At B, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 1.042 × 10⁵ Pa. Adiabatic work W_AB = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 607.5 J, and isobaric compression work W_BC = P_B(V_C − V_B) = -250.0 J (W_CA = 0). Thus W_net = W_AB + W_BC = 358 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 358 J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the magnitude of the isobaric compression work P_B(V_B − V_C).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the adiabatic expansion work W_AB and forgets to subtract the isobaric compression work |W_BC|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_CA along the isochoric leg instead of net work W_net.

items.stem: A heated aluminium block of mass 0.28 kg and specific heat capacity 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 410 K is plunged into 0.32 kg of water (c = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 298 K inside a low-heat-capacity polymeric calorimetry beaker. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. What is the final thermal equilibrium temperature T_eq?
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l), giving T_eq = 315.8 K. Therefore T_eq = 316 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 316 K (B).

items.stem: During an instrument check, a thermostatted noble-gas reference bulb of internal volume 0.012 m³ contains 0.15 mol of Argon-40 (Ar) (molar mass 40 g mol⁻¹) at 147 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15) (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is the pressure inside the chamber?
items.workedSolution: Convert temperature to kelvin: T = 147 + 273.15 = 420.15 K. From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (0.15 × 8.31 × 420.15) / 0.012 = 4.36 × 10⁴ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 4.36 × 10⁴ Pa (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies nRT by volume V instead of dividing nRT by V.

options.label: B

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the amount of substance n in p = nRT / V, solving for 1 mol instead of the given molar amount.

items.stem: Spectroscopic thermometry confirms that Xenon-131 (Xe) atoms (molar mass 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹) in a rigid stainless-steel vacuum-calibration tank are equilibrated at 247 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Determine the molar translational internal energy U_m.
items.workedSolution: T = 247 + 273.15 = 520.15 K. For an ideal monatomic gas, molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T = 1.5 × 8.31 × 520.15 = 6.48 × 10³ J mol⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 520.15 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 6.48 × 10³ J mol⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Includes only one translational degree of freedom (1/2 R T) instead of three.

options.label: B

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses molar enthalpy C_p T = (5/2) R T instead of molar internal energy (3/2) R T.

items.stem: Operating clockwise between 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ and 2.4 × 10⁻³ m³ and between 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa and 6.3 × 10⁵ Pa, 0.4 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber completes cycle A → B → C → D → A. What is the total thermal energy Q_in absorbed by the monatomic gas during the heating legs D → A and A → B?
items.workedSolution: Heat enters on D → A (isochoric, W = 0): Q_DA = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min = 810.0 J, and on A → B (isobaric): Q_AB = (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 1.890 × 10³ J. Total Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = 2.70 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes heatInputJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 2.70 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: C

items.stem: A thermal bath keeps 0.45 mol of ideal gas in a precision pneumatic actuator chamber sealed with a movable piston at 450 K during a reversible expansion from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 7.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is the thermal energy Q supplied to the gas (equal to work done by the gas)?
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 450 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.45 × 8.31 × 450 × ln(7.0 × 10⁻³ / 2.0 × 10⁻³) = 2.11 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 2.11 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A

options.label: D

items.stem: A Carnot engine modelled in a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity uses 0.5 mol of ideal gas operating between a hot reservoir at 527 °C and a cold sink at 67 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). During the high-temperature isothermal stage A → B, the volume increases from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking net work done by the gas as positive (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹), what is the net work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) = 3.046 × 10³ J and η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 0.5749. Net work output W_net = η Q_H = nR(T_H − T_C) ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.75 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 1.75 × 10³ J (C).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) without multiplying by Carnot efficiency (1 − T_C / T_H).

items.stem: Inside an ion-propulsion xenon feed manifold of internal volume 0.045 m³, 1.2 mol of ideal Krypton-84 (Kr) gas (molar mass 83.8 g mol⁻¹) is maintained at 280 K. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what is the mass density of the gas?
items.workedSolution: Total gas mass m = nM = 1.2 × 0.0838 = 0.1006 kg. Density ρ = m / V = 0.1006 / 0.045 = 2.23 kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Applies ρ = nM / V in SI units to obtain 2.23 kg m⁻³ (B).

items.stem: The graph shows the Maxwell–Boltzmann molecular speed distribution for 1.2 mol of ideal Xenon-131 (Xe) gas (molar mass 131.3 g mol⁻¹) inside a laser-interferometer gas-cell enclosure of volume 0.08 m³ at 410 K. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²). What is the root-mean-square (rms) speed of the atoms?
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 410 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 410 / 0.1313) = 279 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 279 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: A monatomic ideal gas (0.8 mol) in a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder transitions from state A (1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B (3.75 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³) and then to state C (3.75 × 10⁵ Pa, 0.0117 m³). Defining expansion work done by the gas as positive, calculate the total thermal energy absorbed by the gas over A → B → C.
items.workedSolution: Along A → B → C, work done by the gas is W_by = 0 + P_B(V_C − V_B) = 2.700 × 10³ J. Total internal energy change ΔU = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A) = 5.569 × 10³ J. Hence Q = ΔU + W_by = 8.27 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 8.27 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the monatomic 3/2 factor in ΔU = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A).

items.stem: Maintained in thermal contact with a 280 K bath, 0.6 mol of ideal gas in a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity expands quasi-statically from 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine ΔS = Q / T for the gas.
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.6 × 8.31 × ln(5.0 × 10⁻³ / 2.5 × 10⁻³) = 3.46 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 3.46 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A

options.label: C
