options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes isothermal heat Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) without dividing by T to obtain ΔS = Q / T.

items.stem: Three reversible stages A → B → C → A form a heat-engine cycle for 0.4 mol of monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) inside a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals: adiabatic expansion from 5.5 × 10⁵ Pa and 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ to 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³, constant-pressure compression to 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³, and constant-volume heating to A. What net mechanical work output does one cycle deliver?
items.workedSolution: At B, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 1.194 × 10⁵ Pa. Adiabatic work W_AB = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 452.5 J, and isobaric compression work W_BC = P_B(V_C − V_B) = -215.0 J (W_CA = 0). Thus W_net = W_AB + W_BC = 238 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 238 J (B).

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_CA along the isochoric leg instead of net work W_net.

items.stem: In a calorimetry run using a stirred insulated immersion calorimeter, a 0.36 kg cylinder of brass (c = 380 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 440 K is quenched in 0.22 kg of mineral oil (c = 1960 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 294 K. During mixing, 1600 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. Find T_eq at thermal equilibrium.
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l) + 1600, giving T_eq = 326.3 K. Therefore T_eq = 326 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 326 K (B).

items.stem: Spectroscopic thermometry confirms that Neon-20 (Ne) atoms (molar mass 0.0202 kg mol⁻¹) in an orbital satellite attitude-control propellant cylinder are equilibrated at 260 K. Use molar gas constant R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Determine the molar translational internal energy U_m.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic gas, molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T = 1.5 × 8.31 × 260 = 3.24 × 10³ J mol⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 260 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 3.24 × 10³ J mol⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: A sample of 0.25 mol of an ideal monatomic gas in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber expands isobarically at constant pressure 7.2 × 10⁵ Pa from volume 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (state A) to 5.2 × 10⁻³ m³ (state B). Taking thermal energy supplied to the gas and work done by the gas as positive, how much thermal energy Q is supplied to the gas during A → B?
items.workedSolution: Work done by the gas W_by = P(V_B − V_A) = 7.2 × 10⁵ × (5.2 × 10⁻³ − 2.0 × 10⁻³) = 2.304 × 10³ J. For a monatomic ideal gas, ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV = 3.456 × 10³ J. By the first law, Q = ΔU + W_by = (5/2) P ΔV = 5.76 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 5.76 × 10³ J (D).

items.stem: A heat-engine test rig (a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell) drives 1 mol of ideal monatomic gas around a rectangular cycle with upper pressure 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa, lower pressure 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa, minimum volume 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³, and maximum volume 8.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking net work done by the gas as positive, what is the net mechanical work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Net work done by the gas equals the enclosed rectangular area: W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = (3.0 × 10⁵ − 1.0 × 10⁵)(8.0 × 10⁻³ − 4.0 × 10⁻³) = 800 J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes netWorkJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 800 J (B).

Taking work done by the gas as positive and R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, how much work is done by the gas?

items.stem: In a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals, 0.3 mol of monatomic ideal gas executes a reversible Carnot heat-engine cycle between a hot reservoir at 277 °C and a cold sink at 117 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15), expanding isothermally at the hot reservoir from V_A = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 7.5 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the theoretical thermal efficiency η of this Carnot cycle?
items.workedSolution: Convert to kelvin: T_H = 550.15 K, T_C = 390.15 K. Carnot efficiency η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 1 − 390.15 / 550.15 = 0.291.

items.stem: The diagram shows a closed four-leg cycle A → B → C → D → A for 0.2 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder, bounded by P_low = 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, P_high = 4.5 × 10⁵ Pa, V_min = 1.8 × 10⁻³ m³, and V_max = 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the total thermal energy Q_in absorbed by the monatomic gas during the heating legs D → A and A → B?
items.workedSolution: Heat enters on D → A (isochoric, W = 0): Q_DA = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min = 810.0 J, and on A → B (isobaric): Q_AB = (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 3.038 × 10³ J. Total Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = 3.85 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes heatInputJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 3.85 × 10³ J (D).

items.stem: A Carnot engine modelled in an insulated aerospace gas-accumulator cylinder uses 1.4 mol of ideal gas operating between a hot reservoir at 560 K and a cold sink at 350 K. During the high-temperature isothermal stage A → B, the volume increases from 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 6.25 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking net work done by the gas as positive (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹), what is the net work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) = 5.970 × 10³ J and η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 0.3750. Net work output W_net = η Q_H = nR(T_H − T_C) ln(V_B / V_A) = 2.24 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 2.24 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) without multiplying by Carnot efficiency (1 − T_C / T_H).

items.stem: Three reversible stages A → B → C → A form a heat-engine cycle for 0.6 mol of monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) inside a closed noble-gas power-conversion loop: adiabatic expansion from 8.0 × 10⁵ Pa and 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³, constant-pressure compression to 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³, and constant-volume heating to A. What net mechanical work output does one cycle deliver?
items.workedSolution: At B, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 1.737 × 10⁵ Pa. Adiabatic work W_AB = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 1.097 × 10³ J, and isobaric compression work W_BC = P_B(V_C − V_B) = -521.2 J (W_CA = 0). Thus W_net = W_AB + W_BC = 576 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 576 J (B).

items.stem: Inside a vacuum-insulated stainless-steel Dewar flask, 0.72 kg of ethanol (specific heat capacity 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 302 K receives a 0.85 kg copper specimen (c = 385 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 475 K. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. Calculate the equilibrium temperature of the mixture.
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l), giving T_eq = 329.2 K. Therefore T_eq = 329 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 329 K (B).

items.stem: At 360 K, 2 mol of Argon-40 (Ar) with molar mass 0.04 kg mol⁻¹ fills an orbital satellite attitude-control propellant cylinder (capacity 0.04 m³). Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), calculate the root-mean-square speed marked v_rms on the distribution.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.04 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 360 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 360 / 0.04) = 474 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 474 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: A monatomic ideal gas (0.8 mol) in a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell transitions from state A (1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B (3.75 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³) and then to state C (3.75 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³). Defining expansion work done by the gas as positive, calculate the total thermal energy absorbed by the gas over A → B → C.
items.workedSolution: Along A → B → C, work done by the gas is W_by = 0 + P_B(V_C − V_B) = 1.237 × 10³ J. Total internal energy change ΔU = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A) = 2.362 × 10³ J. Hence Q = ΔU + W_by = 3.60 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 3.60 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the monatomic 3/2 factor in ΔU = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A).

items.stem: On the P–V diagram, 2.2 mol of an ideal gas in an insulated aerospace gas-accumulator cylinder undergoes a reversible isothermal expansion at 450 K from 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 7.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and expansion work by the gas as positive. Find W_AB.
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 450 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 2.2 × 8.31 × 450 × ln(7.0 × 10⁻³ / 3.5 × 10⁻³) = 5.70 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 5.70 × 10³ J (B).

items.stem: The P–V diagram shows an ideal Otto cycle for 0.25 mol of monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) in a variable-volume optical pressure cell, compressing adiabatically from V_max = 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³ (at 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa) to V_min = 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³, heating isochorically to 1.123 × 10⁶ Pa, expanding adiabatically to 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³, and cooling isochorically back to state A. Calculate the cycle efficiency η = W_net / Q_in.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic Otto cycle (γ = 5/3), η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1) = 1 − (1.5 × 10⁻³ / 4.5 × 10⁻³)^(2/3) = 0.519 (equivalently W_net / Q_in = 583.2 / 1.123 × 10³ = 0.519).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 0.519 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses exponent 1 instead of γ − 1 = 2/3 in the Otto efficiency relation η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes Carnot efficiency 1 − T_A / T_C between extreme cycle temperatures instead of Otto efficiency.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Raises V_min / V_max to γ = 5/3 rather than γ − 1 = 2/3.

items.stem: In a calorimetry run using a closed-lid magnetic-stirrer calorimetry pot, a 0.18 kg cylinder of aluminium (c = 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 410 K is quenched in 0.55 kg of mineral oil (c = 1960 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 294 K. During mixing, 1250 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. What thermal energy does the cylinder give up?
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l) + 1250, giving T_eq = 308.1 K. Heat released by the solid Q_lost = m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = 1.65 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 1.65 × 10⁴ J (C).

items.stem: During an instrument check, a rigid stainless-steel vacuum-calibration tank of internal volume 0.06 m³ contains 2.8 mol of Argon-40 (Ar) (molar mass 0.04 kg mol⁻¹) at 310 K (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is the pressure inside the chamber?
items.workedSolution: From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (2.8 × 8.31 × 310) / 0.06 = 1.20 × 10⁵ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 1.20 × 10⁵ Pa (D).

items.stem: Thermalised Xenon-131 (Xe) vapour of molar mass 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹ fills a high-vacuum synchrotron beamline gas target at a uniform temperature of 680 K. Take k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the mean translational kinetic energy per atom in electronvolts?

items.stem: In a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity, 1.5 mol of a monatomic ideal gas executes a clockwise closed cycle A → B → C → D → A between pressures 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa and 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa and volumes 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ and 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (A → B isobaric expansion at 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa, B → C isochoric cooling, C → D isobaric compression at 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, D → A isochoric heating). Taking net work done by the gas as positive, what is the net mechanical work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Net work done by the gas equals the enclosed rectangular area: W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = (3.0 × 10⁵ − 1.5 × 10⁵)(3.0 × 10⁻³ − 1.2 × 10⁻³) = 270 J.

items.stem: In a closed noble-gas power-conversion loop coupled to a thermal reservoir at 310 K, 1.6 mol of an ideal gas expands reversibly and isothermally from V_A = 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 8.4 × 10⁻³ m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the change in entropy ΔS of the gas?
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.6 × 8.31 × ln(8.4 × 10⁻³ / 3.5 × 10⁻³) = 11.6 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 11.6 J K⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: The diagram shows a reversible Carnot cycle A → B → C → D → A for 1 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber coupled to a hot reservoir at 650 K and a cold sink at 260 K, with isothermal expansion from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what magnitude of thermal energy Q_C is rejected to the cold sink per cycle?

items.stem: An experiment records the molecular speed distribution of 0.3 mol of Helium-4 (He) gas (molar mass 4 g mol⁻¹) occupying 0.04 m³ in a high-vacuum synchrotron beamline gas target at 250 K (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²)). Which value equals the rms speed of the atoms?
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 250 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 250 / 4.0 × 10⁻³) = 1.25 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 1.25 × 10³ m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: A low-density plasma-free Krypton-84 (Kr) sample (M = 0.0838 kg mol⁻¹) is held in an orbital satellite attitude-control propellant cylinder at 440 K. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the molar internal energy of this ideal monatomic gas?
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic gas, molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T = 1.5 × 8.31 × 440 = 5.48 × 10³ J mol⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 440 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 5.48 × 10³ J mol⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Includes only one translational degree of freedom (1/2 R T) instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses molar enthalpy C_p T = (5/2) R T instead of molar internal energy (3/2) R T.

items.stem: A monatomic ideal gas (0.8 mol) in a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity transitions from state A (1.2 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B (1.8 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³) and then to state C (1.8 × 10⁵ Pa, 3.9 × 10⁻³ m³). Defining expansion work done by the gas as positive, calculate the total thermal energy absorbed by the gas over A → B → C.
items.workedSolution: Along A → B → C, work done by the gas is W_by = 0 + P_B(V_C − V_B) = 432.0 J. Total internal energy change ΔU = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A) = 783.0 J. Hence Q = ΔU + W_by = 1.22 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 1.22 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the positive expansion work done by the gas instead of adding Q = ΔU + W_by.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the total internal energy change ΔU_AC and omits the boundary work done during B → C.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the monatomic 3/2 factor in ΔU = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A).

items.stem: The diagram shows a closed four-leg cycle A → B → C → D → A for 0.5 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals, bounded by P_low = 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, P_high = 5.25 × 10⁵ Pa, V_min = 2.4 × 10⁻³ m³, and V_max = 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the thermal efficiency η = W_net / Q_in of this rectangular monatomic-gas cycle?
items.workedSolution: W_net = (5.25 × 10⁵ − 1.5 × 10⁵)(4.8 × 10⁻³ − 2.4 × 10⁻³) = 900.0 J. Heat enters on D → A and A → B: Q_in = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min + (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 4.500 × 10³ J. Efficiency η = W_net / Q_in = 0.200.

markScheme.criterion: Computes thermalEfficiency correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 0.200 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides W_net by Q_AB alone, neglecting the heat input Q_DA on the isochoric leg D → A.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits internal energy gain ΔU_AB when computing total heat input Q_in.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the Carnot efficiency 1 − T_min / T_max between extreme corner temperatures instead of the actual cycle efficiency W_net / Q_in.

items.stem: Maintained in thermal contact with a 350 K bath, 0.45 mol of ideal gas in a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder expands quasi-statically from 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 8.75 × 10⁻³ m³. Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine ΔS = Q / T for the gas.
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.45 × 8.31 × ln(8.75 × 10⁻³ / 2.5 × 10⁻³) = 4.68 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 4.68 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 logarithm log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of the natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Replaces ln(V_B / V_A) with the linear fractional change (V_B − V_A) / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes isothermal heat Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) without dividing by T to obtain ΔS = Q / T.

items.stem: The diagram shows a reversible Carnot cycle A → B → C → D → A for 1.4 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber coupled to a hot reservoir at 800 K and a cold sink at 320 K, with isothermal expansion from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 7.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what magnitude of thermal energy Q_C is rejected to the cold sink per cycle?
items.workedSolution: During isothermal compression C → D at T_C = 320 K, V_C / V_D = V_B / V_A, so heat rejected to the cold sink is Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) = 4.66 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 4.66 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the heat absorbed Q_H from the hot reservoir instead of the heat Q_C rejected to the cold sink.

items.stem: In a cryogenic buffer reservoir in a superconducting magnet rig of volume 0.012 m³, 2.2 mol of Helium-4 (He) (molar mass 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹) is held in thermal equilibrium at 177 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what pressure does the gas exert on the walls?
items.workedSolution: Convert temperature to kelvin: T = 177 + 273.15 = 450.15 K. From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (2.2 × 8.31 × 450.15) / 0.012 = 6.86 × 10⁵ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 6.86 × 10⁵ Pa (D).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the amount of substance n in p = nRT / V, solving for 1 mol instead of the given molar amount.

items.stem: Inside an ion-propulsion xenon feed manifold, an ideal monatomic sample of Argon-40 (Ar) (M = 0.04 kg mol⁻¹) is in thermal equilibrium at 260 K. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Calculate the internal energy per mole of the gas.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic gas, molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T = 1.5 × 8.31 × 260 = 3.24 × 10³ J mol⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 260 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 3.24 × 10³ J mol⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Operating clockwise between 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ and 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ and between 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa and 5.25 × 10⁵ Pa, 0.4 mol of monatomic ideal gas in an insulated aerospace gas-accumulator cylinder completes cycle A → B → C → D → A. Taking net work done by the gas as positive, what is the net mechanical work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Net work done by the gas equals the enclosed rectangular area: W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = (5.25 × 10⁵ − 1.5 × 10⁵)(3.0 × 10⁻³ − 1.2 × 10⁻³) = 675 J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes netWorkJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 675 J (A).

items.stem: In a frictionless piston-cylinder assembly on a thermodynamics test bench, 1 mol of monatomic ideal gas executes a reversible Carnot heat-engine cycle between a hot reservoir at 627 °C and a cold sink at 87 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15), expanding isothermally at the hot reservoir from V_A = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the theoretical thermal efficiency η of this Carnot cycle?
items.workedSolution: Convert to kelvin: T_H = 900.15 K, T_C = 360.15 K. Carnot efficiency η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 1 − 360.15 / 900.15 = 0.600.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 0.600 (B).

options.label: A

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides ΔT by T_C instead of T_H when computing efficiency.

items.stem: The P–V diagram shows an ideal Otto cycle for 1.2 mol of monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) in a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell, compressing adiabatically from V_max = 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (at 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa) to V_min = 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³, heating isochorically to 8.255 × 10⁵ Pa, expanding adiabatically to 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³, and cooling isochorically back to state A. Calculate the cycle efficiency η = W_net / Q_in.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic Otto cycle (γ = 5/3), η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1) = 1 − (2.0 × 10⁻³ / 4.0 × 10⁻³)^(2/3) = 0.370 (equivalently W_net / Q_in = 563.9 / 1.524 × 10³ = 0.370).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 0.370 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses exponent 1 instead of γ − 1 = 2/3 in the Otto efficiency relation η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Raises V_min / V_max to γ = 5/3 rather than γ − 1 = 2/3.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes Carnot efficiency 1 − T_A / T_C between extreme cycle temperatures instead of Otto efficiency.

items.stem: A heated copper block of mass 0.85 kg and specific heat capacity 385 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 510 K is plunged into 0.55 kg of water (c = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 294 K inside a double-walled vacuum Dewar mixing vessel. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. How much thermal energy is released by the copper block in reaching equilibrium?
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l), giving T_eq = 320.9 K. Heat released by the solid Q_lost = m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = 6.19 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 6.19 × 10⁴ J (C).

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the final equilibrium temperature is the unweighted midpoint (T_solid + T_liquid) / 2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the solid cools all the way down to the initial bath temperature T_liquid instead of T_eq.

items.stem: In a thermostatted noble-gas reference bulb (volume 0.025 m³), 1.5 mol of monatomic Argon-40 (Ar) of molar mass 40 g mol⁻¹ is warmed from T₁ = 210 K to T₂ = 473 K, shifting the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed curve as plotted. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), determine v_rms at the higher temperature T₂.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.04 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 473 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 473 / 0.04) = 543 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 543 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: The P–V graph shows an isobaric compression of 0.4 mol of ideal monatomic gas inside a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals at 3.75 × 10⁵ Pa from V_A = 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³. Using the sign convention where work done on the gas is positive, determine the compression work done on the gas.
items.workedSolution: During isobaric compression from 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³ to 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at 3.75 × 10⁵ Pa, work done on the gas W_on = −P(V_B − V_A) = 3.75 × 10⁵ × (4.8 × 10⁻³ − 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.24 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 1.24 × 10³ J (B).

items.stem: The P–V curve shows a reversible isothermal expansion at 310 K of 0.45 mol of ideal gas inside a frictionless piston-cylinder assembly on a thermodynamics test bench from volume 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). Calculate the entropy increase ΔS of the gas.
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.45 × 8.31 × ln(6.0 × 10⁻³ / 2.0 × 10⁻³) = 4.11 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 4.11 J K⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: Three reversible stages A → B → C → A form a heat-engine cycle for 0.8 mol of monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) inside a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder: adiabatic expansion from 6.5 × 10⁵ Pa and 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ to 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³, constant-pressure compression to 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³, and constant-volume heating to A. What net mechanical work output does one cycle deliver?
items.workedSolution: At B, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 6.449 × 10⁴ Pa. Adiabatic work W_AB = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 705.7 J, and isobaric compression work W_BC = P_B(V_C − V_B) = -232.2 J (W_CA = 0). Thus W_net = W_AB + W_BC = 474 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 474 J (B).

items.stem: Inside an expanded-polystyrene adiabatic quenching bath, 0.22 kg of ethanol (specific heat capacity 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 298 K receives a 0.48 kg aluminium specimen (c = 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 475 K. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. Calculate the equilibrium temperature of the mixture.

items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 280 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.6 × 8.31 × 280 × ln(3.6 × 10⁻³ / 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 3.26 × 10³ J.

items.stem: An experiment records the molecular speed distribution of 1.2 mol of Xenon-131 (Xe) gas (molar mass 131.3 g mol⁻¹) occupying 0.04 m³ in a sealed borosilicate acoustic-thermometry sphere at 360 K (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²)). Using the sign convention where work done on the gas is positive, determine the compression work done on the gas.

items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.6 × 8.31 × ln(0.01225 / 3.5 × 10⁻³) = 6.25 J K⁻¹.

items.stem: A closed heat engine (a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity) takes 0.8 mol of monatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) from A (5.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³) adiabatically to V_B = 6.25 × 10⁻³ m³, compresses it at constant pressure back to V_C = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³, and heats it isochorically back to A. Find the net work done by the gas per cycle (work by gas positive).
items.workedSolution: At B, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 1.194 × 10⁵ Pa. Adiabatic work W_AB = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 942.8 J, and isobaric compression work W_BC = P_B(V_C − V_B) = -447.9 J (W_CA = 0). Thus W_net = W_AB + W_BC = 495 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 495 J (B).

items.stem: A heated brass block of mass 0.48 kg and specific heat capacity 380 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 410 K is plunged into 0.55 kg of water (c = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 298 K inside a lagged benchtop thermal-equilibrium chamber. During mixing, 950 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. What is the final thermal equilibrium temperature T_eq?
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l) + 950, giving T_eq = 305.8 K. Therefore T_eq = 306 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 306 K (B).

items.stem: In a calorimetry run using a low-heat-capacity polymeric calorimetry beaker, a 0.18 kg cylinder of copper (c = 385 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 440 K is quenched in 0.55 kg of mineral oil (c = 1960 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 294 K. During mixing, 650 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. Find T_eq at thermal equilibrium.
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l) + 650, giving T_eq = 302.3 K. Therefore T_eq = 302 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 302 K (B).

items.stem: In a rigid stainless-steel vacuum-calibration tank of volume 8.0 × 10⁻³ m³, 1.2 mol of Helium-4 (He) (molar mass 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹) is held in thermal equilibrium at 380 K. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what pressure does the gas exert on the walls?
items.workedSolution: From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (1.2 × 8.31 × 380) / 8.0 × 10⁻³ = 4.74 × 10⁵ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 4.74 × 10⁵ Pa (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies nRT by volume V instead of dividing nRT by V.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts 273.15 from an already-kelvin temperature before applying pV = nRT.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the amount of substance n in p = nRT / V, solving for 1 mol instead of the given molar amount.

items.stem: Inside a high-vacuum synchrotron beamline gas target, an ideal monatomic sample of Argon-40 (Ar) (M = 0.04 kg mol⁻¹) is in thermal equilibrium at 820 K. Use Boltzmann constant 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and elementary charge 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. Find the average translational kinetic energy of a single atom in eV.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 820 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 0.106 eV (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates (1/2) k_B T / e for a single degree of freedom instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes k_B T / e and omits the 3/2 translational factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the 3/2 factor to 3 k_B T / e by omitting the 1/2 in kinetic energy.

items.stem: In a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity, 0.8 mol of a monatomic ideal gas executes a clockwise closed cycle A → B → C → D → A between pressures 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa and 4.5 × 10⁵ Pa and volumes 1.8 × 10⁻³ m³ and 5.4 × 10⁻³ m³ (A → B isobaric expansion at 4.5 × 10⁵ Pa, B → C isochoric cooling, C → D isobaric compression at 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa, D → A isochoric heating). Taking net work done by the gas as positive, what is the net mechanical work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Net work done by the gas equals the enclosed rectangular area: W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = (4.5 × 10⁵ − 1.8 × 10⁵)(5.4 × 10⁻³ − 1.8 × 10⁻³) = 972 J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes netWorkJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 972 J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies the enclosed loop area by an extraneous 3/2 internal-energy factor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the expansion work along A → B and forgets to subtract the compression work along C → D.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes P_B V_B − P_D V_D instead of the enclosed rectangular loop area (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min).

items.stem: A Carnot engine modelled in a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity uses 0.3 mol of ideal gas operating between a hot reservoir at 527 °C and a cold sink at 87 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). During the high-temperature isothermal stage A → B, the volume increases from 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ to 2.4 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking net work done by the gas as positive (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹), what is the net work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.383 × 10³ J and η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 0.5499. Net work output W_net = η Q_H = nR(T_H − T_C) ln(V_B / V_A) = 760 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 760 J (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the rejected heat Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) instead of net work Q_H − Q_C.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) without multiplying by Carnot efficiency (1 − T_C / T_H).

items.stem: On the P–V plot for a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder, 0.8 mol of monatomic working gas (γ = 5/3) expands adiabatically from (4.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³) at A to 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³ at B, returns to 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ isobarically at C, and regains 4.5 × 10⁵ Pa isochorically. Defining work by the gas as positive, calculate W_net.
items.workedSolution: At B, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 9.772 × 10⁴ Pa. Adiabatic work W_AB = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 617.1 J, and isobaric compression work W_BC = P_B(V_C − V_B) = -293.2 J (W_CA = 0). Thus W_net = W_AB + W_BC = 324 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 324 J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the magnitude of the isobaric compression work P_B(V_B − V_C).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the adiabatic expansion work W_AB and forgets to subtract the isobaric compression work |W_BC|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_CA along the isochoric leg instead of net work W_net.

items.stem: A heated copper block of mass 0.36 kg and specific heat capacity 385 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 380 K is plunged into 0.55 kg of water (c = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 285 K inside a well-insulated copper-lined laboratory calorimeter. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. What is the final thermal equilibrium temperature T_eq?
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l), giving T_eq = 290.4 K. Therefore T_eq = 290 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 290 K (B).

items.stem: In a semiconductor lithography purge canister (volume 0.04 m³), 1.2 mol of monatomic Argon-40 (Ar) of molar mass 0.04 kg mol⁻¹ is warmed from T₁ = 320 K to T₂ = 720 K, shifting the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed curve as plotted. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), determine v_rms at the higher temperature T₂.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.04 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 720 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 720 / 0.04) = 670 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 670 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: The P–V graph shows an isobaric compression of 0.4 mol of ideal monatomic gas inside a precision pneumatic actuator chamber sealed with a movable piston at 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa from V_A = 3.9 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³. Using the sign convention where work done on the gas is positive, determine the compression work done on the gas.
items.workedSolution: During isobaric compression from 3.9 × 10⁻³ m³ to 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa, work done on the gas W_on = −P(V_B − V_A) = 3.0 × 10⁵ × (3.9 × 10⁻³ − 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 720 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 720 J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the magnitude of internal energy change |ΔU| = (3/2) P |ΔV| instead of boundary work P |ΔV|.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies pressure by initial volume V_A instead of the volume change |V_B − V_A|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the total heat rejected |Q| = (5/2) P |ΔV| rather than the mechanical work done on the gas.

items.stem: A thermal bath keeps 0.6 mol of ideal gas in a variable-volume optical pressure cell at 520 K during a reversible expansion from 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 8.4 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is the thermal energy Q supplied to the gas (equal to work done by the gas)?
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 520 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.6 × 8.31 × 520 × ln(8.4 × 10⁻³ / 3.5 × 10⁻³) = 2.27 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 2.27 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as remaining constant at P_A, computing P_A(V_B − V_A) instead of ∫ P dV = nRT ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Adds U = (3/2)nRT to isothermal work, overlooking that ΔU = 0 at constant temperature.

items.stem: In a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber, 0.6 mol of an ideal monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) executes an idealised four-leg Otto cycle A → B → C → D → A: adiabatic compression from (1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³) at A to V_B = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at B, isochoric heating to P_C = 1.238 × 10⁶ Pa at C, adiabatic expansion back to V_D = 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³ at D, and isochoric cooling to A. What is the thermal efficiency η of this cycle?
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic Otto cycle (γ = 5/3), η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1) = 1 − (2.5 × 10⁻³ / 5.0 × 10⁻³)^(2/3) = 0.370 (equivalently W_net / Q_in = 1.057 × 10³ / 2.857 × 10³ = 0.370).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 0.370 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses exponent 1 instead of γ − 1 = 2/3 in the Otto efficiency relation η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Raises V_min / V_max to γ = 5/3 rather than γ − 1 = 2/3.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes Carnot efficiency 1 − T_A / T_C between extreme cycle temperatures instead of Otto efficiency.

items.stem: Inside a double-walled vacuum Dewar mixing vessel, 0.42 kg of ethanol (specific heat capacity 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 298 K receives a 0.48 kg aluminium specimen (c = 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 380 K. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. Calculate the equilibrium temperature of the mixture.
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l), giving T_eq = 322.3 K. Therefore T_eq = 322 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 322 K (B).

options.label: D

items.stem: A sample of 2.8 mol of monatomic Argon-40 (Ar) (M = 40 g mol⁻¹) occupies an orbital satellite attitude-control propellant cylinder of fixed volume 0.06 m³ at 310 K. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, calculate the bulk density ρ of the gas.
items.workedSolution: Total gas mass m = nM = 2.8 × 0.04 = 0.1120 kg. Density ρ = m / V = 0.1120 / 0.06 = 1.87 kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Applies ρ = nM / V in SI units to obtain 1.87 kg m⁻³ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies total gas mass nM by container volume V instead of dividing by V.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes molar concentration n / V (mol m⁻³) and omits multiplication by molar mass M.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Leaves molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of converting to kg mol⁻¹, overestimating density by a factor of 1000.

items.stem: Thermalised Xenon-131 (Xe) vapour of molar mass 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹ fills a thermostatted noble-gas reference bulb at a uniform temperature of 820 K. Given k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and 1 eV = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, Find the average translational kinetic energy of a single atom in eV.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 820 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 0.106 eV (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates (1/2) k_B T / e for a single degree of freedom instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes k_B T / e and omits the 3/2 translational factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the 3/2 factor to 3 k_B T / e by omitting the 1/2 in kinetic energy.

items.stem: The diagram shows a closed four-leg cycle A → B → C → D → A for 0.2 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals, bounded by P_low = 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, P_high = 5.25 × 10⁵ Pa, V_min = 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³, and V_max = 7.5 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the thermal efficiency η = W_net / Q_in of this rectangular monatomic-gas cycle?
items.workedSolution: W_net = (5.25 × 10⁵ − 1.5 × 10⁵)(7.5 × 10⁻³ − 3.0 × 10⁻³) = 1.688 × 10³ J. Heat enters on D → A and A → B: Q_in = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min + (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 7.594 × 10³ J. Efficiency η = W_net / Q_in = 0.222.

markScheme.criterion: Computes thermalEfficiency correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 0.222 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides W_net by Q_AB alone, neglecting the heat input Q_DA on the isochoric leg D → A.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits internal energy gain ΔU_AB when computing total heat input Q_in.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the Carnot efficiency 1 − T_min / T_max between extreme corner temperatures instead of the actual cycle efficiency W_net / Q_in.

items.stem: Maintained in thermal contact with a 600 K bath, 0.85 mol of ideal gas in a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder expands quasi-statically from 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine ΔS = Q / T for the gas.
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.85 × 8.31 × ln(5.0 × 10⁻³ / 2.5 × 10⁻³) = 4.90 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 4.90 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 logarithm log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of the natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Replaces ln(V_B / V_A) with the linear fractional change (V_B − V_A) / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes isothermal heat Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) without dividing by T to obtain ΔS = Q / T.

items.stem: The diagram shows a reversible Carnot cycle A → B → C → D → A for 0.3 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber coupled to a hot reservoir at 416 K and a cold sink at 260 K, with isothermal expansion from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what magnitude of thermal energy Q_C is rejected to the cold sink per cycle?
items.workedSolution: During isothermal compression C → D at T_C = 260 K, V_C / V_D = V_B / V_A, so heat rejected to the cold sink is Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) = 712 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 712 J (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A) in Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes net work W_net = Q_H − Q_C instead of the rejected heat Q_C.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the heat absorbed Q_H from the hot reservoir instead of the heat Q_C rejected to the cold sink.

items.stem: 2.8 mol of monatomic Krypton-84 (Kr) (molar mass 0.0838 kg mol⁻¹) fills a cryogenic buffer reservoir in a superconducting magnet rig of volume 0.024 m³ at a steady temperature of 27 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Find the gas pressure.
items.workedSolution: Convert temperature to kelvin: T = 27 + 273.15 = 300.15 K. From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (2.8 × 8.31 × 300.15) / 0.024 = 2.91 × 10⁵ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 2.91 × 10⁵ Pa (D).

items.stem: At 320 K, 1.2 mol of Xenon-131 (Xe) with molar mass 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹ fills a thick-walled titanium deep-sea pressure housing (capacity 0.015 m³). Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), calculate the root-mean-square speed marked v_rms on the distribution.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 320 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 320 / 0.1313) = 246 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A sample of 1.5 mol of an ideal monatomic gas in a cryocooler compression cylinder containing monatomic working gas expands isobarically at constant pressure 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa from volume 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³ (state A) to 6.3 × 10⁻³ m³ (state B). Taking thermal energy supplied to the gas and work done by the gas as positive, how much thermal energy Q is supplied to the gas during A → B?
items.workedSolution: Work done by the gas W_by = P(V_B − V_A) = 1.8 × 10⁵ × (6.3 × 10⁻³ − 3.5 × 10⁻³) = 504.0 J. For a monatomic ideal gas, ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV = 756.0 J. By the first law, Q = ΔU + W_by = (5/2) P ΔV = 1.26 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 1.26 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV, computing ΔU + W = P ΔV + P ΔV = 2 P ΔV instead of (5/2) P ΔV.

items.stem: Inside a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber, 0.3 mol of ideal gas is held at a constant temperature of 350 K while expanding reversibly from V_A = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking work done by the gas as positive and R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, how much work is done by the gas?
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 350 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.3 × 8.31 × 350 × ln(5.0 × 10⁻³ / 2.5 × 10⁻³) = 605 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 605 J (B).

items.stem: In a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell, 1 mol of an ideal monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) executes an idealised four-leg Otto cycle A → B → C → D → A: adiabatic compression from (1.2 × 10⁵ Pa, 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³) at A to V_B = 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ at B, isochoric heating to P_C = 1.348 × 10⁶ Pa at C, adiabatic expansion back to V_D = 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³ at D, and isochoric cooling to A. What is the thermal efficiency η of this cycle?
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic Otto cycle (γ = 5/3), η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1) = 1 − (2.0 × 10⁻³ / 6.0 × 10⁻³)^(2/3) = 0.519 (equivalently W_net / Q_in = 933.2 / 1.797 × 10³ = 0.519).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Raises V_min / V_max to γ = 5/3 rather than γ − 1 = 2/3.

items.stem: A heated brass block of mass 0.65 kg and specific heat capacity 380 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 475 K is plunged into 0.22 kg of water (c = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 290 K inside a precision isothermal-jacket mixing cup. During mixing, 1600 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. How much thermal energy is released by the brass block in reaching equilibrium?
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l) + 1600, giving T_eq = 327.8 K. Heat released by the solid Q_lost = m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = 3.64 × 10⁴ J.

items.workedSolution: During isobaric compression from 0.0112 m³ to 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at 2.4 × 10⁵ Pa, work done on the gas W_on = −P(V_B − V_A) = 2.4 × 10⁵ × (0.0112 − 3.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.85 × 10³ J.

items.stem: In a closed noble-gas power-conversion loop, 1 mol of a monatomic ideal gas executes a clockwise closed cycle A → B → C → D → A between pressures 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa and 5.25 × 10⁵ Pa and volumes 2.4 × 10⁻³ m³ and 7.2 × 10⁻³ m³ (A → B isobaric expansion at 5.25 × 10⁵ Pa, B → C isochoric cooling, C → D isobaric compression at 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, D → A isochoric heating). What is the total thermal energy Q_in absorbed by the monatomic gas during the heating legs D → A and A → B?
items.workedSolution: Heat enters on D → A (isochoric, W = 0): Q_DA = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min = 1.350 × 10³ J, and on A → B (isobaric): Q_AB = (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 6.300 × 10³ J. Total Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = 7.65 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes heatInputJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 7.65 × 10³ J (D).

items.stem: The P–V curve shows a reversible isothermal expansion at 450 K of 0.6 mol of ideal gas inside a frictionless piston-cylinder assembly on a thermodynamics test bench from volume 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). Calculate the entropy increase ΔS of the gas.
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.6 × 8.31 × ln(3.0 × 10⁻³ / 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 3.46 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 3.46 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes isothermal heat Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) without dividing by T to obtain ΔS = Q / T.

items.stem: A Carnot engine modelled in a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell uses 0.75 mol of ideal gas operating between a hot reservoir at 836 K and a cold sink at 380 K. During the high-temperature isothermal stage A → B, the volume increases from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking net work done by the gas as positive (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹), what is the net work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) = 4.774 × 10³ J and η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 0.5455. Net work output W_net = η Q_H = nR(T_H − T_C) ln(V_B / V_A) = 2.60 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 2.60 × 10³ J (C).

items.stem: Engineers charge a high-vacuum synchrotron beamline gas target (capacity 0.012 m³) with 2.8 mol of Helium-4 (He) of molar mass 4 g mol⁻¹ at an equilibrium temperature of 117 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15) (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). Determine the density of the confined gas.
items.workedSolution: Total gas mass m = nM = 2.8 × 4.0 × 10⁻³ = 0.01120 kg. Density ρ = m / V = 0.01120 / 0.012 = 0.933 kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Applies ρ = nM / V in SI units to obtain 0.933 kg m⁻³ (B).

items.stem: Inside an atmospheric research dropsonde reference chamber, an ideal monatomic sample of Argon-40 (Ar) (M = 0.04 kg mol⁻¹) is in thermal equilibrium at 310 K. Use molar gas constant R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Calculate the internal energy per mole of the gas.

items.stem: A heat-engine test rig (a variable-volume optical pressure cell) drives 1 mol of ideal monatomic gas around a rectangular cycle with upper pressure 5.25 × 10⁵ Pa, lower pressure 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, minimum volume 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³, and maximum volume 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the thermal efficiency η = W_net / Q_in of this rectangular monatomic-gas cycle?

items.stem: The diagram shows a reversible Carnot cycle A → B → C → D → A for 0.75 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder coupled to a hot reservoir at 277 °C and a cold sink at 67 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15), with isothermal expansion from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. What is the final thermal equilibrium temperature T_eq?

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 319 K (A).

items.stem: During an instrument check, a thermostatted noble-gas reference bulb of internal volume 0.045 m³ contains 0.35 mol of Argon-40 (Ar) (molar mass 40 g mol⁻¹) at 177 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15) (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is the pressure inside the chamber?
items.workedSolution: Convert temperature to kelvin: T = 177 + 273.15 = 450.15 K. From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (0.35 × 8.31 × 450.15) / 0.045 = 2.91 × 10⁴ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 2.91 × 10⁴ Pa (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies nRT by volume V instead of dividing nRT by V.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes Celsius temperature θ directly into pV = nRT without converting to absolute temperature in kelvin.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the amount of substance n in p = nRT / V, solving for 1 mol instead of the given molar amount.

items.stem: A low-density plasma-free Xenon-131 (Xe) sample (M = 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹) is held in a rigid stainless-steel vacuum-calibration tank at 137 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, What is the molar internal energy of this ideal monatomic gas?
items.workedSolution: T = 137 + 273.15 = 410.15 K. For an ideal monatomic gas, molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T = 1.5 × 8.31 × 410.15 = 5.11 × 10³ J mol⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 410.15 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 5.11 × 10³ J mol⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Includes only one translational degree of freedom (1/2 R T) instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses molar enthalpy C_p T = (5/2) R T instead of molar internal energy (3/2) R T.

items.stem: Operating clockwise between 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ and 0.012 m³ and between 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa and 4.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 1 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber completes cycle A → B → C → D → A. What is the total thermal energy Q_in absorbed by the monatomic gas during the heating legs D → A and A → B?
items.workedSolution: Heat enters on D → A (isochoric, W = 0): Q_DA = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min = 1.215 × 10³ J, and on A → B (isobaric): Q_AB = (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 1.013 × 10⁴ J. Total Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = 1.13 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes heatInputJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 1.13 × 10⁴ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Confuses net cycle heat Q_net = W_net with total heat input Q_in absorbed from the hot source.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic ΔU on both heating legs.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Includes only the heat absorbed during isobaric expansion A → B and omits the isochoric heating D → A.

items.stem: A thermal bath keeps 0.6 mol of ideal gas in a precision pneumatic actuator chamber sealed with a movable piston at 400 K during a reversible expansion from 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 0.01 m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is the thermal energy Q supplied to the gas (equal to work done by the gas)?
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 400 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.6 × 8.31 × 400 × ln(0.01 / 5.0 × 10⁻³) = 1.38 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 1.38 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as remaining constant at P_A, computing P_A(V_B − V_A) instead of ∫ P dV = nRT ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Adds U = (3/2)nRT to isothermal work, overlooking that ΔU = 0 at constant temperature.

items.stem: The diagram shows a reversible Carnot cycle A → B → C → D → A for 1.4 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber coupled to a hot reservoir at 537 K and a cold sink at 290 K, with isothermal expansion from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what magnitude of thermal energy Q_C is rejected to the cold sink per cycle?
items.workedSolution: During isothermal compression C → D at T_C = 290 K, V_C / V_D = V_B / V_A, so heat rejected to the cold sink is Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) = 2.34 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 2.34 × 10³ J (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A) in Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes net work W_net = Q_H − Q_C instead of the rejected heat Q_C.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the heat absorbed Q_H from the hot reservoir instead of the heat Q_C rejected to the cold sink.

items.stem: Inside an ion-propulsion xenon feed manifold of internal volume 0.075 m³, 1.6 mol of ideal Krypton-84 (Kr) gas (molar mass 83.8 g mol⁻¹) is maintained at 520 K. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what is the mass density of the gas?
items.workedSolution: Total gas mass m = nM = 1.6 × 0.0838 = 0.1341 kg. Density ρ = m / V = 0.1341 / 0.075 = 1.79 kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Applies ρ = nM / V in SI units to obtain 1.79 kg m⁻³ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies total gas mass nM by container volume V instead of dividing by V.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes molar concentration n / V (mol m⁻³) and omits multiplication by molar mass M.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Leaves molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of converting to kg mol⁻¹, overestimating density by a factor of 1000.

items.stem: The graph shows the Maxwell–Boltzmann molecular speed distribution for 0.5 mol of ideal Xenon-131 (Xe) gas (molar mass 131.3 g mol⁻¹) inside a laser-interferometer gas-cell enclosure of volume 0.08 m³ at 210 K. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²). What is the root-mean-square (rms) speed of the atoms?
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 210 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 210 / 0.1313) = 200 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 200 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: A monatomic ideal gas (1.2 mol) in a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder transitions from state A (1.2 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B (3.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³) and then to state C (3.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 5.2 × 10⁻³ m³). Defining expansion work done by the gas as positive, calculate the total thermal energy absorbed by the gas over A → B → C.
items.workedSolution: Along A → B → C, work done by the gas is W_by = 0 + P_B(V_C − V_B) = 960.0 J. Total internal energy change ΔU = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A) = 1.980 × 10³ J. Hence Q = ΔU + W_by = 2.94 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 2.94 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the positive expansion work done by the gas instead of adding Q = ΔU + W_by.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the total internal energy change ΔU_AC and omits the boundary work done during B → C.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the monatomic 3/2 factor in ΔU = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A).

items.stem: Maintained in thermal contact with a 310 K bath, 0.45 mol of ideal gas in a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity expands quasi-statically from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 9.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine ΔS = Q / T for the gas.
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.45 × 8.31 × ln(9.0 × 10⁻³ / 2.0 × 10⁻³) = 5.62 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 5.62 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 logarithm log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of the natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Replaces ln(V_B / V_A) with the linear fractional change (V_B − V_A) / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes isothermal heat Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) without dividing by T to obtain ΔS = Q / T.

items.stem: Three reversible stages A → B → C → A form a heat-engine cycle for 1.2 mol of monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) inside a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals: adiabatic expansion from 4.5 × 10⁵ Pa and 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³, constant-pressure compression to 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³, and constant-volume heating to A. What net mechanical work output does one cycle deliver?
items.workedSolution: At B, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 4.465 × 10⁴ Pa. Adiabatic work W_AB = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 610.7 J, and isobaric compression work W_BC = P_B(V_C − V_B) = -200.9 J (W_CA = 0). Thus W_net = W_AB + W_BC = 410 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 410 J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the magnitude of the isobaric compression work P_B(V_B − V_C).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the adiabatic expansion work W_AB and forgets to subtract the isobaric compression work |W_BC|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_CA along the isochoric leg instead of net work W_net.

items.stem: In a calorimetry run using a stirred insulated immersion calorimeter, a 0.48 kg cylinder of brass (c = 380 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 475 K is quenched in 0.32 kg of mineral oil (c = 1960 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 294 K. During mixing, 950 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. Find T_eq at thermal equilibrium.
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l) + 950, giving T_eq = 333.6 K. Therefore T_eq = 334 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 334 K (B).

items.stem: Within a rigid stainless-steel vacuum-calibration tank of volume 0.04 m³, 0.8 mol of monatomic Helium-4 (He) (M = 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹) is maintained at 480 K as represented by the speed distribution curve. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), find v_rms of the gas particles.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 480 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 480 / 4.0 × 10⁻³) = 1.73 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 1.73 × 10³ m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: Spectroscopic thermometry confirms that Neon-20 (Ne) atoms (molar mass 0.0202 kg mol⁻¹) in an orbital satellite attitude-control propellant cylinder are equilibrated at 540 K. Use molar gas constant R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Calculate the internal energy per mole of the gas.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic gas, molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T = 1.5 × 8.31 × 540 = 6.73 × 10³ J mol⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 540 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 6.73 × 10³ J mol⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Includes only one translational degree of freedom (1/2 R T) instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses molar enthalpy C_p T = (5/2) R T instead of molar internal energy (3/2) R T.

items.stem: A sample of 0.6 mol of an ideal monatomic gas in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber expands isobarically at constant pressure 4.8 × 10⁵ Pa from volume 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ (state A) to 5.5 × 10⁻³ m³ (state B). Taking thermal energy supplied to the gas and work done by the gas as positive, how much thermal energy Q is supplied to the gas during A → B?
items.workedSolution: Work done by the gas W_by = P(V_B − V_A) = 4.8 × 10⁵ × (5.5 × 10⁻³ − 2.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.440 × 10³ J. For a monatomic ideal gas, ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV = 2.160 × 10³ J. By the first law, Q = ΔU + W_by = (5/2) P ΔV = 3.60 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 3.60 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the internal energy change ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV and omits the expansion work P ΔV.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV, computing ΔU + W = P ΔV + P ΔV = 2 P ΔV instead of (5/2) P ΔV.

items.stem: A heat-engine test rig (a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell) drives 0.2 mol of ideal monatomic gas around a rectangular cycle with upper pressure 4.2 × 10⁵ Pa, lower pressure 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa, minimum volume 2.4 × 10⁻³ m³, and maximum volume 9.6 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking net work done by the gas as positive, what is the net mechanical work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Net work done by the gas equals the enclosed rectangular area: W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = (4.2 × 10⁵ − 1.2 × 10⁵)(9.6 × 10⁻³ − 2.4 × 10⁻³) = 2.16 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes netWorkJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 2.16 × 10³ J (A).

options.label: B

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes P_B V_B − P_D V_D instead of the enclosed rectangular loop area (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min).

items.stem: Inside a cryocooler compression cylinder containing monatomic working gas, 0.45 mol of ideal gas is held at a constant temperature of 310 K while expanding reversibly from V_A = 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 0.0225 m³. Taking work done by the gas as positive and R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, how much work is done by the gas?
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 310 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.45 × 8.31 × 310 × ln(0.0225 / 5.0 × 10⁻³) = 1.74 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 1.74 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds U = (3/2)nRT to isothermal work, overlooking that ΔU = 0 at constant temperature.

options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as remaining constant at P_A, computing P_A(V_B − V_A) instead of ∫ P dV = nRT ln(V_B / V_A).

items.stem: In an atmospheric research dropsonde reference chamber of volume 0.012 m³, 2.2 mol of Helium-4 (He) (molar mass 4 g mol⁻¹) is held in thermal equilibrium at 520 K. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what pressure does the gas exert on the walls?
items.workedSolution: From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (2.2 × 8.31 × 520) / 0.012 = 7.92 × 10⁵ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 7.92 × 10⁵ Pa (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies nRT by volume V instead of dividing nRT by V.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the amount of substance n in p = nRT / V, solving for 1 mol instead of the given molar amount.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts 273.15 from an already-kelvin temperature before applying pV = nRT.

items.stem: Thermalised Argon-40 (Ar) vapour of molar mass 0.04 kg mol⁻¹ fills a cryogenic buffer reservoir in a superconducting magnet rig at a uniform temperature of 247 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Use Boltzmann constant 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and elementary charge 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. Find the average translational kinetic energy of a single atom in eV.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 520.15 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 0.0673 eV (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates (1/2) k_B T / e for a single degree of freedom instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses temperature in °C rather than absolute temperature in kelvin.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes k_B T / e and omits the 3/2 translational factor.

items.stem: The diagram shows a closed four-leg cycle A → B → C → D → A for 0.4 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder, bounded by P_low = 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, P_high = 5.25 × 10⁵ Pa, V_min = 1.8 × 10⁻³ m³, and V_max = 5.4 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the total thermal energy Q_in absorbed by the monatomic gas during the heating legs D → A and A → B?
items.workedSolution: Heat enters on D → A (isochoric, W = 0): Q_DA = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min = 1.013 × 10³ J, and on A → B (isobaric): Q_AB = (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 4.725 × 10³ J. Total Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = 5.74 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes heatInputJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 5.74 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Confuses net cycle heat Q_net = W_net with total heat input Q_in absorbed from the hot source.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic ΔU on both heating legs.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Includes only the heat absorbed during isobaric expansion A → B and omits the isochoric heating D → A.

items.stem: A Carnot engine modelled in an insulated aerospace gas-accumulator cylinder uses 1 mol of ideal gas operating between a hot reservoir at 950 K and a cold sink at 380 K. During the high-temperature isothermal stage A → B, the volume increases from 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 3.75 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking net work done by the gas as positive (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹), what is the net work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) = 7.234 × 10³ J and η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 0.6000. Net work output W_net = η Q_H = nR(T_H − T_C) ln(V_B / V_A) = 4.34 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 4.34 × 10³ J (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the rejected heat Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) instead of net work Q_H − Q_C.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) without multiplying by Carnot efficiency (1 − T_C / T_H).

items.stem: A closed heat engine (a closed noble-gas power-conversion loop) takes 0.4 mol of monatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) from A (4.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³) adiabatically to V_B = 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³, compresses it at constant pressure back to V_C = 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³, and heats it isochorically back to A. Find the net work done by the gas per cycle (work by gas positive).
items.workedSolution: At B, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 7.211 × 10⁴ Pa. Adiabatic work W_AB = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 525.7 J, and isobaric compression work W_BC = P_B(V_C − V_B) = -216.3 J (W_CA = 0). Thus W_net = W_AB + W_BC = 309 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 309 J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the magnitude of the isobaric compression work P_B(V_B − V_C).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the adiabatic expansion work W_AB and forgets to subtract the isobaric compression work |W_BC|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_CA along the isochoric leg instead of net work W_net.

items.stem: Inside a vacuum-insulated stainless-steel Dewar flask, 0.32 kg of ethanol (specific heat capacity 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 294 K receives a 0.65 kg copper specimen (c = 385 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 440 K. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. Calculate the equilibrium temperature of the mixture.
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l), giving T_eq = 329.4 K. Therefore T_eq = 329 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 329 K (A).
