items.stem: At 250 K, 0.3 mol of Argon-40 (Ar) with molar mass 0.04 kg mol⁻¹ fills an orbital satellite attitude-control propellant cylinder (capacity 0.015 m³). Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), calculate the root-mean-square speed marked v_rms on the distribution.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.04 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 250 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 250 / 0.04) = 395 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 395 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: A monatomic ideal gas (0.6 mol) in a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell transitions from state A (1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B (3.75 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³) and then to state C (3.75 × 10⁵ Pa, 9.9 × 10⁻³ m³). Defining expansion work done by the gas as positive, calculate the total thermal energy absorbed by the gas over A → B → C.
items.workedSolution: Along A → B → C, work done by the gas is W_by = 0 + P_B(V_C − V_B) = 2.025 × 10³ J. Total internal energy change ΔU = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A) = 4.556 × 10³ J. Hence Q = ΔU + W_by = 6.58 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 6.58 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the positive expansion work done by the gas instead of adding Q = ΔU + W_by.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the total internal energy change ΔU_AC and omits the boundary work done during B → C.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the monatomic 3/2 factor in ΔU = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A).

items.stem: On the P–V diagram, 0.85 mol of an ideal gas in an insulated aerospace gas-accumulator cylinder undergoes a reversible isothermal expansion at 520 K from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and expansion work by the gas as positive. Find W_AB.
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 520 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.85 × 8.31 × 520 × ln(6.0 × 10⁻³ / 2.0 × 10⁻³) = 4.04 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 4.04 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as remaining constant at P_A, computing P_A(V_B − V_A) instead of ∫ P dV = nRT ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Adds U = (3/2)nRT to isothermal work, overlooking that ΔU = 0 at constant temperature.

items.stem: Starting at state A (1.2 × 10⁵ Pa, 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³), 0.8 mol of monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) in a variable-volume optical pressure cell is compressed adiabatically to 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³, heated at constant volume to 9.947 × 10⁵ Pa, expanded adiabatically to 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³, and cooled at constant volume back to A. Find η.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic Otto cycle (γ = 5/3), η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1) = 1 − (1.2 × 10⁻³ / 3.0 × 10⁻³)^(2/3) = 0.457 (equivalently W_net / Q_in = 363.8 / 795.8 = 0.457).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 0.457 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses exponent 1 instead of γ − 1 = 2/3 in the Otto efficiency relation η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes Carnot efficiency 1 − T_A / T_C between extreme cycle temperatures instead of Otto efficiency.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Raises V_min / V_max to γ = 5/3 rather than γ − 1 = 2/3.

items.stem: In a calorimetry run using a closed-lid magnetic-stirrer calorimetry pot, a 0.85 kg cylinder of aluminium (c = 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 410 K is quenched in 0.32 kg of mineral oil (c = 1960 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 285 K. During mixing, 1250 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. What thermal energy does the cylinder give up?
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l) + 1250, giving T_eq = 352.8 K. Heat released by the solid Q_lost = m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = 4.38 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 4.38 × 10⁴ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Applies an extra factor of one-half from misremembering the degrees-of-freedom or geometric prefactor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the final equilibrium temperature is the unweighted midpoint (T_solid + T_liquid) / 2.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Assumes the solid cools all the way down to the initial bath temperature T_liquid instead of T_eq.

items.stem: During an instrument check, a rigid stainless-steel vacuum-calibration tank of internal volume 0.024 m³ contains 1.2 mol of Argon-40 (Ar) (molar mass 0.04 kg mol⁻¹) at 340 K (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is the pressure inside the chamber?
items.workedSolution: From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (1.2 × 8.31 × 340) / 0.024 = 1.41 × 10⁵ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 1.41 × 10⁵ Pa (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies nRT by volume V instead of dividing nRT by V.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts 273.15 from an already-kelvin temperature before applying pV = nRT.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the amount of substance n in p = nRT / V, solving for 1 mol instead of the given molar amount.

items.stem: Thermalised Xenon-131 (Xe) vapour of molar mass 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹ fills a high-vacuum synchrotron beamline gas target at a uniform temperature of 820 K. Given k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and 1 eV = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, Find the average translational kinetic energy of a single atom in eV.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 820 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 0.106 eV (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates (1/2) k_B T / e for a single degree of freedom instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes k_B T / e and omits the 3/2 translational factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the 3/2 factor to 3 k_B T / e by omitting the 1/2 in kinetic energy.

items.stem: Operating clockwise between 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ and 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³ and between 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa and 3.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 0.8 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber completes cycle A → B → C → D → A. What is the total thermal energy Q_in absorbed by the monatomic gas during the heating legs D → A and A → B?
items.workedSolution: Heat enters on D → A (isochoric, W = 0): Q_DA = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min = 432.0 J, and on A → B (isobaric): Q_AB = (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 3.240 × 10³ J. Total Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = 3.67 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes heatInputJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 3.67 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Confuses net cycle heat Q_net = W_net with total heat input Q_in absorbed from the hot source.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic ΔU on both heating legs.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Includes only the heat absorbed during isobaric expansion A → B and omits the isochoric heating D → A.

items.stem: In a closed noble-gas power-conversion loop coupled to a thermal reservoir at 400 K, 2.2 mol of an ideal gas expands reversibly and isothermally from V_A = 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the change in entropy ΔS of the gas?
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 2.2 × 8.31 × ln(4.8 × 10⁻³ / 2.0 × 10⁻³) = 16.0 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 16.0 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 logarithm log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of the natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Replaces ln(V_B / V_A) with the linear fractional change (V_B − V_A) / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes isothermal heat Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) without dividing by T to obtain ΔS = Q / T.

items.stem: In a variable-volume optical pressure cell, 0.75 mol of monatomic ideal gas executes a reversible Carnot heat-engine cycle between a hot reservoir at 608 K and a cold sink at 380 K, expanding isothermally at the hot reservoir from V_A = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 7.5 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the theoretical thermal efficiency η of this Carnot cycle?
items.workedSolution: Carnot efficiency η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 1 − 380 / 608 = 0.375.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 0.375 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides ΔT by T_C instead of T_H when computing efficiency.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates T_C / T_H without subtracting from 1.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the isothermal volume ratio 1 − V_A / V_B instead of the reservoir temperature ratio 1 − T_C / T_H.

items.stem: In a semiconductor lithography purge canister (volume 0.025 m³), 0.3 mol of monatomic Xenon-131 (Xe) of molar mass 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹ is warmed from T₁ = 320 K to T₂ = 800 K, shifting the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed curve as plotted. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), determine v_rms at the higher temperature T₂.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 800 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 800 / 0.1313) = 390 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 390 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: The P–V graph shows an isobaric compression of 1.2 mol of ideal monatomic gas inside a precision pneumatic actuator chamber sealed with a movable piston at 2.25 × 10⁵ Pa from V_A = 2.7 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³. Using the sign convention where work done on the gas is positive, determine the compression work done on the gas.
items.workedSolution: During isobaric compression from 2.7 × 10⁻³ m³ to 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at 2.25 × 10⁵ Pa, work done on the gas W_on = −P(V_B − V_A) = 2.25 × 10⁵ × (2.7 × 10⁻³ − 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 270 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 270 J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the magnitude of internal energy change |ΔU| = (3/2) P |ΔV| instead of boundary work P |ΔV|.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies pressure by initial volume V_A instead of the volume change |V_B − V_A|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the total heat rejected |Q| = (5/2) P |ΔV| rather than the mechanical work done on the gas.

items.stem: A thermal bath keeps 1.6 mol of ideal gas in a variable-volume optical pressure cell at 280 K during a reversible expansion from 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 7.5 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is the thermal energy Q supplied to the gas (equal to work done by the gas)?
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 280 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.6 × 8.31 × 280 × ln(7.5 × 10⁻³ / 2.5 × 10⁻³) = 4.09 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 4.09 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as remaining constant at P_A, computing P_A(V_B − V_A) instead of ∫ P dV = nRT ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Adds U = (3/2)nRT to isothermal work, overlooking that ΔU = 0 at constant temperature.

items.stem: The P–V diagram shows an ideal Otto cycle for 1 mol of monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber, compressing adiabatically from V_max = 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (at 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa) to V_min = 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³, heating isochorically to 1.647 × 10⁶ Pa, expanding adiabatically to 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³, and cooling isochorically back to state A. Calculate the cycle efficiency η = W_net / Q_in.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic Otto cycle (γ = 5/3), η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1) = 1 − (2.0 × 10⁻³ / 6.0 × 10⁻³)^(2/3) = 0.519 (equivalently W_net / Q_in = 1.400 × 10³ / 2.696 × 10³ = 0.519).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 0.519 (A).

options.label: D

items.stem: Inside a calibrated heat-transfer bench vessel, 0.72 kg of ethanol (specific heat capacity 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 294 K receives a 0.65 kg brass specimen (c = 380 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 475 K. During mixing, 1600 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. Calculate the equilibrium temperature of the mixture.

items.stem: An experiment records the molecular speed distribution of 0.5 mol of Helium-4 (He) gas (molar mass 4 g mol⁻¹) occupying 0.04 m³ in a high-vacuum synchrotron beamline gas target at 550 K (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²)). Which value equals the rms speed of the atoms?
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 550 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 550 / 4.0 × 10⁻³) = 1.85 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 1.85 × 10³ m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: Spectroscopic thermometry confirms that Neon-20 (Ne) atoms (molar mass 0.0202 kg mol⁻¹) in a thermostatted noble-gas reference bulb are equilibrated at 260 K. Use Boltzmann constant 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and elementary charge 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. Find the average translational kinetic energy of a single atom in eV.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 260 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 0.0336 eV (C).

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the 3/2 factor to 3 k_B T / e by omitting the 1/2 in kinetic energy.

items.stem: A monatomic ideal gas (0.6 mol) in a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity transitions from state A (1.8 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to state B (3.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³) and then to state C (3.6 × 10⁵ Pa, 5.5 × 10⁻³ m³). Defining expansion work done by the gas as positive, calculate the total thermal energy absorbed by the gas over A → B → C.
items.workedSolution: Along A → B → C, work done by the gas is W_by = 0 + P_B(V_C − V_B) = 1.080 × 10³ J. Total internal energy change ΔU = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A) = 2.295 × 10³ J. Hence Q = ΔU + W_by = 3.37 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 3.37 × 10³ J (D).

options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the positive expansion work done by the gas instead of adding Q = ΔU + W_by.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the total internal energy change ΔU_AC and omits the boundary work done during B → C.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the monatomic 3/2 factor in ΔU = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A).

items.stem: The diagram shows a closed four-leg cycle A → B → C → D → A for 1 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals, bounded by P_low = 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa, P_high = 4.5 × 10⁵ Pa, V_min = 1.8 × 10⁻³ m³, and V_max = 3.6 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the thermal efficiency η = W_net / Q_in of this rectangular monatomic-gas cycle?
items.workedSolution: W_net = (4.5 × 10⁵ − 1.8 × 10⁵)(3.6 × 10⁻³ − 1.8 × 10⁻³) = 486.0 J. Heat enters on D → A and A → B: Q_in = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min + (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 2.754 × 10³ J. Efficiency η = W_net / Q_in = 0.176.

markScheme.criterion: Computes thermalEfficiency correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 0.176 (A).

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the Carnot efficiency 1 − T_min / T_max between extreme corner temperatures instead of the actual cycle efficiency W_net / Q_in.

items.stem: Maintained in thermal contact with a 280 K bath, 0.3 mol of ideal gas in a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder expands quasi-statically from 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 5.25 × 10⁻³ m³. Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine ΔS = Q / T for the gas.
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.3 × 8.31 × ln(5.25 × 10⁻³ / 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 3.12 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 3.12 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: D

items.stem: The diagram shows a reversible Carnot cycle A → B → C → D → A for 1.4 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber coupled to a hot reservoir at 572 K and a cold sink at 260 K, with isothermal expansion from 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what magnitude of thermal energy Q_C is rejected to the cold sink per cycle?
items.workedSolution: During isothermal compression C → D at T_C = 260 K, V_C / V_D = V_B / V_A, so heat rejected to the cold sink is Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) = 2.10 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 2.10 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: D

items.stem: In a cryogenic buffer reservoir in a superconducting magnet rig of volume 0.016 m³, 0.65 mol of Helium-4 (He) (molar mass 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹) is held in thermal equilibrium at 117 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what pressure does the gas exert on the walls?
items.workedSolution: Convert temperature to kelvin: T = 117 + 273.15 = 390.15 K. From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (0.65 × 8.31 × 390.15) / 0.016 = 1.32 × 10⁵ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 1.32 × 10⁵ Pa (C).

items.stem: A low-density plasma-free Argon-40 (Ar) sample (M = 0.04 kg mol⁻¹) is held in an ion-propulsion xenon feed manifold at 680 K. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Calculate the internal energy per mole of the gas.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic gas, molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T = 1.5 × 8.31 × 680 = 8.48 × 10³ J mol⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 680 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 8.48 × 10³ J mol⁻¹ (C).

items.stem: Operating clockwise between 2.4 × 10⁻³ m³ and 9.6 × 10⁻³ m³ and between 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa and 2.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 1 mol of monatomic ideal gas in an insulated aerospace gas-accumulator cylinder completes cycle A → B → C → D → A. Taking net work done by the gas as positive, what is the net mechanical work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Net work done by the gas equals the enclosed rectangular area: W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = (2.0 × 10⁵ − 1.0 × 10⁵)(9.6 × 10⁻³ − 2.4 × 10⁻³) = 720 J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes netWorkJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 720 J (A).

items.stem: In a frictionless piston-cylinder assembly on a thermodynamics test bench, 1 mol of monatomic ideal gas executes a reversible Carnot heat-engine cycle between a hot reservoir at 427 °C and a cold sink at 87 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15), expanding isothermally at the hot reservoir from V_A = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 6.25 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the theoretical thermal efficiency η of this Carnot cycle?
items.workedSolution: Convert to kelvin: T_H = 700.15 K, T_C = 360.15 K. Carnot efficiency η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 1 − 360.15 / 700.15 = 0.486.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 0.486 (A).

items.stem: The P–V diagram shows an ideal Otto cycle for 0.8 mol of monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) in a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell, compressing adiabatically from V_max = 3.6 × 10⁻³ m³ (at 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa) to V_min = 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³, heating isochorically to 2.059 × 10⁶ Pa, expanding adiabatically to 3.6 × 10⁻³ m³, and cooling isochorically back to state A. Calculate the cycle efficiency η = W_net / Q_in.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic Otto cycle (γ = 5/3), η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1) = 1 − (1.2 × 10⁻³ / 3.6 × 10⁻³)^(2/3) = 0.519 (equivalently W_net / Q_in = 1.050 × 10³ / 2.022 × 10³ = 0.519).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 0.519 (A).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Raises V_min / V_max to γ = 5/3 rather than γ − 1 = 2/3.

items.stem: A heated copper block of mass 0.28 kg and specific heat capacity 385 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 475 K is plunged into 0.55 kg of water (c = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 298 K inside a double-walled vacuum Dewar mixing vessel. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. How much thermal energy is released by the copper block in reaching equilibrium?
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l), giving T_eq = 305.9 K. Heat released by the solid Q_lost = m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = 1.82 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 1.82 × 10⁴ J (C).

items.stem: In a thermostatted noble-gas reference bulb (volume 0.05 m³), 1.5 mol of monatomic Argon-40 (Ar) of molar mass 40 g mol⁻¹ is warmed from T₁ = 550 K to T₂ = 1238 K, shifting the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed curve as plotted. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), determine v_rms at the higher temperature T₂.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.04 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 1238 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 1238 / 0.04) = 878 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 878 m s⁻¹ (D).

items.stem: The P–V graph shows an isobaric compression of 0.6 mol of ideal monatomic gas inside a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals at 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa from V_A = 7.7 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³. Using the sign convention where work done on the gas is positive, determine the compression work done on the gas.
items.workedSolution: During isobaric compression from 7.7 × 10⁻³ m³ to 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa, work done on the gas W_on = −P(V_B − V_A) = 1.8 × 10⁵ × (7.7 × 10⁻³ − 3.5 × 10⁻³) = 756 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 756 J (A).

options.label: D

items.stem: On the P–V diagram, 0.45 mol of an ideal gas in an insulated aerospace gas-accumulator cylinder undergoes a reversible isothermal expansion at 520 K from 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and expansion work by the gas as positive. Find W_AB.
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 520 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.45 × 8.31 × 520 × ln(3.0 × 10⁻³ / 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.35 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 1.35 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A

options.label: D

items.stem: A closed heat engine (a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder) takes 1 mol of monatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) from A (5.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³) adiabatically to V_B = 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³, compresses it at constant pressure back to V_C = 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³, and heats it isochorically back to A. Find the net work done by the gas per cycle (work by gas positive).
items.workedSolution: At B, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 8.814 × 10⁴ Pa. Adiabatic work W_AB = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 856.8 J, and isobaric compression work W_BC = P_B(V_C − V_B) = -352.5 J (W_CA = 0). Thus W_net = W_AB + W_BC = 504 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 504 J (B).

items.stem: Inside an expanded-polystyrene adiabatic quenching bath, 0.22 kg of ethanol (specific heat capacity 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 285 K receives a 0.85 kg aluminium specimen (c = 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 475 K. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. Calculate the equilibrium temperature of the mixture.

options.distractorRationale: Computes the Carnot efficiency 1 − T_min / T_max between extreme corner temperatures instead of the actual cycle efficiency W_net / Q_in.

items.stem: On the P–V diagram, 1.6 mol of an ideal gas in a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell undergoes a reversible isothermal expansion at 310 K from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 7.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and expansion work by the gas as positive. Find W_AB.
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 310 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.6 × 8.31 × 310 × ln(7.0 × 10⁻³ / 2.0 × 10⁻³) = 5.16 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 5.16 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as remaining constant at P_A, computing P_A(V_B − V_A) instead of ∫ P dV = nRT ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Adds U = (3/2)nRT to isothermal work, overlooking that ΔU = 0 at constant temperature.

items.stem: In a variable-volume optical pressure cell, 0.75 mol of monatomic ideal gas executes a reversible Carnot heat-engine cycle between a hot reservoir at 770 K and a cold sink at 350 K, expanding isothermally at the hot reservoir from V_A = 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 7.0 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the theoretical thermal efficiency η of this Carnot cycle?
items.workedSolution: Carnot efficiency η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 1 − 350 / 770 = 0.545.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 0.545 (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates T_C / T_H without subtracting from 1.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses the isothermal volume ratio 1 − V_A / V_B instead of the reservoir temperature ratio 1 − T_C / T_H.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides ΔT by T_C instead of T_H when computing efficiency.

items.stem: 2.2 mol of monatomic Krypton-84 (Kr) (molar mass 0.0838 kg mol⁻¹) fills a thick-walled titanium deep-sea pressure housing of volume 0.045 m³ at a steady temperature of 340 K. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Find the gas pressure.
items.workedSolution: From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (2.2 × 8.31 × 340) / 0.045 = 1.38 × 10⁵ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 1.38 × 10⁵ Pa (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies nRT by volume V instead of dividing nRT by V.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts 273.15 from an already-kelvin temperature before applying pV = nRT.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the amount of substance n in p = nRT / V, solving for 1 mol instead of the given molar amount.

items.stem: An experiment records the molecular speed distribution of 1.5 mol of Xenon-131 (Xe) gas (molar mass 131.3 g mol⁻¹) occupying 0.05 m³ in a sealed borosilicate acoustic-thermometry sphere at 290 K (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²)). Which value equals the rms speed of the atoms?
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 290 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 290 / 0.1313) = 235 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 235 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: A sample of 0.6 mol of an ideal monatomic gas in a closed noble-gas power-conversion loop expands isobarically at constant pressure 6.0 × 10⁵ Pa from volume 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³ (state A) to 8.1 × 10⁻³ m³ (state B). Taking thermal energy supplied to the gas and work done by the gas as positive, how much thermal energy Q is supplied to the gas during A → B?
items.workedSolution: Work done by the gas W_by = P(V_B − V_A) = 6.0 × 10⁵ × (8.1 × 10⁻³ − 4.5 × 10⁻³) = 2.160 × 10³ J. For a monatomic ideal gas, ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV = 3.240 × 10³ J. By the first law, Q = ΔU + W_by = (5/2) P ΔV = 5.40 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 5.40 × 10³ J (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the boundary work W = P ΔV done by the gas and ignores the increase in internal energy ΔU.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the internal energy change ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV and omits the expansion work P ΔV.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV, computing ΔU + W = P ΔV + P ΔV = 2 P ΔV instead of (5/2) P ΔV.

items.stem: In a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder coupled to a thermal reservoir at 350 K, 0.45 mol of an ideal gas expands reversibly and isothermally from V_A = 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 6.75 × 10⁻³ m³. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is the change in entropy ΔS of the gas?
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.45 × 8.31 × ln(6.75 × 10⁻³ / 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 5.62 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 5.62 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 logarithm log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of the natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Replaces ln(V_B / V_A) with the linear fractional change (V_B − V_A) / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes isothermal heat Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) without dividing by T to obtain ΔS = Q / T.

items.stem: Three reversible stages A → B → C → A form a heat-engine cycle for 1.2 mol of monatomic gas (γ = 5/3) inside a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity: adiabatic expansion from 4.5 × 10⁵ Pa and 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³, constant-pressure compression to 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³, and constant-volume heating to A. What net mechanical work output does one cycle deliver?
items.workedSolution: At B, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 1.417 × 10⁵ Pa. Adiabatic work W_AB = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 499.6 J, and isobaric compression work W_BC = P_B(V_C − V_B) = -283.5 J (W_CA = 0). Thus W_net = W_AB + W_BC = 216 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 216 J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the magnitude of the isobaric compression work P_B(V_B − V_C).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the adiabatic expansion work W_AB and forgets to subtract the isobaric compression work |W_BC|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_CA along the isochoric leg instead of net work W_net.

items.stem: A heated brass block of mass 0.85 kg and specific heat capacity 380 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 380 K is plunged into 0.32 kg of water (c = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 302 K inside a lagged benchtop thermal-equilibrium chamber. During mixing, 1250 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. What is the final thermal equilibrium temperature T_eq?
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l) + 1250, giving T_eq = 316.4 K. Therefore T_eq = 316 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 316 K (B).

items.stem: In an atmospheric research dropsonde reference chamber (volume 0.025 m³), 1.2 mol of monatomic Helium-4 (He) of molar mass 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹ is warmed from T₁ = 480 K to T₂ = 1080 K, shifting the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed curve as plotted. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), determine v_rms at the higher temperature T₂.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 1080 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 1080 / 4.0 × 10⁻³) = 2.59 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 2.59 × 10³ m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: Thermalised Neon-20 (Ne) vapour of molar mass 0.0202 kg mol⁻¹ fills a rigid stainless-steel vacuum-calibration tank at a uniform temperature of 327 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, Determine the molar translational internal energy U_m.
items.workedSolution: T = 327 + 273.15 = 600.15 K. For an ideal monatomic gas, molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T = 1.5 × 8.31 × 600.15 = 7.48 × 10³ J mol⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 600.15 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 7.48 × 10³ J mol⁻¹ (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Includes only one translational degree of freedom (1/2 R T) instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the 3/2 factor in monatomic molar internal energy U_m = (3/2) R T.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses molar enthalpy C_p T = (5/2) R T instead of molar internal energy (3/2) R T.

items.stem: The P–V graph shows an isobaric compression of 1.2 mol of ideal monatomic gas inside a variable-volume optical pressure cell at 5.4 × 10⁵ Pa from V_A = 5.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³. Using the sign convention where work done on the gas is positive, determine the compression work done on the gas.
items.workedSolution: During isobaric compression from 5.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at 5.4 × 10⁵ Pa, work done on the gas W_on = −P(V_B − V_A) = 5.4 × 10⁵ × (5.5 × 10⁻³ − 2.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.62 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 1.62 × 10³ J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the magnitude of internal energy change |ΔU| = (3/2) P |ΔV| instead of boundary work P |ΔV|.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies pressure by initial volume V_A instead of the volume change |V_B − V_A|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the total heat rejected |Q| = (5/2) P |ΔV| rather than the mechanical work done on the gas.

items.stem: A heat-engine test rig (a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell) drives 0.8 mol of ideal monatomic gas around a rectangular cycle with upper pressure 3.75 × 10⁵ Pa, lower pressure 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, minimum volume 2.4 × 10⁻³ m³, and maximum volume 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking net work done by the gas as positive, what is the net mechanical work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Net work done by the gas equals the enclosed rectangular area: W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = (3.75 × 10⁵ − 1.5 × 10⁵)(4.8 × 10⁻³ − 2.4 × 10⁻³) = 540 J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes netWorkJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 540 J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies the enclosed loop area by an extraneous 3/2 internal-energy factor.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the expansion work along A → B and forgets to subtract the compression work along C → D.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes P_B V_B − P_D V_D instead of the enclosed rectangular loop area (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min).

items.stem: A thermal bath keeps 1.6 mol of ideal gas in a precision pneumatic actuator chamber sealed with a movable piston at 600 K during a reversible expansion from 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 0.012 m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is the thermal energy Q supplied to the gas (equal to work done by the gas)?
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 600 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.6 × 8.31 × 600 × ln(0.012 / 5.0 × 10⁻³) = 6.98 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 6.98 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as remaining constant at P_A, computing P_A(V_B − V_A) instead of ∫ P dV = nRT ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Adds U = (3/2)nRT to isothermal work, overlooking that ΔU = 0 at constant temperature.

items.stem: A Carnot engine modelled in a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell uses 0.5 mol of ideal gas operating between a hot reservoir at 464 K and a cold sink at 290 K. During the high-temperature isothermal stage A → B, the volume increases from 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ to 2.4 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking net work done by the gas as positive (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹), what is the net work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.336 × 10³ J and η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 0.3750. Net work output W_net = η Q_H = nR(T_H − T_C) ln(V_B / V_A) = 501 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 501 J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the rejected heat Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) instead of net work Q_H − Q_C.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_H = nRT_H ln(V_B / V_A) without multiplying by Carnot efficiency (1 − T_C / T_H).

items.stem: Inside an ion-propulsion xenon feed manifold of internal volume 8.0 × 10⁻³ m³, 0.15 mol of ideal Helium-4 (He) gas (molar mass 4 g mol⁻¹) is maintained at 340 K. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what is the mass density of the gas?

markScheme.criterion: Applies ρ = nM / V in SI units to obtain 0.0750 kg m⁻³ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies total gas mass nM by container volume V instead of dividing by V.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes molar concentration n / V (mol m⁻³) and omits multiplication by molar mass M.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Leaves molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of converting to kg mol⁻¹, overestimating density by a factor of 1000.

items.stem: Spectroscopic thermometry confirms that Argon-40 (Ar) atoms (molar mass 0.04 kg mol⁻¹) in a sealed quartz spectroscopy cell are equilibrated at 260 K. Given k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and 1 eV = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, Find the average translational kinetic energy of a single atom in eV.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 260 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 0.0336 eV (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates (1/2) k_B T / e for a single degree of freedom instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes k_B T / e and omits the 3/2 translational factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the 3/2 factor to 3 k_B T / e by omitting the 1/2 in kinetic energy.

items.stem: In a frictionless piston-cylinder assembly on a thermodynamics test bench, 0.8 mol of a monatomic ideal gas executes a clockwise closed cycle A → B → C → D → A between pressures 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa and 4.2 × 10⁵ Pa and volumes 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ and 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (A → B isobaric expansion at 4.2 × 10⁵ Pa, B → C isochoric cooling, C → D isobaric compression at 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa, D → A isochoric heating). What is the thermal efficiency η = W_net / Q_in of this rectangular monatomic-gas cycle?
items.workedSolution: W_net = (4.2 × 10⁵ − 1.2 × 10⁵)(3.0 × 10⁻³ − 1.2 × 10⁻³) = 540.0 J. Heat enters on D → A and A → B: Q_in = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min + (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 2.430 × 10³ J. Efficiency η = W_net / Q_in = 0.222.

markScheme.criterion: Computes thermalEfficiency correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 0.222 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides W_net by Q_AB alone, neglecting the heat input Q_DA on the isochoric leg D → A.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits internal energy gain ΔU_AB when computing total heat input Q_in.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the Carnot efficiency 1 − T_min / T_max between extreme corner temperatures instead of the actual cycle efficiency W_net / Q_in.

items.stem: The diagram shows a reversible Carnot cycle A → B → C → D → A for 0.3 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a cryocooler compression cylinder containing monatomic working gas coupled to a hot reservoir at 648 K and a cold sink at 350 K, with isothermal expansion from 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 4.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what magnitude of thermal energy Q_C is rejected to the cold sink per cycle?
items.workedSolution: During isothermal compression C → D at T_C = 350 K, V_C / V_D = V_B / V_A, so heat rejected to the cold sink is Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) = 605 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 605 J (C).

options.label: A

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the heat absorbed Q_H from the hot reservoir instead of the heat Q_C rejected to the cold sink.

items.stem: A closed heat engine (a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals) takes 1 mol of monatomic ideal gas (γ = 5/3) from A (5.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³) adiabatically to V_B = 8.0 × 10⁻³ m³, compresses it at constant pressure back to V_C = 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³, and heats it isochorically back to A. Find the net work done by the gas per cycle (work by gas positive).
items.workedSolution: At B, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 5.457 × 10⁴ Pa. Adiabatic work W_AB = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 995.2 J, and isobaric compression work W_BC = P_B(V_C − V_B) = -327.4 J (W_CA = 0). Thus W_net = W_AB + W_BC = 668 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 668 J (B).

options.label: C

options.label: D

items.stem: In a calorimetry run using a low-heat-capacity polymeric calorimetry beaker, a 0.48 kg cylinder of copper (c = 385 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 475 K is quenched in 0.72 kg of mineral oil (c = 1960 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 298 K. During mixing, 1600 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. Find T_eq at thermal equilibrium.
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l) + 1600, giving T_eq = 317.5 K. Therefore T_eq = 317 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 317 K (B).

items.stem: In a rigid stainless-steel vacuum-calibration tank of volume 0.06 m³, 0.35 mol of Helium-4 (He) (molar mass 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹) is held in thermal equilibrium at 460 K. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what pressure does the gas exert on the walls?
items.workedSolution: From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (0.35 × 8.31 × 460) / 0.06 = 2.23 × 10⁴ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 2.23 × 10⁴ Pa (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies nRT by volume V instead of dividing nRT by V.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts 273.15 from an already-kelvin temperature before applying pV = nRT.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the amount of substance n in p = nRT / V, solving for 1 mol instead of the given molar amount.

items.stem: Thermalised Argon-40 (Ar) vapour of molar mass 0.04 kg mol⁻¹ fills a high-vacuum synchrotron beamline gas target at a uniform temperature of 310 K. Use Boltzmann constant 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and elementary charge 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the mean translational kinetic energy per atom in electronvolts?

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 310 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 0.0401 eV (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates (1/2) k_B T / e for a single degree of freedom instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes k_B T / e and omits the 3/2 translational factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the 3/2 factor to 3 k_B T / e by omitting the 1/2 in kinetic energy.

items.stem: In a micro-electro-mechanical gas spring cavity, 0.5 mol of a monatomic ideal gas executes a clockwise closed cycle A → B → C → D → A between pressures 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa and 5.25 × 10⁵ Pa and volumes 2.4 × 10⁻³ m³ and 7.2 × 10⁻³ m³ (A → B isobaric expansion at 5.25 × 10⁵ Pa, B → C isochoric cooling, C → D isobaric compression at 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa, D → A isochoric heating). Taking net work done by the gas as positive, what is the net mechanical work output W_net per cycle?
items.workedSolution: Net work done by the gas equals the enclosed rectangular area: W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = (5.25 × 10⁵ − 1.5 × 10⁵)(7.2 × 10⁻³ − 2.4 × 10⁻³) = 1.80 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Computes netWorkJ correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 1.80 × 10³ J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the expansion work along A → B and forgets to subtract the compression work along C → D.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies the enclosed loop area by an extraneous 3/2 internal-energy factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes P_B V_B − P_D V_D instead of the enclosed rectangular loop area (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min).

items.stem: In a variable-volume optical pressure cell, 0.75 mol of monatomic ideal gas executes a reversible Carnot heat-engine cycle between a hot reservoir at 512 K and a cold sink at 320 K, expanding isothermally at the hot reservoir from V_A = 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 3.6 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the theoretical thermal efficiency η of this Carnot cycle?
items.workedSolution: Carnot efficiency η = 1 − T_C / T_H = 1 − 320 / 512 = 0.375.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 0.375 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides ΔT by T_C instead of T_H when computing efficiency.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates T_C / T_H without subtracting from 1.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Uses the isothermal volume ratio 1 − V_A / V_B instead of the reservoir temperature ratio 1 − T_C / T_H.

items.stem: On the P–V plot for a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder, 0.25 mol of monatomic working gas (γ = 5/3) expands adiabatically from (8.0 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³) at A to 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³ at B, returns to 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ isobarically at C, and regains 8.0 × 10⁵ Pa isochorically. Defining work by the gas as positive, calculate W_net.
items.workedSolution: At B, P_B = P_A (V_A / V_B)^(5/3) = 1.282 × 10⁵ Pa. Adiabatic work W_AB = (3/2)(P_A V_A − P_B V_B) = 1.246 × 10³ J, and isobaric compression work W_BC = P_B(V_C − V_B) = -512.8 J (W_CA = 0). Thus W_net = W_AB + W_BC = 733 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 733 J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the magnitude of the isobaric compression work P_B(V_B − V_C).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes only the adiabatic expansion work W_AB and forgets to subtract the isobaric compression work |W_BC|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates total heat input Q_CA along the isochoric leg instead of net work W_net.

items.stem: A heated copper block of mass 0.48 kg and specific heat capacity 385 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 410 K is plunged into 0.72 kg of water (c = 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 298 K inside a well-insulated copper-lined laboratory calorimeter. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. What is the final thermal equilibrium temperature T_eq?
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l), giving T_eq = 304.5 K. Therefore T_eq = 304 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 304 K (B).

items.stem: In a semiconductor lithography purge canister (volume 0.08 m³), 0.5 mol of monatomic Argon-40 (Ar) of molar mass 0.04 kg mol⁻¹ is warmed from T₁ = 360 K to T₂ = 900 K, shifting the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed curve as plotted. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), determine v_rms at the higher temperature T₂.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.04 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 900 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 900 / 0.04) = 749 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 749 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of kg mol⁻¹ into √(3RT / M), underestimating v_rms by a factor of √1000 ≈ 31.6.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 3 from the three translational degrees of freedom, evaluating √(RT / M).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Uses a factor of 2 instead of 3, computing the most probable speed v_p = √(2RT / M) rather than v_rms.

items.stem: The P–V graph shows an isobaric compression of 0.6 mol of ideal monatomic gas inside a precision pneumatic actuator chamber sealed with a movable piston at 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa from V_A = 3.3 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³. Using the sign convention where work done on the gas is positive, determine the compression work done on the gas.
items.workedSolution: During isobaric compression from 3.3 × 10⁻³ m³ to 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ at 3.0 × 10⁵ Pa, work done on the gas W_on = −P(V_B − V_A) = 3.0 × 10⁵ × (3.3 × 10⁻³ − 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 540 J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 540 J (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the magnitude of internal energy change |ΔU| = (3/2) P |ΔV| instead of boundary work P |ΔV|.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies pressure by initial volume V_A instead of the volume change |V_B − V_A|.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the total heat rejected |Q| = (5/2) P |ΔV| rather than the mechanical work done on the gas.

items.stem: A thermal bath keeps 2.2 mol of ideal gas in a variable-volume optical pressure cell at 450 K during a reversible expansion from 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is the thermal energy Q supplied to the gas (equal to work done by the gas)?
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 450 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 2.2 × 8.31 × 450 × ln(4.5 × 10⁻³ / 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 9.04 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates W = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 9.04 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Treats pressure as remaining constant at P_A, computing P_A(V_B − V_A) instead of ∫ P dV = nRT ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Adds U = (3/2)nRT to isothermal work, overlooking that ΔU = 0 at constant temperature.

items.stem: A closed reciprocating loop (a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber) carries 0.8 mol of monatomic ideal gas (adiabatic index 5/3) around Otto cycle A → B → C → D → A between volume limits 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³ and 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³, with initial pressure P_A = 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa and peak pressure P_C = 1.048 × 10⁶ Pa. Determine its thermal efficiency.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic Otto cycle (γ = 5/3), η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1) = 1 − (2.5 × 10⁻³ / 5.0 × 10⁻³)^(2/3) = 0.370 (equivalently W_net / Q_in = 793.0 / 2.143 × 10³ = 0.370).

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the closed adiabatic heat-engine cycle to obtain 0.370 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Uses exponent 1 instead of γ − 1 = 2/3 in the Otto efficiency relation η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Raises V_min / V_max to γ = 5/3 rather than γ − 1 = 2/3.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes Carnot efficiency 1 − T_A / T_C between extreme cycle temperatures instead of Otto efficiency.

items.stem: Inside a double-walled vacuum Dewar mixing vessel, 0.32 kg of ethanol (specific heat capacity 2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 294 K receives a 0.65 kg aluminium specimen (c = 900 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) initially at 510 K. Thermal energy exchange with the surroundings and container is negligible. Calculate the equilibrium temperature of the mixture.
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l), giving T_eq = 386.5 K. Therefore T_eq = 387 K.

markScheme.criterion: Applies calorimetry energy balance to obtain 387 K (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Takes the unweighted arithmetic mean of the two initial temperatures, ignoring both masses and specific heat capacities.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Weights initial temperatures by mass alone and ignores the much larger specific heat capacity of the liquid.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Swaps the specific heat capacities of the solid specimen and the liquid bath.

items.stem: A sample of 1.2 mol of monatomic Argon-40 (Ar) (M = 40 g mol⁻¹) occupies an orbital satellite attitude-control propellant cylinder of fixed volume 0.016 m³ at 520 K. Given R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, calculate the bulk density ρ of the gas.
items.workedSolution: Total gas mass m = nM = 1.2 × 0.04 = 0.04800 kg. Density ρ = m / V = 0.04800 / 0.016 = 3.00 kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Applies ρ = nM / V in SI units to obtain 3.00 kg m⁻³ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies total gas mass nM by container volume V instead of dividing by V.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes molar concentration n / V (mol m⁻³) and omits multiplication by molar mass M.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Leaves molar mass in g mol⁻¹ instead of converting to kg mol⁻¹, overestimating density by a factor of 1000.

items.stem: A low-density plasma-free Xenon-131 (Xe) sample (M = 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹) is held in a thermostatted noble-gas reference bulb at 820 K. Take k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the mean translational kinetic energy per atom in electronvolts?

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes T = 820 K into the monatomic kinetic-theory energy relation to obtain 0.106 eV (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Evaluates (1/2) k_B T / e for a single degree of freedom instead of three.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Computes k_B T / e and omits the 3/2 translational factor.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Doubles the 3/2 factor to 3 k_B T / e by omitting the 1/2 in kinetic energy.

items.stem: The diagram shows a closed four-leg cycle A → B → C → D → A for 0.2 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a laboratory heat-engine indicator rig with low-friction seals, bounded by P_low = 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa, P_high = 5.4 × 10⁵ Pa, V_min = 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³, and V_max = 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³. What is the thermal efficiency η = W_net / Q_in of this rectangular monatomic-gas cycle?
items.workedSolution: W_net = (5.4 × 10⁵ − 1.8 × 10⁵)(4.8 × 10⁻³ − 1.2 × 10⁻³) = 1.296 × 10³ J. Heat enters on D → A and A → B: Q_in = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min + (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 5.508 × 10³ J. Efficiency η = W_net / Q_in = 0.235.

markScheme.criterion: Computes thermalEfficiency correctly for the closed rectangular cycle to obtain 0.235 (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Divides W_net by Q_AB alone, neglecting the heat input Q_DA on the isochoric leg D → A.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits internal energy gain ΔU_AB when computing total heat input Q_in.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the Carnot efficiency 1 − T_min / T_max between extreme corner temperatures instead of the actual cycle efficiency W_net / Q_in.

items.stem: Maintained in thermal contact with a 350 K bath, 1.2 mol of ideal gas in a high-efficiency reciprocating research engine cylinder expands quasi-statically from 5.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 0.012 m³. Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, determine ΔS = Q / T for the gas.
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.2 × 8.31 × ln(0.012 / 5.0 × 10⁻³) = 8.73 J K⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ΔS = nR ln(V_B / V_A) to obtain 8.73 J K⁻¹ (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses base-10 logarithm log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of the natural logarithm ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Replaces ln(V_B / V_A) with the linear fractional change (V_B − V_A) / V_A.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes isothermal heat Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) without dividing by T to obtain ΔS = Q / T.

items.stem: The diagram shows a reversible Carnot cycle A → B → C → D → A for 1 mol of monatomic ideal gas in a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber coupled to a hot reservoir at 638 K and a cold sink at 290 K, with isothermal expansion from 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ to 3.6 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, what magnitude of thermal energy Q_C is rejected to the cold sink per cycle?
items.workedSolution: During isothermal compression C → D at T_C = 290 K, V_C / V_D = V_B / V_A, so heat rejected to the cold sink is Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A) = 2.65 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Carnot thermodynamics in kelvin to obtain 2.65 × 10³ J (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Uses log₁₀(V_B / V_A) instead of ln(V_B / V_A) in Q_C = nRT_C ln(V_B / V_A).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes net work W_net = Q_H − Q_C instead of the rejected heat Q_C.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Computes the heat absorbed Q_H from the hot reservoir instead of the heat Q_C rejected to the cold sink.

items.stem: 0.45 mol of monatomic Krypton-84 (Kr) (molar mass 0.0838 kg mol⁻¹) fills a cryogenic buffer reservoir in a superconducting magnet rig of volume 0.016 m³ at a steady temperature of 227 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15). Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Find the gas pressure.
items.workedSolution: Convert temperature to kelvin: T = 227 + 273.15 = 500.15 K. From the ideal gas equation p = nRT / V = (0.45 × 8.31 × 500.15) / 0.016 = 1.17 × 10⁵ Pa.

markScheme.criterion: Applies p = nRT / V in SI units to obtain 1.17 × 10⁵ Pa (C).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Multiplies nRT by volume V instead of dividing nRT by V.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Substitutes Celsius temperature θ directly into pV = nRT without converting to absolute temperature in kelvin.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the amount of substance n in p = nRT / V, solving for 1 mol instead of the given molar amount.

items.stem: At 250 K, 2 mol of Xenon-131 (Xe) with molar mass 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹ fills a thick-walled titanium deep-sea pressure housing (capacity 0.015 m³). Using R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (kinetic-theory pressure relation: pV = ⅓ N m v_rms²), calculate the root-mean-square speed marked v_rms on the distribution.
items.workedSolution: Convert molar mass to SI units: M = 0.1313 kg mol⁻¹. Using v_rms = √(3RT / M) at T = 250 K gives v_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 250 / 0.1313) = 218 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates √(3RT / M) with M in kg mol⁻¹ to obtain 218 m s⁻¹ (D).

options.label: A

items.stem: A sample of 0.8 mol of an ideal monatomic gas in a cryocooler compression cylinder containing monatomic working gas expands isobarically at constant pressure 1.8 × 10⁵ Pa from volume 3.5 × 10⁻³ m³ (state A) to 0.0112 m³ (state B). Taking thermal energy supplied to the gas and work done by the gas as positive, how much thermal energy Q is supplied to the gas during A → B?
items.workedSolution: Work done by the gas W_by = P(V_B − V_A) = 1.8 × 10⁵ × (0.0112 − 3.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.386 × 10³ J. For a monatomic ideal gas, ΔU = (3/2) P ΔV = 2.079 × 10³ J. By the first law, Q = ΔU + W_by = (5/2) P ΔV = 3.47 × 10³ J.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates the first-law energy transfer with consistent work sign to obtain 3.47 × 10³ J (D).

items.stem: Inside a magnetically coupled piston calorimeter chamber, 1.2 mol of ideal gas is held at a constant temperature of 520 K while expanding reversibly from V_A = 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to V_B = 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking work done by the gas as positive and R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, how much work is done by the gas?
items.workedSolution: At constant temperature T = 520 K, ΔU = 0 and W_by = Q = nRT ln(V_B / V_A) = 1.2 × 8.31 × 520 × ln(6.0 × 10⁻³ / 2.0 × 10⁻³) = 5.70 × 10³ J.

items.stem: A closed reciprocating loop (a closed-cycle Stirling regenerator test cell) carries 0.25 mol of monatomic ideal gas (adiabatic index 5/3) around Otto cycle A → B → C → D → A between volume limits 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ and 4.8 × 10⁻³ m³, with initial pressure P_A = 1.2 × 10⁵ Pa and peak pressure P_C = 2.661 × 10⁶ Pa. Determine its thermal efficiency.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal monatomic Otto cycle (γ = 5/3), η = 1 − (V_min / V_max)^(γ − 1) = 1 − (1.2 × 10⁻³ / 4.8 × 10⁻³)^(2/3) = 0.603 (equivalently W_net / Q_in = 1.576 × 10³ / 2.613 × 10³ = 0.603).

During mixing, 650 J of thermal energy escapes to the surroundings. How much thermal energy is released by the brass block in reaching equilibrium?
items.workedSolution: Enthalpy balance: m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = m_l c_l (T_eq − T_l) + 650, giving T_eq = 314.5 K. Heat released by the solid Q_lost = m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = 1.74 × 10⁴ J.

items.stem: In a closed noble-gas power-conversion loop, 1 mol of a monatomic ideal gas executes a clockwise closed cycle A → B → C → D → A between pressures 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa and 2.0 × 10⁵ Pa and volumes 2.4 × 10⁻³ m³ and 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³ (A → B isobaric expansion at 2.0 × 10⁵ Pa, B → C isochoric cooling, C → D isobaric compression at 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa, D → A isochoric heating). What is the total thermal energy Q_in absorbed by the monatomic gas during the heating legs D → A and A → B?
items.workedSolution: Heat enters on D → A (isochoric, W = 0): Q_DA = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min = 360.0 J, and on A → B (isobaric): Q_AB = (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 1.800 × 10³ J. Total Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = 2.16 × 10³ J.

items.stem: The P–V curve shows a reversible isothermal expansion at 280 K of 0.6 mol of ideal gas inside a frictionless piston-cylinder assembly on a thermodynamics test bench from volume 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³ (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹). Calculate the entropy increase ΔS of the gas.
items.workedSolution: For a reversible isothermal expansion, ΔU = 0 so Q = W_by = nRT ln(V_B / V_A). Therefore ΔS = Q / T = nR ln(V_B / V_A) = 0.6 × 8.31 × ln(4.5 × 10⁻³ / 1.5 × 10⁻³) = 5.48 J K⁻¹.

items.workedSolution: (a) Adiabatic relation gives P_B = 4.76 × 10⁵ Pa. (b) Isochoric heat input Q_in = 1.03 × 10³ J. (c) By cyclic energy conservation ΔU_cycle = 0, W_net = Q_in − Q_out = 381 J.

items.stem: Inside a frictionless piston-cylinder assembly on a thermodynamics test bench, 1.2 mol of monatomic ideal gas undergoes two sequential processes plotted on the P–V graph: isochoric heating from A (1.2 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³) to B (1.8 × 10⁵ Pa, 2.5 × 10⁻³ m³), followed by isobaric expansion to C (1.8 × 10⁵ Pa, 4.5 × 10⁻³ m³). workingSteps: For a monatomic ideal gas, U = (3/2) PV, so ΔU_AC = (3/2)(P_C V_C − P_A V_A).

parts.prompt: Determine the total thermal energy Q supplied to the gas over the complete path A → B → C.
workingSteps: By the first law of thermodynamics, Q = ΔU_AC + W_by = 765.0 + 360.0 = 1.12 × 10³ J.

items.stem: At 680 K, an ion-propulsion xenon feed manifold contains monatomic Helium-4 (He) of molar mass 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg mol⁻¹. Adopt k_B = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹, elementary charge 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) E_k,avg = (3/2) k_B T = 0 J. (b) Dividing by 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C gives 0.0880 eV. (c) v_rms = √(3RT / M) = 2.06 × 10³ m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Applies E_k = (3/2) k_B T in kelvin.
Divides energy in joules by elementary charge e.

parts.prompt: Calculate the mean translational kinetic energy of a single atom in joules.
Convert this mean translational kinetic energy into electronvolts.
Determine the root-mean-square speed of the Helium-4 (He) atoms.

items.stem: In an insulated aerospace gas-accumulator cylinder, 0.4 mol of an ideal monatomic gas undergoes the clockwise closed heat-engine cycle A → B → C → D → A: isobaric expansion A → B at 3.5 × 10⁵ Pa from 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³ to 6.0 × 10⁻³ m³, isochoric cooling B → C to 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa, isobaric compression C → D at 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa back to 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³, and isochoric heating D → A to 3.5 × 10⁵ Pa. Take work done by the gas as positive.
items.workedSolution: (a) W_net = (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min) = 750 J. (b) Q_in = Q_DA + Q_AB = (3/2)(P_high − P_low)V_min + (5/2)P_high(V_max − V_min) = 3.75 × 10³ J. (c) η = W_net / Q_in = 0.200.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates enclosed loop area (P_high − P_low)(V_max − V_min).
Identifies heat input on both D → A (isochoric) and A → B (isobaric).
Uses monatomic factors (3/2) on D → A and (5/2) on A → B.
Divides W_net from (a) by Q_in from (b).

parts.prompt: Calculate the net mechanical work W_net done by the gas in one complete cycle.
Calculate the total thermal energy Q_in supplied to the monatomic gas during the heating stages D → A and A → B.
Determine the thermal efficiency η of this cycle.

items.stem: Within a frictionless piston-cylinder assembly on a thermodynamics test bench, 0.5 mol of monatomic working gas completes a four-stage Carnot engine loop between a hot reservoir at 427 °C and a cold sink at 117 °C (take T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15), expanding from 1.5 × 10⁻³ m³ to 3.75 × 10⁻³ m³ while in contact with the hot source (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹; net work output by the gas positive).

markScheme.criterion: Converts temperatures to kelvin and applies 1 − T_C / T_H.
Multiplies η by Q_H (or evaluates Q_H − Q_C).

parts.prompt: Calculate the thermal efficiency η of the Carnot cycle.
Calculate the thermal energy Q_H absorbed from the hot reservoir during the isothermal expansion A → B.
Determine the net mechanical work W_net done by the gas per cycle.

items.stem: A sample of 0.35 mol of monatomic Xenon-131 (Xe) gas (molar mass 131.3 g mol⁻¹) is sealed inside a semiconductor lithography purge canister of constant volume 0.045 m³ at 520 K. Take R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.
items.workedSolution: (a) p = nRT / V = (0.35 × 8.31 × 520) / 0.045 = 3.36 × 10⁴ Pa. (b) Single-atom mass m = M / N_A = 0 kg. (c) Density ρ = nM / V = 1.02 kg m⁻³.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes Kelvin temperature into p = nRT / V.
Converts molar mass to kg mol⁻¹ and divides by Avogadro constant.
Evaluates ρ = nM / V in SI units.

parts.prompt: Calculate the pressure exerted by the gas on the walls of the vessel.
Determine the mass of a single Xenon-131 (Xe) atom in kilograms.
Calculate the macroscopic density of the gas inside the vessel.

items.stem: On the P–V diagram for a solar-thermal helium Brayton demonstrator cylinder, 0.8 mol of ideal monatomic gas (adiabatic index 5/3) undergoes adiabatic expansion A → B from (6.5 × 10⁵ Pa, 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³) to 3.0 × 10⁻³ m³, followed by isobaric compression B → C to 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³ and isochoric regeneration C → A. Adopt positive work for expansion by the gas.
items.workedSolution: (a) Adiabatic relation gives P_B = 1.41 × 10⁵ Pa. (b) Isochoric heat input Q_in = 916 J. (c) By cyclic energy conservation ΔU_cycle = 0, W_net = Q_in − Q_out = 281 J.

markScheme.criterion: Applies P V^(5/3) = const along A → B.
Uses Q_in = (3/2) ΔP V on the isochoric heating leg.
Evaluates W_net = Q_in − Q_out (or sums leg works).

parts.prompt: Calculate the pressure P_B of the gas at state B.
Calculate the thermal energy Q_in absorbed by the gas during the isochoric heating leg.
workingSteps: On C → A (constant V = 1.2 × 10⁻³ m³, P_C = P_B), Q_in = ΔU_CA = (3/2)(P_A − P_B) V_A = 916 J.

parts.prompt: Determine the net mechanical work W_net done by the gas per cycle.
workingSteps: Heat rejected on isobaric leg B → C is Q_out = (5/2) P_B (V_B − V_C) = 635.2 J; W_net = Q_in − Q_out = 281 J.

items.stem: A 0.16 kg copper cup (specific heat 385 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) inside a lagged benchtop thermal-equilibrium chamber contains 0.22 kg of ethanol (2440 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) equilibrated at 290 K. Engineers transfer a 0.36 kg glass sample (840 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at 475 K into the liquid with zero external heat loss.
items.workedSolution: (a) Solving the enthalpy balance yields T_eq = 352 K. (b) Heat released by the hot solid Q_lost = m_s c_s (T_s − T_eq) = 3.72 × 10⁴ J. (c) Heat gained by the ethanol Q_liq = m_l c_liq (T_eq − T_l) = 3.33 × 10⁴ J.

markScheme.criterion: Sets up full calorimetry heat-balance equation.
